# Engine coverage

The goal is a full MTG rules engine. This file is the honest state of it: what
the model actually implements, and what it does not. Scenario tests are written
against this list, so keep it current - a mechanic moves from "not modelled" to
"modelled" only when a scenario test covers it.

Read this before writing a scenario. If the mechanic is in the second table, the
test you write should be `xfail` with a reason, not a test bent until it passes.

A striation ("N+ \| ...", plus every following line up to the next symbol - `abilities.station_striations`) is a static ability: `layers._station_symbol_effects` grants its lines in layer 6 at N charge counters, and for the striation holding the printed P/T box (`abilities.station_creature_threshold`, read off the "It's an artifact creature at N+" reminder) adds the creature type (layer 4) and base P/T (7b). `parse_abilities` tags each striation ability `station_threshold`, and the printed-ability lists (`activated_abilities_of`, `triggered_abilities_of`, `parse_mana_abilities`) leave it out - it arrives through `added_ability_lines` only while granted; `CardState.class_ability_text` drops an unreached striation the way it drops an unreached Class level. | A copy of a spell or of a card, outside the zones each is allowed in, ceases to exist (state-based action) | CR 704.5e (both sentences), 707.10a, 707.10f, 111.13, 112.1a, 112.1b | `Game._copies_that_cease_to_exist`, called from `_check_state_based_actions_impl` alongside `tokens_that_cease_to_exist` (CR 704.5d) - every `CardState.is_copy` object outside `{Zone.STACK, Zone.BATTLEFIELD}`, in `shared_zones` and every player's own zones, removed from wherever it sits. One flag and one sweep cover both sentences: the same copy is "a copy of a card" (CR 112.1b) before it is ever cast and "a copy of a spell" (CR 112.1a) once it is, and the exempt-zone set is simply the union the two sentences allow (stack only for a spell-copy; stack and battlefield for a card-copy). Never a copy of a *permanent* spell that already resolved: CR 707.10f/111.13 ("as that copy resolves, it ceases being a copy of a spell and becomes a token permanent") is why `Game._resolve_top_impl` now clears `is_copy` in the same branch that sets `token = True` - without that, a copied permanent would have been swept the round after it landed (the second sentence's own battlefield exemption covers the identical case too, belt and braces - nothing in the pool currently reaches the battlefield still carrying `is_copy`, but the exemption is read from the rule's own words rather than relied on staying moot). CR 722.3c's own exile copy is this rule's one written exception ("This is an exception to rule 704.5e"): a copy in `Zone.EXILE` named by some battlefield permanent's `prepared_copy_id` is spared, the same link `Game.become_prepared`/`become_unprepared` already maintain - once cast, or once the permanent loses the designation or leaves the battlefield, nothing exempts it and the next check removes it. | `scenarios/test_copies_cease_to_exist.py` (Enroot's CR 722.3c prepare-spell copy and Alania, Divergent Storm's copy of Lightning Bolt for the first sentence; Isochron Scepter's own copy of its imprinted card, abandoned mid-resolution with `DecisionPending` so the ability's own hand-written decline-cleanup never runs, for the second) |

Every `origin_zone`/`mana_spent`/`cast_record(` read across `models/game/` and `machines/effects/` was audited in the session this was built: every "cast from a zone" reader is a positive check that already reads correctly for a copy (`Zone.STACK` matches no zone clause it could be mistaken for), and every `mana_spent`/`spend_effects` reader already reads empty for a copy since neither field is ever populated for one. Who controls a copy is CR 707.10's own base paragraph, not 707.10b (which is about an ability copy's *source*, not its controller): "A copy of a spell is owned by the player under whose control it was put on the stack... controlled by the player under whose control it was put on the stack" - exactly `Game.copy_spell`'s existing default, now citable. | `scenarios/test_copy_carries_choices.py` |

| Card data | - | `models/card.py` | `test_card.py` |
| Known information (reveal/look knowledge and expiry) | CR 103.5, 105.2b, 108.3b, 121.1, 201.5, 205.3k, 400.2, 400.7, 400.11a, 401.2, 402.3, 406.3, 608.2n, 701.20a, 701.20b, 701.20c, 701.20d, 701.20e, 701.22a, 701.23a, 701.23e, 701.24a, 701.25a, 701.48a, 702.75a, 702.85a | `Reveal` (`models/game/_zones.py`) records every reveal (CR 701.20a, `Game.reveal`, `viewers=None`) and every look (CR 701.20e, `Game.look`, `viewers=[viewer]`) as frozen data: `zone_change_stamp`, `turn`, and `library_epoch` for a library card. `Game.known_to(viewer)` is pure and returns frozen `KnownCard`s (ids only; `index_from_top` computed live for a library card). A record is live only if the viewer saw it, the card is still in the recorded zone with the recorded stamp (CR 400.7), and for a library record the owner's `Player.library_epoch` still equals the recorded one (CR 701.20d, CR 701.24a); a record of any other shape fails closed. **Epoch-incrementing paths** (CR 401.2 keeps the library one ordered pile): `Game.shuffle_library` (the `keep=` form too), `Player.shuffle` (the pregame and mulligan shuffle, CR 103.5), `Player.add` into `Zone.LIBRARY` (so `Player.move`, `Game.put_cards_into_library` top or bottom, CR 103.5 mulligan bottoming in `Player.keep_hand`, cascade/Possibility Storm/hideaway/random-order bottoms, Green Sun's Zenith's shuffle-in, and every effect putting a card on the bottom), `Game.scry` and `Game.surveil` put-backs, and `Player.note_library_changed` at each direct list write: the Devourer of Destiny keep-on-top (`machines/delayed.py`), the explore put-back and the look-top-N rest-to-bottom (`machines/effects/library.py`), Subtlety's top-or-bottom (`_put_spell_in_library`), and a cost rewind returning a card to a library (`machines/cost/` `_return`). Drawing or taking a card off a library does not move the epoch. **A put that leaves the other cards in their order keeps their records** (CR 401.2, CR 701.20d's "any revealed cards that are reordered"): `Player.note_library_changed(placed=...)` moves the epoch and `Game.keep_untouched_library_records` appends a `LibraryOrderKept` row (card, stamp, new epoch) to `Game.library_orders_kept` for every card not in `placed` that has a live library record; `known_to` and the carry read a record made at an earlier epoch as live when every epoch since has a row for that card and stamp, and `Reveal.library_epoch` is never rewritten. Schema bumped 9 -> 10 for the new field, then 10 -> 11 on merging impending's `CardState.cast_with_keyword`, which had bumped 9 -> 10 independently. That is every put onto the bottom (`Player.add` into a library, so `put_cards_into_library(to_bottom=True)`, CR 103.5 mulligan bottoming, cascade/hideaway/random-order bottoms, Subtlety's bottom, the look-top-N rest-to-bottom) and the scry and surveil put-backs, whose own cards are the placed ones; a record of a placed card still ends. A shuffle, a put on top (`put_cards_into_library` top, Subtlety's top, the explore and Devourer keep-on-top put-backs) and a cost rewind still end every library record, as before. **Known-draw policy (owner decision, not a CR rule):** when a card with a live library record moves straight from its owner's library to that owner's hand (a CR 121.1 draw, Goblin Guide's or explore's land, any effect), `Player.add` calls `Game.carry_knowledge_into_hand`, which appends a `KnownCarry` with the card's new stamp and the record's viewers to `Game.known_carries`; `known_to` returns it with `zone=HAND`, `carried=True` until the card's next zone change (discard, cast, CR 103.5 mulligan). A record already ended by an epoch change is not carried. **The same carry from outside the game:** a card revealed from a sideboard (CR 400.11a, CR 701.20a) and then put into its owner's hand (CR 108.3b) is carried the same way (`Player.add` passes the origin zone; a non-library record needs no epoch), so Karn, the Great Creator's -2 find is known to every player in hand until it changes zones. This did not work before: the sideboard record expired the instant the card moved (CR 400.7), although this row claimed Karn's reveal was populated. The Burning Wish family ("You may reveal a `<quality>` card you own from outside the game and put it into your hand. Exile `<this>`.", `_parse_reveal_from_outside_the_game_into_hand_clause`) resolved to nothing and is read now, sharing Karn's `_reveal_and_bring_into_hand`; its "Exile `<this>`" is CR 201.5's self-reference, and CR 608.2n's graveyard step skips a spell already in exile. Glittering Wish's "multicolored" (CR 105.2b) and "monocolored" (CR 105.2a) are read as color counts by the shared `_quality_matcher` (`_COLOR_COUNT_WORDS`), so it is no longer left unread. Learn's Lesson half (CR 701.48a, "If you didn't discard a card, you may reveal a Lesson card you own from outside the game and put it into your hand") is performed by `machines/effects.learn` through the same `_reveal_and_bring_into_hand`, offering only CR 205.3k Lesson cards, and only when no card was discarded; before this, `learn` did only the discard-to-draw half and claimed the engine had no outside-the-game group. Wish ("You may play a card you own from outside the game this turn") brings its card into exile, a public zone, so it needs no carry. The reveal callers (opening-hand reveal, Goblin Guide shape, Karn -2, the Burning Wish family, Wish, explore) populate the new fields through `Game.reveal`; Mishra's Bauble's "look at the top card of target player's library" (and every printing of that clause) now records a look through `Game.look`. Library-top looks and reveals record every card shown, following the printed verb: Goblin Charbelcher's reveal-until (`_parse_reveal_until_land_damage_clause`) and the reveal-top-N-one-pick-per-card-type run (`_merge_reveal_top_one_card_per_type_clauses`: Atraxa, Grand Unifier; Portent of Calamity) record a public `Reveal` per card; Duskwatch Recruiter's family (`_merge_look_top_reveal_to_hand_clauses`) records a public reveal for the card taken, and its looks come from `Game.look_at_top_and_split`, one per card. Cards then put into the hand are carried; cards put on the bottom "in any order" (CR 401.4) stay known to the controller until the next reordering, and cards put on the bottom "in a random order" (Narset, Parter of Veils; Thundertrap Trainer, through `rest_in_random_order=True`) are ended by the epoch. Schema bumped 7 -> 8, then 8 -> 9 on merging `Decision.source_id`, which had bumped 7 -> 8 independently. **Recorded by the library-selection keyword actions** (CR 400.2, 406.3, 701.22a, 701.23a, 701.23e, 701.25a, 702.75a, 702.85a): `Game.scry` records a look for the scrier on every card put back, top or bottom, after the put-back moves the epoch, and `Game.surveil` does the same for the cards kept on top (a card put into the graveyard is public and gets no record). All three first record a look for the chooser on every looked-at card, where it sits, before asking where each goes (CR 701.22a and CR 701.25a look, "then put"), so the look is live while the choice is pending - a paused command's half-applied game holds it; `_end_looks` drops those records at the put-back (CR 701.20d), leaving one look per card. `Game.look_at_top_and_split` records a look for the chooser on every looked-at card pinned to the epoch one reordering on, the one its caller's single put-back produces, so the rest put back into the library is known against the chooser's order (a caller putting the rest back in a random order pins it to the current epoch instead, so the put-back ends it); a card that went anywhere else has a new stamp and fails closed. Cascade (`machines/keywords.cascade`) reveals every card it exiles face up to all players; the bottomed ones change zones into a reordered library and are known to nobody. Hideaway (`_hideaway_effect`) records a look for its controller on each looked-at card (voided by the bottoming) and a look on the face-down exiled card against its exile stamp, so it stays known to that player through a library shuffle and ends when it leaves exile (CR 406.3). CR 702.75a grants the look to "the player who controls the permanent that exiled this card", so `Game.note_hideaway_viewers` records a look for the linked permanent's current controller as the card is exiled and again whenever `ContinuousEffects.create`/`add` stores a layer 2 control effect (Threaten on Watcher for Tomorrow); CR 406.3's "once a player is allowed to look ... may continue to look" keeps that look after control goes back, until the card leaves exile. Watcher for Tomorrow's "When this creature leaves the battlefield, put the exiled card into its owner's hand" is the CR 607.2a linked reference `_parse_return_imprinted_clause` already read for Ugin's Labyrinth's "return ... to" wording, now matching the "put ... into" wording too; the CR 603.10a look-back trigger finds the hidden card through `Game.card_imprinted_on` and its face-down look ends as it leaves exile. `Game.search_library` records nothing: the searcher's view ends in the CR 701.24a shuffle. **A search whose text prints a reveal** (CR 701.23e) records the find publicly. Every search-reveal-put template goes through `Game.search_and_put`, which searches, reveals each find while it is still the library's object (CR 701.20a-b), puts it, then shuffles. So a find put into its owner's hand is carried, and known to every player until it changes zones. The templates are: `_SEARCH_AND_PUT_RE` and `_REFERENT_SEARCH_RE`'s "reveal it"/"reveal that card" (Expedition Map, Ranger-Captain of Eos, Trinket Mage, Sylvan Scrying, and the Sanctum of Ugin/Formidable Speaker consequence), `_SEARCH_UP_TO_N_AND_PUT_RE`'s "reveal them" (Tooth and Nail), `_SEARCH_MV_LTE_COUNT_RE` (Beseech the Queen), and typecycling/transmute. Before this, the regexes read and discarded the reveal, and Trinket Mage's wording did not match at all. Search reveals are proven off-pool on Trinket Mage, Sylvan Scrying, Beseech the Queen, Tooth and Nail and (no reveal) Demonic Tutor; the outside-the-game carry on Burning Wish, Living Wish and Glittering Wish, and Learn's Lesson reveal on Igneous Inspiration (with Environmental Sciences as the Lesson). Proven off-pool (neither `~/Documents/mtg-decks/decks/*/decklist.txt` nor `magic-cards-model-api/decks/*.txt` lists them) on Opt, Umbral Collar Zealot, Commune with Nature, Bloodbraid Elf (cascade), and Watcher for Tomorrow with Threaten (hideaway: the private looks at the library cards, the face-down card staying known through a shuffle until it leaves exile, and the control change). Mosswort Bridge and Fight Rigging are eldrazi-ramp deck cards and are tested beside them, not as the off-pool proof. | `scenarios/test_knowledge_expires_on_zone_change_and_shuffle.py`, `scenarios/test_known_card_drawn_stays_known.py`, `scenarios/test_looked_at_cards_known_to_looker.py`, `scenarios/test_scry_and_surveil_kept_cards_known_to_chooser.py`, `scenarios/test_cascade_and_hideaway_reveals_are_known.py`, `scenarios/test_library_search_leaves_nothing_known.py`, `scenarios/test_search_reveal_makes_the_find_known.py`, `scenarios/test_reveal_from_outside_the_game_stays_known_in_hand.py`, `scenarios/test_bottom_put_keeps_untouched_library_knowledge.py`, `scenarios/test_learn.py`, `test_known_to_purity.py`, `test_game_schema_version.py` |

They are **not** the object's characteristics. `Game.characteristics_of` / `Game.computed_board` is, and CR 613.5 has the layer system applied "continually and automatically". A land animated by earthbend (CR 701.66a) is a creature in layer 4 (CR 613.1d, "in addition to its other types" - CR 205.1b) with mana value 0 (CR 202.3a), and every consumer reading the printed side walked straight past it. **68 sites were audited across the whole engine and 63 fixed**, at the call sites - `machines/effects/` (13, behind one `computed_permanents` helper), `models/game/` (16), `machines/keywords.py` (6), `machines/cost/` (4), `machines/replacement/` (7), `machines/targeting.py` (4), `machines/legal_actions.py` (4), `machines/combat.py` (2), `machines/casting/` (2), `machines/triggers/` (2), plus `abilities.py`, `delayed.py`, `objects_as_costs.py`, `models/token.py` and `models/card_state.py`. Consequences that were live defects, not theory: Wrath of the Skies spared an animated land it should have swept; `legal_actions` never offered an animated land as an attacker or blocker even though `why_cannot_attack`/`why_cannot_block` allowed it; "sacrifice a creature" and "tap an untapped creature you control" could not be paid with one; equip refused it as a host; CR 106.6's restricted mana refused its abilities; the legend rule could not see a clone's copied name or supertype. **`CardState.types` was deliberately NOT made layer-aware**: `CardState._asking_the_board` guards re-entrancy per object, so a board computation entered from A's `.types` would read B's unguarded `.types` and start a whole nested board computation - branching, not merely recursive. Every fix is at the call site, and every loop over the battlefield hoists one `computed_board()` because `Game.characteristics_of` reruns the entire layer stack per call. The five sites left printed are each justified: `CardState.is_class`/`class_ability_text` (read from *inside* board computation by `layers.effects_for`/`quoted_ability_grants`, so the same blowup), the cast-spell trigger emitter and `ManaSpend.casting` (a spell is on the stack, which `computed_board` does not cover), and `cost.is_snow_source` (no card in the pool grants a supertype in layer 4). Copy effects and characteristic-defining abilities keep their printed reads on purpose - `layers.printed_characteristics` IS CR 613.1's starting point, and `_become_a_copy_builder` is CR 707.2's copiable values. | `scenarios/test_layer_computed_type_selection.py`, `test_restricted_mana_reads_the_computed_source.py`, `test_legal_actions_computed_creature_type.py`, `test_combat_computed_characteristics.py`, `test_targeting_computed_supertype_subtype_historic.py`, `test_computed_board_trigger_events.py`, `test_computed_board_static_reads.py`, `test_computed_board_activation_conditions.py`, `test_computed_board_cost_reduction.py`, `test_computed_board_triggers.py`, `test_sacrifice_and_tap_costs_read_the_computed_board.py`, `test_among_colors_reads_the_computed_board.py`, `test_layer_computed_dies_replacements.py`, `test_layer_computed_counter_reducer.py`, `test_layer_computed_enters_conditions.py`, `test_layer_computed_totem_armor.py`, `test_layer_computed_cast_grants.py`, `test_layer_computed_token_attacking.py`, `test_layer_computed_planeswalker.py` |

The enumeration reaches the mixture too: `Game.mana_color_options` is the pool of colours and `Game.mana_color_choice_count` how many of them are named (the mana count here, 1 everywhere else, 0 for an ability offering no choice), carried on the enumerated action as `Action.color_options` / `Action.color_choice_count` - so a caller driving the engine through `legal_actions` alone names `{W}{U}`, which the flat colour pool by itself could never express | `scenarios/test_mana_spend_restrictions.py`, `scenarios/test_mana_abilities.py`, `scenarios/test_devotion_mana_ability.py`, `scenarios/test_mana_any_combination.py` |

| Mana spend restrictions ("Spend this mana only to ...") | CR 106.6 (the restriction half of it; CR 703.4q / 500.5 for when the mana and the tag are lost; CR 118.3a for paying being the removal of *that* mana) | `models/mana.py` carries the tag on the mana in the pool, never on its source: `ManaRestriction` (the printed sentence plus a tuple of `SpendClause` alternatives), `RestrictedMana` (how much of `ManaPool.floating` carries each), and `ManaSpend` (what a cost is *for* - `casting(card, zone=...)` against `activating(card)`, which is what tells a creature **spell** apart from an ability of a creature **source**, plus the zone the cast started from - see the zone clause below). `ManaPool._spendable_buckets` removes mana the restriction forbids before the payment search runs, so an illegal purpose is **refused** rather than deprioritised; `ManaPool._buckets` then orders restricted mana ahead of unrestricted, so the mana that can do less is the mana spent and a legal play is never stranded. `ManaPool.empty` drops the tags with the mana. `machines/cost/payment.py` reads the sentence (`spend_restriction`), tags what a source produces (`CostPayment.tap_for_mana`, inferring which ability was activated from what it produced when the caller does not say - `restriction_for_production` - and reading **both** of CR 106.6's tags off that one ability, so a tap can never carry one ability's restriction beside another's spend effect), and carries the purpose (`CostPayment.spend`, set by `Casting.determine_cost` and `Game.begin_activating`). `auto_tap` offers a restricted ability exactly when the restriction permits the cost being paid. **Every spend-restriction printing in the pool is read bar one documented fail-closed row**, and `test_every_printed_restriction_in_the_pool_is_read` sweeps the pool rather than naming them, asserting the unread set is exactly `KNOWN_UNREAD_RESTRICTIONS` in both directions - so a printing added later that opens a new grammar shape fails the test instead of quietly failing closed in a game, and a row the grammar has since learned to read fails it too rather than outliving its reason. The one row is Rosheen Meanderer, kept unread on purpose as the standing proof of `Action.restriction_understood is False` (see below). Read: Shang-Chi, Master of Kung Fu, Sunken Citadel, Eldrazi Temple, Cavern of Souls (needs CR 614.12a's chosen creature type on the permanent), Delighted Halfling, Tablet of Discovery, Fíli and Kíli, Joyous, Interdimensional Web Watch, Smokebraider, Orb of Dragonkind, Woodland Weavemaster, Codsworth, Handy Helper, Séance Board, Rivaz of the Claw. Grammar shapes beyond a single quality word are read, all of them by mechanic and none by card: **(a) a joined list of qualities** - "cast instant and sorcery spells" (Tablet of Discovery), "cast Dwarf, Equipment, and Saga spells" (Fíli and Kíli, Joyous), "cast Aura and/or Equipment spells" (Codsworth, Handy Helper), "cast instant, sorcery, Demon, and Spirit spells" (Séance Board) - is ONE clause holding every listed quality, and the qualities are **alternatives**: CR 205.2b's "satisfy the criteria for any effect that applies to any of their card types" is what makes it mean that, and no spell is both an instant and a sorcery, so reading a joined list as a conjunction says nothing at all. **The joining word is the discriminator, and juxtaposition is the other reading**: "Dragon creature spells" (Rivaz of the Claw), "colorless Eldrazi spells" (Eldrazi Temple), "an Elf creature spell" (Gnarlroot Trapper) describe one object that is every one of those things at once, so every quality is required - which is what makes "artifact creature spells" refuse a plain creature, a shape no printing uses today and so one the rule has to come from the templating for. `SpendClause.joined` carries which reading a clause got, and a phrase that mixes the two ("artifact creature or enchantment spells") is refused rather than read either way. Before this, a clause asked for one of its card types **and** one of its subtypes, which is both readings applied at once: Séance Board's four alternatives permitted nothing at all, and "artifact creature spells" would have accepted a plain creature. "and", "or" and "and/or" are all joiners **and all three split two whole clauses** - "cast Elf spells and activate abilities of Elf sources" (Woodland Weavemaster) and "cast Room spells and unlock doors" (Smoky Lounge) print "and" in the role Eldrazi Temple prints "or" in, and splitting on " or " alone left the first of those reading as nothing at all. The printed word does not say which of the two roles it is in, so the whole phrase is offered to the grammar before any split: "a Knight or Equipment spell" stays one clause while Eldrazi Temple's cast-or-activate sentence still becomes two. The same ordering is what keeps ", and" from cutting an Oxford comma out of a type list: the rider cut ("and that spell can't be countered") is only tried once the whole phrase fails to read. **(b) a printed plural** - "activate abilities of Elementals" (Smokebraider), "of Dragons" (Orb of Dragonkind), "of artifacts" (Soldevi Machinist) - names the subtype or card type a type line prints in the singular, and nothing in a game state ever holds the plural, so the clause matched nothing while `understood` still reported True. `data/subtypes.py` reads it back: every subtype WOTC has printed (Scryfall's catalogs, written by `scripts/add_subtypes.py`, the same list CR 205.3g-q prints) run through the plural forms English gives a word of its shape, indexed, and a printed word that lands on no subtype - or on two - resolves to nothing and fails the clause closed. It runs from the known subtype outwards rather than singularising an arbitrary word, which is what makes Elves/Elf, Mice/Mouse, Oxen/Ox and Fungi/Fungus work beside Myr and Eldrazi, and what keeps a wrong morphology rule from ever inventing a subtype. A two-word subtype ("Time Lord", the one CR 205.3m names) is not joined back up and so fails closed. **(c) a zone tail** - "cast spells from exile" (Interdimensional Web Watch) - puts one of CR 400.1's zones on `SpendClause.zone`, checked against `ManaSpend.zone`. That zone is the one the cast *started* in: CR 601.2a moves the card to the stack as the first step of the announcement, so it is carried from `Casting.origin_zone` (the payment path) and `CardState.zone` (the `legal_actions` enumeration) rather than read off the spell, and `ManaSpend.casting` takes it as a keyword argument with **no default** so no call site can quietly guess "hand". A zone phrase this engine cannot check - one naming an owner ("from your graveyard"), since `ManaSpend` carries the zone and not whose it was, or a non-zone word ("from anywhere other than your hand") - fails the whole restriction closed rather than being widened to every zone. **CR 106.6's second clause is modelled too** - "an additional effect that affects the spell or ability that mana is spent on". `models/mana.ManaSpendEffect` is the tag (the printed sentence), `SpendEffectMana` says how much of the pool carries it, `_Bucket` gained a fourth slot for it beside the restriction slot, and `ManaPayment.spend_effects_spent` records which of the mana a payment actually spent carried one. Both production sites tag it (`Game.activate_ability` and `CostPayment.tap_for_mana`, off `ManaAbility.spend_effect`), `Casting._move_to_the_stack` records it on `CastRecord.spend_effects` at CR 601.2h, and `Game._apply_mana_spend_effects` turns it into the layer 6 grant (CR 613.1f) as the permanent enters, read by `machines/layers.spend_effect_effects`. Arena of Glory's haste is the printing that works end to end. An unreadable sentence gives nothing away rather than failing closed, because this clause never narrows what the mana may pay for. **Still not modelled**: the "and that spell can't be countered" form of the same clause (Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling) and CR 106.6's third thing, a delayed triggered ability. Clause qualities outside the closed vocabulary ("kicked spells", "spells with mana value 4 or greater", "your commander") are unread and so fail closed; no printing in the pool has one. A payment that cannot name what it is for (`CostPayment.spend` left `None` - a foretell/plot cost, a keyword "unless you pay") gets no restricted mana at all, and a sentence the grammar cannot read produces a restriction with no clauses that permits nothing: both fail closed. Restricted mana added by an *effect* rather than a mana ability (`machines/effects/`'s mana-adding clauses) is still added untagged. **The restriction is now visible before the mana is made, not only after.** `machines/legal_actions._mana_descriptor` fills three flat fields on every `ACTIVATE_MANA` action - `Action.produces` (the printed "Add ..." phrase, read by `machines/abilities.printed_production`), `Action.restriction` (`spend_restriction`'s own `ManaRestriction.text`, verbatim) and `Action.restriction_understood` (`ManaRestriction.understood`, where `False` is the loud "this mana will pay for nothing" case) - so a seat choosing between two abilities on one permanent can tell them apart by what they *do*. Eldrazi Temple's two rows used to be byte-identical apart from `ability_index`, and Cavern of Souls's two overlap in colour as well, so `color_options` alone could not separate them either. Deliberately **not** board-resolved: Nykthos's CR 700.5 devotion count and Mox Amber's CR 106.5 narrowing are both unknowable before a colour is chosen, and an `Action` is a snapshot a caller acts on later, so a number that has since gone wrong is worse than no number - counting and colour resolution stay in `Game.activate_ability`. Both `Action` construction sites in `_battlefield_ability_actions` read one `_ManaDescriptor` computed once per ability, the `Affordability.UNKNOWN` fallback for an unpriceable activation cost included, since that is exactly where a descriptor would otherwise be dropped. Each inline resolution that adds mana re-raises that event, and the chain is bounded by `Game.TRIGGERED_MANA_ABILITY_LOOP_BOUND`, past which `Game.drawn` is set (CR 104.4b). **This is the only loop shape detected anywhere** - see `Game.drawn`'s docstring. **Both mana paths resolve them inline now** (battle 7, B7-02): `Game.activate_ability`'s fast path used to discard the triggers CR 106.12a's tap event raised, so Leyline of Abundance's and Badgermole Cub's "add an additional {G}" went on the stack, and `CostPayment.tap_for_mana` queued them for the stack too. Both now hand the tap event's and the adding event's triggers to `resolve_triggered_mana_abilities`, which resolves each CR 605.1b ability (no target, an effect `machines/abilities.parse_triggered_mana` reads as adding mana) without `_resolve_ability`'s before-priority step, into `Game.mana_pool_receiving` - the open payment's pool during a payment, so the mana pays that cost (CR 601.2g-h) and CR 733.1's rewind takes it back. The readable mana is a literal symbol run, "one mana of the chosen/that color", "N mana of any color / in any combination of colors" (asked of the player adding it, CR 608.2d) and "one mana of any type that <permanent> produced" (the tap event's `mana_added`); the recipient is the ability's controller, "its controller" (the tapped permanent's) or "that player". A land subtype in the condition ("a Swamp", "a Forest is tapped") is matched (`_required_tapped_subtype`). **The payment search counts it** (B7-03): `_scan_mana_candidates` extends each source's options with `triggered_mana_bonus` (the triggers a tap would set off, read by the side-effect-free `machines/triggers.abilities_triggered_by`), so `auto_tap`, `plan_mana_payment`, `could_pay_mana_cost`, `legal_actions` affordability and dry-run casts all see it; a plan entry lists the ability's own mana first, and `tap_for_mana` accepts a production naming the triggered mana after it (`_activated_mana_ability_with_triggers`), passing those colours as `color_hints`. Proven off-pool on Wild Growth, Fertile Ground, Nirkana Revenant, Vernal Bloom and Zendikar Resurgent. **A count** ("<mana> for each <Subtype or card type> on the battlefield / you control", `machines/abilities.parse_mana_count`) is taken as the mana is added (CR 608.2h, `machines/triggers.triggered_mana_count`) and by the payment search, which is deterministic because the tap changes no count; proven off-pool on Elvish Guidance. **"May add"** (CR 608.2d) is asked in place as a `MAY` question, and an unscripted seat takes the mana (the engine's `MAY` default). Snowfall's "If that Island is snow, ... instead" reads the tapped permanent's computed snow supertype (CR 205.4a), and its "Spend this mana only to pay cumulative upkeep costs" travels on the mana as a CR 106.6 restriction; the restriction grammar reads it into `SpendPurpose.PAY_CUMULATIVE_UPKEEP`, which only a cumulative upkeep payment carries (see the Cumulative upkeep row), so the mana pays that and nothing else. In the payment search a may is not deterministic, so a plan may take it or leave it: `CostPayment.auto_tap` answers the may from its own plan (taken if the plan counted the mana, declined if not, never asked mid-payment), and a hand-pinned tap asks. Restricted bonus mana is left out of the search, because the candidate scan is hoisted independent of what is being paid for. Snowfall, the only printing of a "may add" triggered mana ability, is off-pool. Radha, Heir to Keld, Thran Turbine and Mana Echoes also print "may add" but trigger on no mana ability, so CR 605.5a keeps them on the stack. Not read: Sasaya's Essence's "for each other land you control with the same name as it" (its only printing is the flipped face of a flip card, which can never be on the battlefield here, see Not modelled), a condition naming a mana type (Gauntlet of Power) and "land creature" (Autumn Willow): each fails closed to the ordinary stack. Caged Sun's own "add an additional one mana of that color" is read now by `_parse_mana_adding_trigger`, whose "one mana of the chosen color" shape was widened to CR 607.1's anaphoric "that color" (the same CR 614.12a choice on `CardState.choice`). **Still missing, in `models/game/_stack_priority.py`**: the same `and ability.ability.event is not None` gate on `Game._effect_of` - Caged Sun's condition has no `TriggerEvent` either, so the effect is never looked up | `judge/test_judge_mana_abilities.py`, `scenarios/test_triggered_mana_abilities.py`, `scenarios/test_mana_adding_triggers.py`, `scenarios/test_tap_for_mana_triggers.py` |

## Can you actually play a game?

A game starts and runs now: `Match.start_game` loads each registered deck
(`Player.load_deck`, with the sideboard set aside for games two and three -
CR 103.2a), shuffles it seeded (CR 103.3), sets life to 20 (CR 103.4), deals
opening hands of seven (CR 103.5), and then leaves the game *resting* in
`Step.MULLIGAN` - the first of two pregame steps that are not CR 500 steps of a
turn (CR 500.1) and say so: no phase, `turn_number` and `turns_taken` at 0, no
priority. Seats declare through `Game.declare_mulligan` and take CR 103.6's
actions through `Game.take_opening_hand_action` /
`Game.finish_opening_hand_actions`, none of which asks anybody anything, so a
live seat never blocks the engine. `Game.settle_pregame` - which
`Match.run_mulligans` is a thin wrapper over - is the headless path and settles
both sequences through the ordinary decision defaults in one call. Who goes
first is decided by CR 103.1 - randomly,
by name, or by the loser of the previous game through `Match.chooser_for_next_game`.
`scenarios/test_starting_a_game.py`, `scenarios/test_mulligans.py`,
`scenarios/test_pregame_steps.py`, and
`scenarios/test_opening_hand_actions.py` play it
through with real tournament decklists. From there, `Game(automatic_turn_based_actions=True)`
drives the whole turn: untap, draw, the combat declarations through the decision
machinery, cleanup - a creature attack declared by its player, blocked by the
defender, and dealt damage, all from `advance()` (`scenarios/test_combat_turn_based_actions.py`).

What still separates this from a game two people could actually play:

1. **The card effects registry is the bottleneck.** `machines/effects/` is a
   hand-written registry keyed by card name; every card without an entry
   resolves as a no-op, which is most of them. Casting, targeting, paying, and
   the stack all work - it is the resolution that does nothing. **A slice of
   this is now closed**: `parse_player_effect`/`parse_player_effect_for_spell`
   read a single-clause, no-target, no-choice player effect - life gain and
   loss, energy, drawing, milling, surveil, scry, and any straight-line
   combination of those joined by "and"/"then"/a sentence boundary (CR
   608.2c) - straight off a card's own printed text, tried on a registry miss
   in all three resolution paths (`effect_for`, `trigger_effect_for`,
   `activated_effect_for`). It fails **closed**: one clause it cannot read
   (a target, a modal choice) throws the whole effect away rather than
   running the part it understood. **"You may `<clause>`." is now read
   too** (CR 608.2d), for both the player-effect wave above and the
   targeted wave (destroy/exile/return/tap/untap/counters/damage-target,
   `parse_targeted_effect`/`parse_targeted_effect_for_spell`) - wrapping is
   only ever applied over a clause the parser already understands, so "you
   may `<something unread>`" still throws the whole effect away rather than
   asking a question it could not carry out. "`<A>`. If you do, `<B>`." (CR
   118.12) is now read for the **sacrifice** shape: "you may sacrifice this
   `<type>`" (Sanctum of Ugin - the permanent bearing the ability itself,
   never a choice among several) and "you may sacrifice another `<type>`"
   (Disciple of Freyalise - a real CR 608.2d choice among whatever the
   player controls of that type), each paired with its own "if you do"
   consequence - a plain mandatory search (`_search_and_place_for`, run with
   `optional=False` since CR 118.12's own "you may" already gated it) or a
   magnitude-threaded pair of clauses reading "X" as the sacrificed
   permanent's power, captured before `Game.sacrifice` moves it to the
   graveyard the same CR 608.2i way `_parse_anaphoric_clause_pair` already
   does. CR 118.12's own text is the reason the consequence never re-checks
   the board afterward: "the 'If \[a player\] does' clause checks whether
   the player chose to pay ... regardless of what events actually
   occurred" - CR 701.21a's sacrifice has no failure mode for a permanent
   the player controls, so "did you do it" is only ever "did you say yes".
   `machines/effects._parse_conditional_sacrifice_clause`,
   `ConditionalClauseNotice`; `scenarios/test_conditional_sacrifice_clauses.py`.
   Still not implemented: the **pay-life** cousin of the same CR 118.12 shape -
   Necrodominance's "you may pay any amount of life. If you do, draw that many
   cards." It once needed a decision primitive this engine did not have -
   "choose an amount of life to pay" is not `PAY_LIFE`'s fixed `amount`, and
   no `DecisionKind` read a variable answer back as an integer. That primitive
   exists now: `DecisionKind.PAY_ENERGY_AMOUNT` and `Game.pay_any_amount_of_
   energy` (see the energy row above), built for Galvanic Discharge's and
   Wrath of the Skies's own "you may pay any amount of {E}" rather than for
   Necrodominance - its own clause is still unwired, but the missing piece was
   the shape of the question (an integer, not a boolean), which is no longer
   a gap in the machinery, only in which cards call it. **Turntimber
   Symbiosis's own clause is fixed (W13)** - see its own row below in "Cards
   from the metagame" - and turned out not to need this primitive at all: "you
   may put a creature card ... onto the battlefield. If that card has mana
   value 3 or less, ..." is a plain CR 608.2d `MAY`/`CHOOSE_CARDS` choice with
   a check on the chosen card's own mana value read inline, not an amount
   fed back as an integer. Targeted effects with a restriction the
   parser cannot enforce, other choices, and token creation are still the
   registry's job.
2. **Opening-hand actions are modelled; CR 103.5b's are not.** CR 103.6's
   sequence is a step the game rests in (`Step.PREGAME_ACTIONS`), driven either
   seat by seat through `Game.take_opening_hand_action` /
   `Game.finish_opening_hand_actions` or in one call by
   `Game.take_opening_hand_actions`, over `machines/opening_hand.py` - both
   subrules, in CR 103.6's own order (starting player first, then the rest).
   CR 103.6a's begin-on-the-battlefield action covers the four Leylines in the
   pool and Gemstone Caverns, including its "you're not the starting player"
   restriction (CR 103.8), its luck counter, and its "exile a card from your
   hand" rider; CR 103.6b's reveal covers Devourer of Destiny, including the
   delayed triggered ability (CR 603.7) its reveal creates for the revealer's
   first upkeep, and Chancellor of the Forge's "at the beginning of the first
   upkeep" (the game's first upkeep, whoever's). Riders are parsed, never
   looked up by name (`machines/opening_hand.read_rider`): "If you do, " plus
   an optional "at the beginning of your/the first upkeep, " (a
   `CreatedTriggeredAbility` delayed trigger, CR 603.7) plus an effect read by
   `trigger_effect_for`. Both are asked as a `DecisionKind.OPENING_HAND_ACTION`
   question and declined by an unscripted player. See
   `scenarios/test_opening_hand_actions.py`,
   `scenarios/test_opening_hand_begin_on_battlefield.py` and
   `scenarios/test_opening_hand_reveal_first_upkeep.py`. **What is left**: CR
   103.5b's "any time [that player] could mulligan" effects, and a rider with
   other timing - Chancellor of the Annex's "when each opponent casts their
   first spell of the game", Chancellor of the Tangle's "your first main phase"
   - neither is in the fixture pool. A card that prints an opening-hand
   paragraph the reader cannot match, or one that matches but carries a rider
   `read_rider` cannot read, is refused
   the action outright and recorded on `Game.opening_hand_notices` rather than
   half-performed.
3. **Decisions default rather than ask.** Unscripted questions - a mulligan,
   an attack declaration - take the documented default answer rather than
   waiting for a player, because there is no player agent: a human at the API
   or a scenario script is the only source of answers. That is a default, not
   a wall: `MAY`/`PAY_LIFE`/`SCRY`/`SURVEIL`/`CHOOSE_CARDS`/`CHOOSE_TARGETS`
   flow through `Game.ask`, and CR 103.5's mulligan declaration follows the
   same order inside `ask_mulligan` (script, then `DecisionScript.recorded`,
   then `default_answer`), so a live caller answers by staging into the script
   or the tape. The two combat declarations (`ask_attackers`, `ask_blockers`)
   follow the identical order - script, then tape, then `default_answer` -
   through `DecisionScript.take`/`take_from_tape` directly rather than
   `Game.ask`.

Scenario tests that need the manual path still call the combat moves by hand;
`automatic_turn_based_actions` off leaves every turn-based action to the caller.

### A harness convenience, not a rule: auto-passing after an action (magic-cards-model-api)

The self-test API's player-facing tools (`magic-cards-model-api`'s `mcp.py`
and `seat_cli.py`) make every action tool - `cast`, `play_land`, `activate`,
`declare_attackers`, `declare_blockers`, `resolve_top`, `advance`, `decide`,
`pass` - do the action, then release priority, then block until that seat next
has something to do, all in one call. The engine's own rule underneath this is
correct and unchanged: **CR 117.3c** - "If a player has priority when they
cast a spell, activate an ability, or take a special action, that player
receives priority afterward" - which is exactly what `Game.retain_priority`
already gives back to the actor. What the harness adds on top is a
convenience, not part of the rule: it auto-passes that regained priority away
on the caller's behalf unless the caller asks to keep it, because two
AI agents playing through a seat found "act, then separately remember to
pass, then wait" chatty and easy to forget a step of. The escape hatch back to
the real rule is the `hold_priority` parameter every one of those tools takes:
set true, the action still runs and the actor still keeps priority exactly as
CR 117.3c says, but the tool returns immediately without auto-passing or
blocking - for casting into one's own trick, activating twice before passing,
or any other sequence a human player would do without giving priority up
first. See `magic-cards-model-api/src/magic_cards_model_api/seatkit.py` for
the implementation (`run_action`) shared by both transports.

Every row here is a gap that still exists, checked against the source in the
session that last edited this file. `scripts/known_gaps.py` reprints this table
as the "do not report these" brief handed to playtest agents, so a row that
describes *finished* work costs a real bug report - if a mechanic works, its row
belongs in the Modelled table above or nowhere. Roughly in the order they block
other work.

Slumbering Trudge's "three minus X" parses into the expression shape and has no resolver, so it is skipped too. |
| Self-replacement effects | CR 614.15, 616.1a | CR 616.1a's forced first choice is a hook in `order_effects` that never fires, because a self-replacement effect is an effect of a *resolving spell* replacing its own effect and `machines/effects/` has no way to express one. Not to be confused with `ReplacementEffect.self_replacement`, which is CR 614.12's narrower "affects only that permanent". |
| Skip effects, and replacing a step | CR 614.1b, 614.10, 614.10a, 614.10b, 500.11 | `ReplacementKind.SKIP` is produced by the parser and consumed nowhere. Only two skips are hand-rolled: `Game.players_skipping_next_untap` (a per-username count, so two grants cost two untap steps) and `TurnMachine.skips_draw` for CR 103.8a. Necrodominance's "Skip your draw step" feeds neither, and no phase or whole turn can be skipped. |
| Replacing a draw with something other than a draw or a mill | CR 121.6, 121.6b, 614.11a | `ReplaceableEvent` carries a player and a count, and nothing that could name a substituted action. Redirecting a draw to another player (Plagiarize) and doubling one are both built; dredge's own mill-and-return is now offered too (`Game._offer_dredge`, FD1). Replacing a draw with a reveal or a search is not. |
| Effects that say something *can't* happen | CR 614.17, 614.17c | Only CR 614.17d's can't-enter family is built (`_cant_enter_replacements`, Grafdigger's Cage). CR 614.17c's precedence - "if an event can't happen, it can only be replaced by a self-replacement effect" - is a rule this machinery cannot express, so a can't-enter effect competes for CR 616.1's ordering instead of pre-empting it. Every other "can't" effect is unmodelled. |
| Modal templating other than bullets | CR 700.2e, 700.2i, 601.7 | Pawprint modes and a mode chosen by a player other than the controller leave `ModalProfile.understood` False. CR 700.2h (a mode with its own cost printed before its effect - Spree, Tiered) is built: `machines/modes.py` reads the keyword's own reminder-text parenthetical as the instruction line and each mode's cost via `Mode.cost`, `machines/casting/`'s `choose_modes` charges it automatically as CR 601.2f-h's mandatory additional cost, and `machines/effects/`'s `mode_effect_text` strips the cost prefix before resolution (`scenarios/test_tiered.py`, Fire Magic and the off-pool Thunder Magic). **No longer left open**: CR 702.172b's `+`-symbol bullets are read - bullet detection widens to `•` or `+` followed by whitespace, told apart from a loyalty ability's own "+1:"/"+2:" line (CR 606.4) by that whitespace - proved against real Spree printings (`scenarios/test_spree_bullets.py`: Smuggler's Surprise, Three Steps Ahead, the off-pool Final Showdown), including choosing one, two, or all three modes (the costs summed as CR 702.172a's own additional cost), zero modes refused, and a mode this wave does not yet read (Final Showdown's own "lose all abilities"/"gains indestructible" modes) failing closed with a `ModeNotice` rather than blocking the readable one. **T16 closed every mode of the four pool Spree cards** (`--card` reports all four HANDLED): a general "search your library for `<quality>` card[, reveal it,] then shuffle and put that card on top" reader with an optional reveal (Insatiable Avarice's own first mode, off-pool proof Ainok Guide, `scenarios/test_search_put_on_top.py`); a general "target creature becomes a `<color>` `<creature type>` with base power and toughness N/M[ until end of turn]" layer effect, leading or trailing duration, one ability in four layers (Metamorphic Blast, off-pool proof Startling Development, `scenarios/test_becomes_creature_type_and_base_pt.py`); a general "mill N. You may put [up to K] `<description>` cards from among the milled cards into your hand" reader widened to an "and/or"-joined quality list, and given its first path from a mode's own text at all (Smuggler's Surprise's first mode, off-pool proof Seed of Hope, `scenarios/test_mill_then_take_from_milled.py`); the mass-pump/keyword-grant family's bare "creatures you control" subject widened with a "with power N or greater" filter, the set of creatures locked in once at resolution (CR 611.2c) rather than re-checked as power changes afterward (Smuggler's Surprise's third mode, off-pool proof Gustrider Exuberant, `scenarios/test_group_grant_power_filter.py`); and the token-copy-of-target reader's noun phrase widened from the single literal "target creature you control" to "target `<word>`[ or `<word>`] you control" (Three Steps Ahead's second mode, off-pool proof Cackling Counterpart, `scenarios/test_token_copy_of_target.py`). Two adjacent defects surfaced and were fixed alongside: `mode_rules_text` (`machines/modes.py`) fed the targeting parser a mode's own *unstripped* CR 700.2h cost prefix, so a mode whose printed cost digit differed from its own target count (Metamorphic Blast's second mode, `{3} — Target player draws two cards.`) could never be cast with a legal target list at all - it now strips the cost the same way `mode_effect_text` already does for a resolution-time reader; and `_mass_creature_group_targets`'s own plain-prefix `startswith` check silently dropped a "with power N or greater" filter and swept in every creature the caster controls rather than reading it - now checked before that fallback. |
| Keyword abilities with no execution path | CR 702 | `scripts/sweep_pool.py --keywords` is the list, and **the number it prints is the number** - re-run it rather than quoting a figure from here, because the pool grows and this row goes stale the moment a card is added. Two cautions about that report. It counts a keyword as executed only if `machines/combat.py`, `machines/casting/` or the mana path reads it, so improvise, splice and firebending are listed despite being wired up elsewhere (`models/game/_casting.py`'s `Game.cast` for improvise - see the object-cost-payment row above for the defect this used to be a false negative for, before `Game.cast` actually called into it - `Casting.splice`, `keywords._TRIGGER_EXPANSIONS`) - a gap in `executed_keywords`, not in the engine. And Scryfall's `keywords` includes mode names: "Look Around", "Bring Down", "Mind Swap", "Darkforce Inversion" and "Project Image" are CR 207.2d flavor words with no rules meaning. |

CR 704.5d, CR 704.5e (both sentences, `Game._copies_that_cease_to_exist`), CR 704.5f, CR 704.5h, CR 704.5i, CR 704.5m, CR 704.5n, CR 704.5p and CR 704.5z are all dispatched from `Game._state_based_actions_once`. |

What it still cannot judge is a *player's* protection against an "Enchant player" Aura, and an Aura that is also a creature. Both fail open. No pairing in the pool reaches either. |

Reducing by a Phyrexian or snow symbol (CR 118.7g) is modelled, and a cost containing hybrid, Phyrexian or snow symbols survives any increase or reduction intact. |

The rules do not say this in so many words; it follows from CR 107.4e leaving the choice until the cost is paid. |
| Where the CR 601.2f self-reduction hook lives | CR 601.2f | `Casting.determine_cost` does not consult the game, so a spell that reduces its own cost off the board only gets its discount through `Game.determine_total_cost`. A scenario that calls `casting.determine_cost()` directly pays full price. |
| `count_expression`'s qualifier is a single card type only | CR 205.2a, 300.1 | `machines/effects/amounts.py`'s shared "the number of \<type>[s] you control" / "\<type> cards in your graveyard" evaluator reads the fifteen card types and nothing else. A coloured qualifier, a named-subtype qualifier, or a compound one returns `None` and the caller falls through to its ordinary fail-closed path rather than guessing. No card in the pool needs one yet. |
| A mana ability's own "another effect" beyond three known shapes | CR 405.6c, 605.1a | `machines/abilities._parse_mana_rider` reads "This \<noun> deals N damage to you.", "You lose N life." and "You gain N life." off a mana ability's trailing sentence. Any other shape becomes `ManaAbility.unparsed_rider` and `Game.why_cannot_activate` refuses the whole activation - CR 405.6c ties the mana and the other effect together as one event, so minting the mana while dropping the rider would be a silent wrong answer. No printing in the pool exercises this path. |
| A cast-trigger's mana-value clause in an unrecognised shape | CR 202.3 | `condition_matches` reads five comparison shapes. A condition that says "mana value" some other way fails the whole condition closed rather than being read as unrestricted, and records a `CastConditionNotice` so the gap is visible. No printing in the pool needs one. |
| A token-creating trigger's effect anaphoric to the permanent that just entered | CR 707.2, 400.7 | Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm's "Whenever another nontoken Dragon you control enters, create a token that's a copy of it, except the token isn't legendary" and Ashling, the Limitless's "Whenever you sacrifice a nontoken Elemental, create a token that's a copy of it" both read "it" back to the permanent the trigger's own event just named - distinct from `_parse_city_blessing_token_copy_clause`'s ascend shape ("a token you control that entered this turn") and from `_parse_create_token_copy_of_target_clause`'s targeted shape, neither of which this is. `_parse_token_clause` refuses any "copy of" clause outright (CR 707.2 needs copiable values it does not read), and no `TRIGGER_EFFECTS` row exists for either card, so both conditions now fire correctly (2026-09-08's nontoken fix, `docs/2026-09-08-trigger-findings.md`) and both resolve to nothing: `trigger_effect_for` falls through to `None`, the same fail-closed, no-partial-instruction silence CR 608.2c already gives every other unread effect in this table. Exposed by that same fix - previously unreachable because both conditions never matched at all. |
| Ashling, the Limitless's own sacrifice condition reads only "nontoken", not "Elemental" | CR 205.3a, 603.2 | "You sacrifice a nontoken Elemental" needs a creature-subtype check the same way Miirym's "nontoken Dragon" needs one on ENTERS_THE_BATTLEFIELD (`_required_entering_subtype`/`_subtype_matches`) - `condition_matches`'s IS_SACRIFICED branch has no equivalent read for a subtype at all, only `_types_match`'s card types, which "Elemental" is not one of. The 2026-09-08 nontoken fix enforces "nontoken" there but does not add subtype enforcement, so as shipped Ashling's trigger fires on sacrificing any nontoken permanent, not only an Elemental one. `docs/2026-09-08-trigger-findings.md` scoped this fix to the nontoken restriction specifically; the subtype gap is a separate, adjacent one. |
| "Becomes crewed" | CR 702.122e | CR 702.122e's "whenever this Vehicle becomes crewed" reads as "whenever a crew ability of this Vehicle resolves", which needs a trigger event nothing emits; a Vehicle printing one would crew correctly and never fire it. CR 702.122d's "can't crew Vehicles" is not read either. Convoke and delve are not offered *automatically* - `CostPayment.auto_tap` solves mana only. Harmonize is not wired up either - the keyword appears nowhere in `src/`, no printing in the pool carries it, and `knowledge_search` returned no numbered rule for it, so none is cited. |
| Multiplayer options beyond Free-for-All defaults | CR 801.3, 802.3, 803.1, 805.8, 806.2b, 808.3a, 800.4a | Free-for-All with its defaults works at three or more players. Not modelled: limited range of influence, the attack-left/right and attack-multiple-players options (`declare_attacker` will let any opponent be attacked), and every team variant. CR 800.4a moves a departed player's objects by *controller* - `Game._player_left` selects on `state.controller == username` even though ownership is modelled separately on `CardState.owner`. |
| Protection beyond targeting, damage, attachment and blocking | CR 702.16c, 702.16j | CR 702.16b and CR 702.16e are enforced end to end, for granted protection as well as printed, and for players as well as permanents. Since S23, CR 702.16c (Auras), CR 702.16d (Equipment, Fortifications) and CR 702.16f (blocking an attacker) are enforced for a protected *permanent* - see the S23 section. Not enforced: CR 702.16c for a *player* with protection against an "Enchant player" Aura. "Protection from everything" (CR 702.16j) is enforced since EP-01 R2 T2. |
| Making a controlled player act, beyond priority | CR 723.5, 723.5b, 723.7 | `PriorityMachine.require` gives the pass to the controller and refuses it to the controlled player. Casting, activating, attacking and blocking take no "who decided this" argument, so nothing checks that the controller chose: `Game.why_cannot_decide_for` answers the question and has no production caller - only assertions in `scenarios/test_controlling_another_player.py`. (Whose resources pay, CR 723.5a, is enforced: see the row above.) CR 723.7's restrict/require clauses are not modelled. |
| Emrakul, the Promised End's control duration | CR 723.1 | The cast trigger is fully registered, control half and extra turn both. `Game.gain_control_of_player` takes no duration argument, so control is handed over and never returned. |
| Imprint clause shapes other than the two now read | CR 207.2c, 607.2a | `_parse_imprint_clause` reads only "you may exile a `<quality>` card ... from your hand"; `_merge_each_player_clauses` reads only "each player exiles the top N cards of their library[ face down]". An "Imprint —" (or plain "exiled with `<name>`") clause shaped some other way - "exile up to one target card" (a targeted exile rather than a `may` choice), "look at the top N cards of your library and exile one" (a choice among a dig rather than a flat count) - leaves no link and no `ImprintNotice` either, since neither parser even matches it to know it failed. No printing in the pool needs one yet; if one does, it should get its own notice the way the two shapes above already have. |
| Persist (the sorcery), and any "return target ... to the battlefield with a counter on it" card | CR 614.1c | Persist's own "Return target nonlegendary creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield with a -1/-1 counter on it" is CR 614.1c's *enters-with* replacement, not a return-then-add-counters sequence - nothing in `Game.put_onto_battlefield`/`enter_the_battlefield` (`models/game/_stack_priority.py:4602`, `:4460`) accepts a counter argument, and the entering-with path is driven off the *entering permanent's own printed text* (`game.py:4470-4475`), which a target chosen by another card's ability is not. The nearest precedent, `_parse_put_exiled_target_onto_battlefield_clause`, adds counters **after** the permanent is already on the battlefield, and its own docstring says that ordering is only correct because that card's counters are "additional" rather than part of how the permanent enters - copying it for Persist would let the reanimated creature exist briefly at its full toughness (e.g. a 1/1 alive for an instant) before the counter lands, a wrong event order a state-based action or a "dies as it enters" trigger could observe. Left unread (not shipped, not xfailed as a scenario - the effect registry simply has no entry for this card's clause; not to be confused with the *keyword* Persist, CR 702.79a, which is fully modelled - see the Modelled table's "Persist, and last known counters" row). |
| "Except the first one you draw in each of your draw steps" on a draw *replacement* | CR 504.1, 121.2, 500.8 | Alhammarret's Archive's replacement (`machines/replacement._archive_draw_applies`) reads `ReplaceableEvent.draw_step_draw`, which `Game.draw_cards` sets for the first card of *every* draw instruction made during the active player's draw step (`index == 0`), not for the first card drawn in that step. A second instruction in the same draw step (a Brainstorm after the turn-based draw) is therefore wrongly exempted too. The trigger side of the same wording (Orcish Bowmasters) already reads the per-step count `Game.cards_drawn_in_own_draw_step` instead; the replacement side has not been moved onto it. Noted 2026-09-22, not fixed. |
| Fuse's target legality recheck loses per-half protection specificity | CR 702.102b/d, 702.16b | `Casting.targeting`/`Game._resolution_profile` combine both halves' `TargetingProfile`s when a spell is fused (`machines/casting.cast_fused`, `tests/scenarios/test_fuse.py`), but the combined profile is built with `source_card=None` rather than either half's own `Card` - `TargetRequirement.rejects`'s CR 702.16b protection-quality check (a permanent with protection from the *source's* colors/types can't be targeted) reads `TargetingProfile.source_card` for that comparison, and a fused spell has two source cards, not one. `Game.legal_target`'s own `protection_refusal` recheck (a separate, always-run check keyed off `Game._source_card_of(spell)`, not off the profile) still catches the ordinary case - a permanent with protection from artifacts is still refused as Wear's target - so this is a narrower gap than it sounds: it is CR 702.16b judged *twice*, at announcement and at resolution, and only the announcement-time copy inside the combined profile is blunted for a fused spell specifically. No printing in the pool combines fuse with a target-restricting keyword line (ward, hexproof-from, protection-granting riders) that this would visibly change. |

## Finding the gaps: `scripts/sweep_pool.py`

Two holes look identical from a passing test, and the script reports both:

```sh
uv run python scripts/sweep_pool.py --keywords   # keywords nothing acts on
uv run python scripts/sweep_pool.py --effects    # cards with text and no effect entry
uv run python scripts/sweep_pool.py --targeting  # targeting text the parser cannot read
uv run python scripts/sweep_pool.py --card "Grief"
```

**The support oracle: `magic_cards_model.support.card_support` (2026-09-23,
F6 W1).** The per-clause classifier this script used to own now lives in the
installed package, and the script only reports through it - one source of
truth. `card_support(card)` takes any `Card` built from a Scryfall printing
(never a name lookup) and returns a frozen `CardSupport`: `status` is the
worst clause's (`silent` < `unaudited` < `notice` < `handled`; the sweep's
`static_unaudited` is `unaudited`, and `unmatchable_condition`/
`quoted_effect` fold into `silent`), and `clauses` lists every spell face,
activated, triggered and static ability, and keyword with its own `outcome`
(the sweep's category), `status` and `reason`. `effect_outcome`/
`effect_detail` are exactly `classify_card`'s verdict. It is deterministic
and side-effect free - probes run on throwaway boards under a fresh uuid4 id
allocator, so a call inside a game's `_id_allocator_scope()` never shifts that
game's ids - and memoized per `ENGINE_VERSION` (package version plus
`Game.CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`), oracle id and printed data. The whole
printings pool classifies cold in about 1.5s (`tests/test_card_support.py`
asserts under 5s). A deck checker warning that a card "may not be fully
supported" reads this, never its own copy of the rules.

**The format filter (2026-09-23, T01).** `--keywords`, `--effects` and
`--targeting` filter `names` through `in_target_formats` before reporting -
`CLAUDE.md`'s own clamp to Modern, Pioneer and Standard, applied to the
measurement tool for the first time rather than only to `models/card.py`'s
`Legalities`. A printing is in scope the moment any one of the three
`Legality` is not `not_legal` - **banned counts as in scope**, since a banned
card was printed into that format's pool and can be unbanned, and a
not-yet-sanctioned pod running the format's card list can still play it; only
`not_legal` in all three (a Standard-only rotated-out card, a Commander-only
printing, an Alchemy digital-only card) drops it. `--all-formats` disables the
filter and reports on the whole pool; `--card NAME` always reports the named
card regardless, printing "outside Modern/Pioneer/Standard - not counted"
when the filter would have dropped it from the pool-wide reports. Every
filtered report's own footer states how many pool cards the rule excluded.
This is the owner rule the filter exists to serve: every card legal in one of
the three target formats must be **fully supported**, so `--effects` also
lists a legal card whose worst clause fails closed with a `NOTICE` in its own
"legal cards failing closed" section (`legal_cards_failing_closed`) - a
fail-closed notice is ordinarily correct, fail-*closed* behaviour, but for a
legal card it is a still-open gap, never a clean pass, and an out-of-format
card's own notice is not tracked there. See `MEMORY.md`'s 2026-09-23 T01 line
for the ability-word/flavor-word rules the same rewrite carries.

The targeting report exists to keep a number at zero: a phrase
`machines/targeting.py` cannot read comes back `understood=False` and CR 115
legality is then not checked at all, which looks exactly like a card that
targets nothing. Measured with `uv run python scripts/sweep_pool.py --targeting`
at this commit, it is **0 unreadable targeting phrases across 772 cards**. Do not
quote that count from here - re-run the script, because the pool grows. It was 6
before the target-predicate wave: Drown in
the Loch's graveyard-counted bound (three phrases, card-level and both modes),
Prismatic Ending's converge condition, and Mishra's Factory's hyphenated
Assembly-Worker creature type (two). Zero here is a moving target, not a
finished one - it goes back above zero the day a card with a phrase this parser
has not met enters the pool, which is exactly what happened when Prismatic
Ending did.

The keyword report is the one that used to be missing. A card can have its
keyword parsed, printed, and returned by `parse_abilities`, and still have
nothing anywhere that acts on it - which is how evoke sat in the pool on five
cards doing nothing while every card-level sweep called them fine. A keyword
counts as executed only if `machines/combat.py`, `machines/casting/`, or the
mana-ability path reads it; everything else is listed, with the cards carrying
it. Keep the two exception lists in the script honest, because anything on them
is a keyword the report will never mention again.

**What `--effects` actually measures, and the hole it had until 2026-09-08.**
The report sorts every clause into six buckets, not four: `handled`, `notice`,
`static_unaudited`, `silent` (see W15 below for what each of those four
means), plus **`unmatchable_condition`** and **`quoted_effect`**. Both are new,
and both close the same finding
(`docs/2026-09-08-trigger-findings.md`'s "sweeper's blind spot"): `--effects`
used to classify a triggered ability as `handled` the moment `ability.event`
parsed and `trigger_effect_for` returned a real callable - it never asked
`machines/triggers.condition_matches` (CR 603.2) whether that printed
*condition* could ever be satisfied by a real permanent, and it never asked
whether a text-fallback parser's answer came from the clause's own words or
from a *quoted* span meant for a different object entirely (a token's own
granted ability, most often). Weapons Manufacturing's "a nontoken artifact you
control enters" was the finding's original example, scoring `handled` on both
counts at the time: a substring guard in `condition_matches` inverted
"nontoken" into "must be a token", so no real nontoken artifact entering it
ever fired it, and the effect it "found" was `_DAMAGE_TARGET_RE` reading
"deals 2 damage to any target" out of the token's own quoted reminder text,
not Weapons Manufacturing's own clause. Both of Weapons Manufacturing's own
holes are since fixed on `main` (`30f2b07`, independently of this closure) -
its own condition now fires correctly and its own effect no longer misparses
- which is exactly what a closure built against the *production* functions is
supposed to do: track a fix with no code change of its own, rather than keep
reporting a bug that is gone. `tests/test_sweep_pool.py` pins this directly:
Weapons Manufacturing and Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm (the finding's second named
card) both now report their conditions reachable, and the pool's live
`unmatchable_condition` cards are two others sharing the same escaping shape
for a different, still-open reason (below).

`unmatchable_condition` is a triggered ability whose event parsed but whose
condition `_condition_can_fire` (`scripts/sweep_pool.py`) proved can never be
satisfied by any real, honestly-labelled permanent, tried under both
controllers, both token states, and every entry qualifier the condition names
- built and tested against the *production* `condition_matches`, never a
re-derivation of what the condition is supposed to mean. It is tracked
separately from `silent` on purpose: a trigger that never registers at all is
a different, more fundamental defect than one that registers and does
nothing, and folding the two together would hide exactly the distinction this
finding is about. `quoted_effect` is a clause whose dispatcher answer changes
from a real effect to `None` when its quoted span is blanked to a neutral,
non-empty placeholder (never removed outright - that would also misfire on
every legitimate "gains '\<ability\>'" grant, CR 113.10, that genuinely needs
its own quoted payload, Urza's Saga among them).

Measured at this commit: of 762 cards with rules text, 124 are `silent`, 434
`handled`, 31 `notice`, 171 `static_unaudited`, 2 `unmatchable_condition`
(Ygra, Eater of All and Blade of the Bloodchief, by an unrelated gap in
`condition_matches`'s `DIES` branch: a condition naming neither a
self-reference nor "another"/"other" never matches anything, which Ygra's "a
Food is put into a graveyard from the battlefield" and Blade's "a creature
dies" both hit - nobody is fixing this one yet), 0 `quoted_effect`. Ygra was
newly found by this closure (previously `handled`, fully invisible to every
prior sweep); Blade of the Bloodchief was already known broken but for a less
precise reason (previously `silent`). On `quoted_effect`: a real search - the
fixture pool plus over a dozen other real Scryfall printings sharing Weapons
Manufacturing's own "create a token / gains an ability with a quoted payload"
shape - found no live card reaching the misparse any more, and inspection of
the three other unanchored-prefix damage regexes still in `machines/effects/`
found they cannot cross a quote boundary at all (their `\.?$` suffix refuses
the trailing `"` a quoted grant's closing text always carries, unlike the
old, tail-permissive `_DAMAGE_TARGET_RE` this fix replaced) - there is
currently no live regex, not just no live card, this specific shape could
exploit. The detector itself (`_effect_matched_inside_quotes`) is still
exercised directly by `tests/test_sweep_pool.py`, against its own contract
rather than a card or regex that is no longer vulnerable.

**The "unread condition" bucket had the same class of measurement bug.**
`classify_clauses` used to stamp a triggered ability `silent` the instant its
own `ability.event` was `None`, never asking whether `machines/triggers/`
could still read the condition text - but `triggered_abilities_of` and
`_state_trigger_abilities` both already do, through `_unread_trigger_events`
(CR 603.1b's multi-condition abilities) and `_STATE_COUNTER_TRIGGER_RE` (CR
603.8). Re-scoring the 18 clauses this bucket held showed 10 across 9 cards
already reach the stack in a real game; four (Basking Broodscale, Emperor of
Bones, Hardened Academic, **Murktide Regent**) had no other silent clause and
left the `silent` list entirely once the sweeper asked the same two
questions the runtime does. `tests/test_sweep_pool.py` pins the sweeper's
readability against `triggered_abilities_of`'s own gate directly, over the
whole pool, so the two cannot drift apart again.

Do not quote these counts from here either - re-run the script.

## Card effects

`machines/effects/` is a scripted registry keyed by card name, not a rules
engine. There are three tables in it.

**`EFFECTS`, what a spell does.** Counterspell,
Swords to Plowshares, Twisted Image, Giant Growth, Dismember,
Unholy Heat, Mutagenic Growth, Assault Strobe, Violent Urge,
Malevolent Rumble, Monstrous Rage, Savor the Moment,
Preordain. Lightning Bolt no longer has a
row - see "Targeted single-object effects (wave 2)" below - and neither does
Lightning Helix any more: "deals 3 damage to any target and you gain 3 life"
mixes a targeted clause and a player clause, which `parse_mixed_effect_for_spell`
now reads clause by clause, trying the targeted parser and then the player
parser on each one (see "Mixed targeted/player effects" below). Spectral
Procession is gone too (W4): "Create three 1/1 white Spirit creature tokens
with flying" is one clause of `_parse_token_clause`'s shape - see "Token
creation (wave 4)" below. **W8 removes six more rows**: Electrolyze
("deals N damage divided as you choose among one or two targets", read by
`_DIVIDED_DAMAGE_RE`), Lava Dart and Violent Urge were tried too but Lava
Dart's flashback line still refuses the whole text (its row stays, see below)
while Violent Urge's own second-sentence *delirium* shape already reached
`create_continuous_effect` through `_is_layer_effect_text`, so its row was
dead weight the same way Preordain's used to be; Fog/Angelsong ("prevent all
combat damage that would be dealt this turn", `_PREVENT_ALL_COMBAT_DAMAGE_RE`),
Bandage ("prevent the next N damage that would be dealt to \<target> this
turn", `_PREVENT_NEXT_DAMAGE_TO_TARGET_RE`), and Awe Strike ("the next time
target creature would deal damage this turn, prevent that damage[, You gain
life equal to the damage prevented this way.]", read as one CR 608.2c
instruction by `_merge_prevent_damage_from_target_clauses`). Every other card
without a row either resolves and does nothing or is reached by one of the
effect parsers off its own printed text.

You may put a `<quality>` card from among them into your hand. Put the rest into your graveyard." template shared with Grisly Salvage and Satyr Wayfinder (`tests/scenarios/test_reveal_top_n_put_one_into_hand.py`). **`TRIGGER_EFFECTS`, what a triggered ability does**, keyed by
`(card name, TriggerEvent, marker)`. The third part is a lowercase fragment of
the trigger's own printed text, and it is what lets a card with two triggers on
one event have two entries: `trigger_effect_for` still takes `(name, event)`,
because `Game._effect_of` has only those, and returns a dispatcher that reads the
resolving ability's text when a card has more than one. An empty marker means
"every trigger this card has on this event", which is what most entries carry.

**Ability-side routing to `create_continuous_effect_of_ability` is text-driven
now, not a per-card row.** Basking Rootwalla's and Karn, the Great Creator's
`ACTIVATED_EFFECTS` rows existed only to route the ability there - the actual
pump/type-change/P-T-set was always `machines/layers/`'s
`parsed_layer_effects` reading the ability's own text - so
`machines/effects/continuous.py`'s `_is_layer_effect_text` (tried after the ordinary
clause parser fails) recognises the shape and reaches the same function with
no row, and `ACTIVATED_EFFECTS` is now empty. The same recognition reaches a
**triggered** ability of the same shape, which never had a row-based path at
all: Oliphaunt's "Whenever this creature attacks, another target creature you
control gets +2/+0 and gains trample until end of turn." used to fire and
resolve to nothing; it now actually pumps and grants trample, proven in
`scenarios/test_parsed_layer_effects.py` by a trampler dealing damage through
a blocker it could not have without both halves applying. Getting a
*triggered* ability's own effect text this far also exposed a shape
`parsed_layer_effects` had never had to read before: its trigger condition
("Whenever this creature attacks, ") shares the line with the effect and
`_effect_sentences` did not strip it the way it already stripped an
activated ability's cost - `_TRIGGER_CONDITION_PREFIX_RE` is the fix.
`Tower Above`'s "Until end of turn, target creature gets +4/+4 and gains
trample, wither, and \"...\"" is the spell-side twin of the same gap:
duration-first phrasing failed even the loose "does this look like our
territory" check (`_LOOKS_LIKE_LAYER_EFFECT_RE` anchored on the subject
coming first) and did nothing with no `LayerNotice`.
`_normalize_duration_first` reads the duration wherever it sits (CR 611.2a
states it "as stated by the spell or ability", not pinned to one end of the
sentence); Tower Above's granted keywords are still not one this wave reads
(a bare word list, not a quoted extra ability), so it now fails closed with a
notice instead of silently doing nothing. The anthem shape (CR 611.3) is
deliberately excluded from this routing decision
(`is_resolution_layer_effect_text`): a permanent spell whose only text is a
"Creatures you control get +N/+N." (Glorious Anthem) must not also create a
one-shot copy of its own static ability on cast, which is what a first,
too-eager version of this routing did - the anthem is CR 611.3's own
`effects_for` battlefield sweep and never a CR 611.2 resolution effect.

| Goblin Bombardment | `Sacrifice a creature:` | 1 damage to any target - no longer a table row, reached by the wave-2 targeted-effect parser. Whole ability - the sacrifice is a cost (CR 602.1a) and is paid before the ability is on the stack. |
| Ghost Quarter | `{T}, Sacrifice this land:` | Destroys the target land (CR 701.8a), then its **controller** searches for a basic land (a supertype, CR 205.4c) and puts it onto the battlefield, in printed order (CR 608.2c), then shuffles. Both questions - CR 701.23g's printed "may search" and CR 701.23b's "isn't required to find" - are put to the *victim*, not to the activator. Has no `ACTIVATED_EFFECTS` row (W3): `parse_mixed_effect` reads the destroy clause and the "its controller may search" clause together off the printed text - see `scenarios/test_search_as_a_clause.py`. |

An ability with no entry still triggers or activates, still goes on the stack,
can still be responded to, and is still removed by CR 608.2n. It simply has no
effect when it gets there.

This is the single biggest gap between the model and a real engine, and it is
deliberate: a general effect system needs targeting, triggers, and continuous
effects first. Until then, a scenario relying on a card's text must add that
card's effect to the registry.

## Targeted single-object effects (wave 2)

Wave 1 (above) taught the model untargeted player effects - gain life, draw,
mill, scry, surveil - off a card's own printed text, with no table row. Wave 2
does the same for the largest remaining block: a **single** targeted verb -
`Destroy target X.`, `Exile target X.`, `<Source> deals N damage to target X.`
(and "to any target"), `Return target X to its owner's hand.`,
`Tap`/`Untap target X.`, and `Put N +1/+1 (or -1/-1) counters on target X.`
Each is one clause naming exactly one target (CR 115.6's "up to" and "one or
two" are excluded on purpose). `parse_targeted_effect_for_spell` and
