an Empower Jace clause - they do not (verified against Scryfall and this
pool's own fixtures: neither printing's oracle text contains the word
"empower" anywhere). Their own clause this stream (S5) actually closed is
"whenever you activate a loyalty ability"/"an opponent activates a loyalty
ability" (`LOYALTY_ABILITY_ACTIVATED`, the table above), which is what put
their names in this stream's own pool additions in the first place.
No pre-existing card regressed. Registry rows (`EFFECTS`/`TRIGGER_EFFECTS`/
`ACTIVATED_EFFECTS`) stay at 7, unchanged - every fix in this section is a
parser or a matcher, never a name-keyed row.

## FRA S1: Empower Jace (CR 701.71)

Reality Fracture's own keyword action, and the Jace planeswalker token it
creates. 35 `set:fra` printings carry the word "empower" in their oracle text
(`cards/search?q=set%3Afra+oracle%3Aempower`, verified this session) - not 37
as this stream's own assignment first said, and not the 37-minus-Ajani-and-
Gideon reading either: see the correction just above this section, which this
stream's own investigation is what prompted.

**CR 701.71a**: "To empower Jace N means 'If you don't control a Jace
planeswalker token, create a blue Jace planeswalker token with 0 loyalty,
"[-1]: Surveil 1," and "[-3]: Draw a card." Choose a Jace planeswalker token
you control. Put N loyalty counters on it.'" Three CR 608.2c instructions,
read as a single keyword action embedded in other abilities' and spells'
effect text - the same shape earthbend/amass/airbend/investigate already are,
so `machines/keywords.executes("empower")` is told the word for the same
reason theirs are, even though no `fra` printing's own Scryfall `keywords`
list actually carries "Empower" (its reminder-text scan picks up "Surveil"
and "Behold" off the token's own quoted abilities and Countersculpt's own
cost instead - `empower` would only ever matter for a future printing that
is tagged).

**The token** - `models/token.JACE`, registered in `PREDEFINED["Jace"]`
alongside the S3 wave's own table. Built to match the real `tfra` printing
exactly rather than CR 111.4's generic fallback: `name="Jace"` (not "Jace
Token" - the creating text specifies the name the same way CR 111.9's Boo
does), not legendary (CR 306.4 retired the planeswalker uniqueness rule and
the real printing carries no Legendary supertype, so "if you don't control
one" alone is what keeps ordinary play from making a second), and
`loyalty="0"` - a new `TokenDefinition` field, threaded into `to_card()`,
that lets the existing `CardState.intrinsic_entering_counters` (CR 306.5b) do the
"enters with 0 loyalty" half with no code of its own, the same way every
printed planeswalker's own entry already works. Its two granted abilities are
printed with the real minus sign (`−`), matching the ordinary loyalty-cost
reader (`machines/abilities._LOYALTY_SYMBOL`) with no changes there either -
"Surveil 1." and "Draw a card." are both already-general effect shapes, so
the token's own loyalty abilities activate and resolve with no card-specific
code anywhere.

**The clause parser** - `machines/effects._parse_empower_jace_clause`/
`empower_jace`, registered once in the shared per-clause dispatcher
(`_parse_mixed_clause`, right after amass) so it is reachable from spell
text, a triggered ability's body, an activated ability's body, and a modal
spell's own chosen-mode text alike, with no rewrite of `_parse_mixed_clause`/
`parse_mixed_effect(_for_spell)` itself - S6 was mid-flight on those same
functions' fallback and mode-composition behaviour when this stream forked,
and the instruction was to stay a self-contained addition so the eventual
merge order does not matter. "Empower Jace N" and "Empower Jace X, where X is
`<expr>`" both read through `_fixed_or_where_x_amount`, the same CR 107.3f
reader earthbend and amass already share - "the number of Islands you
control" (Jace, Reality Sculptor's own `+1`), "the number of creatures you
control" (Repurposed Enforcer) and "the number of creatures exiled this way"
(Overwrite the Multiverse) all read correctly with no code of their own.

The choice of *which* Jace token ("choose a Jace planeswalker token you
control") is CR 608.2d, not a target (CR 601.2c's word is never printed): the
ordinary case is exactly one candidate and needs no question; the
`DecisionKind.CHOOSE_CARDS` question (the same kind `_knowledge_pool_free_
cast_effect` already asks for "choose one of several cards") is only asked
when a copy effect or similar has produced more than one, which nothing in
this stream's own scope does but a future one might.

**Overwrite the Multiverse's own X** - "the number of creatures exiled this
way" - needed a second, small addition: `_parse_exile_each_clause`/
`_exile_matching`, the exile-side twin of `_parse_destroy_each_clause`/
`_destroy_matching` (same qualifier grammar, `_parse_mass_destroy_predicate`,
reused verbatim), which records its count with `Game.record_count` so
`count_expression`'s already-general "`<verb>` this way" reader
(`_COUNT_THIS_WAY_RE`, `counted_this_way`) answers correctly for "Exile all
creatures." + "... where X is the number of creatures exiled this way."
without either sentence needing to know about the other.

**Violent Echoes' own X** - "that excess damage" - is CR 120.10: "Some
triggered abilities check whether a permanent has been dealt excess damage
... If [sources] dealt an amount of damage to a creature greater than lethal
damage, excess damage equal to the difference was dealt ... If [sources]
dealt an amount of damage to a planeswalker greater than that planeswalker's
loyalty before the damage was dealt, excess damage equal to the difference
was dealt ... the greatest of the calculated amounts for each of the card
types it has." Read as one whole-text parser,
`_parse_damage_then_empower_if_excess_clause` (the same "read the whole
two-sentence shape, ahead of `parse_mixed_effect_for_spell`'s per-clause
split" idiom `_DAMAGE_TARGET_KICKED_INSTEAD_RE` already uses for Burst
Lightning's kicker), since the second sentence refers back to how much the
first one actually dealt - no per-clause dispatcher can carry that on its
own. `_lethal_amount_before_damage` reads the target's remaining toughness or
loyalty *before* `Game.deal_damage` runs (the call itself is what marks
damage or removes loyalty counters), and excess is `deal_damage`'s own
returned amount minus that - CR 609.7b's prevention/replacement already
applied, not the printed N. Kept as its own named helper so a future card
checking "excess damage" for a different follow-up reuses the same CR 120.10
reading rather than a second copy of it.

**Two general bugs this stream's own proof cards found, both fixed at their
real cause rather than worked around:**

- `machines/abilities.self_normalized_effect_text` rewrote *any* whole-word
  match of a card's own short name to "this permanent" (CR 201.5), with no
  exception for a fixed keyword-action phrase that happens to share the word:
  Jace, Reality Sculptor's own `+1: Empower Jace X, where X is the number of
  Islands you control.` was silently corrupted to `+1: Empower this permanent
  X, ...` before `_parse_empower_jace_clause` ever saw it, because the
  source's own short name is "Jace" and CR 701.71a's keyword phrase also
  always says "Jace" - coincidentally, and never as a self-reference. Fixed
  with a lookbehind (`_EMPOWER_KEYWORD_LOOKBEHIND`) that exempts "Jace"
  immediately after "empower ", not a Jace-specific special case - a future
  "empower `<name>`" keyword sharing a different planeswalker's own short
  name would hit the identical collision and reads correctly the same way.
  Proven by `test_jace_reality_sculptor_plus_one_empowers_x_islands_and_the_
  token_works`, which also activates the created token's own `-3: Draw a
  card.` to prove the token's granted abilities work at all.
- **Fixed, on coordinator review** (originally left as a documented,
  out-of-scope gap - see the correction below): `Game.why_cannot_activate`
  checked "on the battlefield" unconditionally after its own CR 113.6j/113.6m
  zone-rule branch, rather than only when that branch found no zone rule at
  all - so *no* ability CR 113.6j ever legitimately moves off the battlefield
  (Campus Crier's own "{1}, Exile this card from your graveyard: Empower Jace
  2.", the same shape Seasoned Pyromancer's own graveyard ability and
  Boseiju's Channel are) could ever actually be activated, even once
  `machines/abilities._activated_ability_zone` correctly read its zone. Now
  `elif`, not two independent `if`s: once `ability.zone` names a zone, CR
  113.6's flat "usually only on the battlefield" default has already been
  displaced by the sub-rule that put the ability somewhere else, so a
  permanent correctly sitting in that zone no longer also fails the flat rule
  a moment later. `Game.begin_activating` had the same battlefield
  assumption one call downstream: its `ManaSpend.activating(self.
  characteristics_of(permanent))` call raised `NotOnBoard`, because `Game.
  computed_board` only ever covers the battlefield (CR 613.1's layers apply
  to permanents) - fixed by passing the permanent itself (already a
  `HasCharacteristics`, reading its own printed face) when it is not on the
  battlefield, the same split `ManaSpend.casting` already draws for a spell
  on the stack. `test_self_referential_costs.py`'s own Seasoned Pyromancer
  and Boseiju tests, and `test_empower_jace.py`'s own Campus Crier test, now
  go through `Scenario.activate`/`Game.activate_ability` for real rather than
  building and paying the `TotalCost` by hand. Full suite re-verified green
  afterward, `test_off_battlefield_activation.py`, `judge/test_judge_ability_
  zones.py`, `test_cycling.py`, `test_unearth.py` and `test_suspend_
  sacrifice_activation.py` included - none of those go through this same
  gate (`machines/keywords.off_battlefield_activation`/`off_zone_activation`
  is its own, separate door that never called `why_cannot_activate`), so
  fixing the gate they had already worked around could not regress them, and
  did not.
- `machines/abilities._activated_ability_zone` gained one more CR 113.6j
  shape alongside `_DISCARDS_ITSELF`: `_EXILES_ITSELF_FROM_ZONE`, "exile this
  card from your `<zone>`" read the same general way, off the words alone -
  Campus Crier's `ActivatedAbility.zone` now correctly reads `graveyard`, and
  (with the fix just above) actually activates through the ordinary door.

**Cards (35), classified with `scripts/survey_cards.py --file ... --json`
after this stream's own changes, `classify_clauses`-level detail where the
top-level bucket does not already say so:** 20 `handled` outright (Academic
Ascent, Arcane Amphisbaena, Campus Crier, Countersculpt, Fatehold Charm,
Hexhaven Battalion, Inspired Tethermage, Keeper of the Quiet Hour, Mindseeker
Oculus, No Admittance, Overwrite the Multiverse, Protege's Awakening,
Repurposed Enforcer, Rewrite Regrets, Tam's Resistance, Violent Echoes,
Vraska's Final Mercy, Way of the Mentor, Way of the Mind Sculptor, Way of the
Necromancer); 9 `static_unaudited` because a sibling "Planeswalkers you
control have '...'" grant (S4's own scope) sits on the same card, empower
clause itself independently confirmed `handled` by `classify_clauses` for
every one (Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes, Sanctum Lurker, Theorist's Sanctum,
Way of the Cryomancer/Deathbringer/Healer/Pyromancer/Warlord/Wildspeaker); 6
`silent` at the card level only because a *different* clause on the same card
has no reader yet (S4's loyalty-ability-permission/life-gain grants on Jace's
Machinations and Way of the Paradox, S10's own "the next spell you cast this
turn can't be countered" on Theorist's Proxy, S7/S8's reveal-hand-choose-
discard on Solve for Disappointment and the ETB permanent-bounce on Plan for
All Outcomes, and Jace, Reality Sculptor's own other two loyalty abilities) -
`classify_clauses` independently confirms this
stream's own empower clause `handled` on every one of the six once each
card's text is read clause-by-clause rather than by its single worst bucket.
Every one of these six will read fully once the sibling clause lands; nothing
about that landing touches this stream's own parser, by construction (shared
dispatcher, no ordering dependency).

**Sweep, this stream:** `scripts/sweep_pool.py --effects` stays at 129 silent
of 1039 (baseline: 129 of 1028 - the 11-card growth is this stream's own
`scripts/add_card.py` proof cards, none of them left silent) and registry
rows stay at 7 (`EFFECTS` 1, `TRIGGER_EFFECTS` 6, `ACTIVATED_EFFECTS` 0,
unchanged) - every fix in this section is a parser, a table row keyed on
"Jace"/predicate text, or a general zone/self-reference reader, never a
card-name-keyed row.

Scenario tests: `tests/scenarios/test_empower_jace.py` - 13 tests covering a
spell's second sentence composed with an existing pump clause, a creature's
own ETB trigger, reuse of an already-created token rather than a second one,
an attack trigger's own X ("creatures you control"), a loyalty ability's own
X ("Islands you control", plus the token's own granted ability actually
activating), a modal spell's own chosen mode, the new exile-each clause's X
("creatures exiled this way"), CR 120.10's excess damage on both a creature
and a planeswalker (plus the "exactly lethal is not excess" negative case),
and CR 608.2d's choice among two pre-existing tokens.

## FRA S4: the planeswalker and loyalty subsystem

Every "loyalty counters", "planeswalker" and "you may activate loyalty
abilities" mechanic this set's own Jaces, Tomik, Sorin, Garruk, Sanctum
Lurker and the six "Way of the `<name>`" enchantments needed, built as
general parsers and one new group-grant selector rather than card-name rows.
Registry rows unchanged from the FRA S1 baseline this stream inherited
(`EFFECTS` 1, `TRIGGER_EFFECTS` 6, `ACTIVATED_EFFECTS` 0).

**"Planeswalkers you control have "`<ability>`"." group ability grants**
(CR 611.3, CR 613.1f, CR 113.10a) - `machines/layers/`'s `_GROUP_QUOTED_
ABILITY_GRANT_RE`/`_group_quoted_ability_grant_builder`, over the identical
`permanents_controlled_by(source.controller, Type.PLANESWALKER)` selector
every other "`<card type>`s you control" static already reads with - a
planeswalker is CR 300.1's own card type, not a new kind of subject.
Registered a second time in `quoted_ability_grants` (the function `sync_
granted_ability_texts` reads every battlefield sweep) so the granted line
is not merely present on the computed board but actually reaches
`CardState.granted_ability_texts` and is genuinely activatable through the
ordinary door - the same two-registration split `_ATTACHED_CREATURE_
STATIC_RE`'s own Equipment-quoted-ability shape already needs. Proven on
seven differently-shaped granted bodies: Tomik, Orzhov Lawmage's attack
restriction (below), Sanctum Lurker's damage-and-lifegain `[+2]`, Avatar of
Burgeoning Echoes' per-land `+1/+1` counter `[-10]`, and the six Way of the
`<name>` enchantments' own grants - a spell-copy, a sacrifice-for-token, a
token-plus-surveil, a plain mana ability, a two-target damage split, and a
bare token creation - none of which needed a parser of its own beyond what
already existed for the identical clause shape printed directly on a card.

**A general splitting bug this stream's own multi-sentence grants exposed**,
fixed at its real cause: `machines/abilities.py`'s `_layer_readable_
sentences_uncached` (feeding `machines/layers._effect_sentences`, which
`parsed_layer_effects` reads) split a static ability's own body on every
`". "` boundary with no notion of a quoted span - so Way of the
Deathbringer's own "Planeswalkers you control have '[-2]: You may
sacrifice a creature. If you do, create a 4/4 green Beast creature token
with trample.'" was cut in half at the period inside the quote, and
`parsed_layer_effects` read two unreadable fragments instead of the one
whole grant. Fixed with `_split_top_level_sentences`, a quote-depth toggle
that only treats a period as a sentence boundary outside an open `"`. The
identical bug, in a second, independent splitter, made a token's own quoted
CDA ability unreadable whenever it followed a keyword list -
`machines/effects/`'s `_parse_whole_text_token_clause` refused *any* period
outside a single trailing one, which caught Wrenn and Seven's own `-3`
("Create a green Treefolk creature token with reach and 'This token's power
and toughness are each equal to the number of lands you control.'" - the
period inside the quote) even before this stream ever touched a Way of the
`<name>` card. Fixed the same way, with its own `_has_period_outside_
quotes` (kept local to `machines/effects/` rather than shared, since the two
splitters' own surrounding logic differs too much to unify safely under
this stream's own time budget).

**A second general bug in the same territory, found writing scenario tests
for the grant mechanism**: CR 107.7's loyalty symbol is bracketed - `[+N]`,
`[0]`, `[-N]` - and every one of this pool's *quoted* granted loyalty
lines is templated with the brackets (Sanctum Lurker's own oracle text
reads `"[+2]: This planeswalker deals ..."`), while a planeswalker's own
*printed* card never carries them (Jace, Reality Sculptor's `+1:`, `−3:`,
`0:` have none). `machines/abilities._LOYALTY_SYMBOL` - the regex
`_classify_cost` matches a cost piece against to recognise a loyalty
ability at all (CR 606.2) - was only ever written for the bracket-free
shape, so every quoted grant's own cost classified as `CostKind.OTHER` and
`Game.activation_cost` refused it outright the moment anyone actually tried
to activate it (`ValueError: cannot build a cost for '[+2]'`) - reproduced
for Sanctum Lurker, Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes, and all six Way-of cards.
The grant mechanism above was never broken; every one of these abilities
was correctly granted and correctly *listed* - only activating one raised.
Fixed by making the brackets optional in `_LOYALTY_SYMBOL` itself (both
capture groups unchanged, so the one existing consumer, `_loyalty_symbol`,
needed no change of its own).

**A third general bug the same pass found**: Way of the Warlord's own
granted `[-4]` ("This planeswalker deals 2 damage to up to one target
creature or planeswalker **and** 2 damage to target player.") - CR 608.2c's
one instruction, cut in half by `_CLAUSE_SEPARATOR`'s bare "and" split, left
the second half ("2 damage to target player") with no subject or verb of
its own, and nothing recombined the pair. `_merge_split_damage_clauses`
(`machines/effects/`) reunites this shape - CR 601.2c already keeps the
two target requirements separate at announcement, so resolution only needs
"how much" for each. Proven off-set on Lunge's identically-shaped "Lunge
deals 2 damage to target creature and 2 damage to target player or
planeswalker."

**The unequal-amount half of that same shape, closed on `fra-s4`**:
`_merge_split_damage_clauses` originally refused a pair whose two halves
printed *different* amounts (`<n> != <m>`), since nothing recorded which
resolved target belonged to which of the two requirements once
`Game.resolve_targets` flattened them together. `AbilityOnStack.target_
amounts`/`CardState.target_amounts` now record one amount per entry of
`targets`, classified against each requirement's own restriction
(`TargetRequirement.rejects`, read back through `profile_for_text` on each
half's own phrase) rather than assumed by position, so the pairing is
correct whichever order the targets were announced or stored in. Proven
off-set on Hungry Flames ("Hungry Flames deals 3 damage to target creature
and 2 damage to target player or planeswalker.") - a real Scryfall printing
outside this stream's own deck pool, with two independently-typed mandatory
requirements so the unequal amounts are the only thing under test
(`tests/scenarios/test_split_damage_targets.py`).

**CR 704.5i's 0-loyalty state-based action, exempted per controller** -
Sanctum Lurker's own "Planeswalkers you control aren't put into their
owners' graveyards for having 0 loyalty." `Game._zero_loyalty_exemption_
controllers` (`_ZERO_LOYALTY_EXEMPTION_RE`, read off `class_ability_text`
directly - a controller-scoped exemption from a state-based action, not a
grantable quoted ability, so it does not go through the group-grant
mechanism above) filters `Game._state_based_action_losers`'s own CR 704.5i
sweep. Reads printed text directly rather than the computed board, the
same posture `attacker_cap_restriction` below takes and for the identical
reason: CR 101.2's "the card overrides the rule" needs the card to still
carry the ability, and nothing in the pool grants this one to a second
source to make the computed-board distinction matter yet.

**"No more than one creature can attack this planeswalker each combat."**
(CR 508.1c) - `machines/combat.attacker_cap_restriction`, read off a
defender's own computed ability text the same self-referential way
`_evasion_restriction_sentences` already reads "can't be blocked" ("this
planeswalker"/"this battle", or the card's own short name for a
self-printed line). Enforced once per whole attack declaration, not once
per attacker, by `Game._refuse_illegal_attacker_caps` (called from `Game.
declare_attackers` alongside the existing CR 508.1d requirement check) -
grouping the declared attacks by defender and refusing the whole
declaration the moment two or more land on the same capped defender.
Proven on Tomik, Orzhov Lawmage's own grant and, off-set, on The Eternal
Wanderer's identically-shaped *self-printed* line ("No more than one
creature can attack The Eternal Wanderer each combat.") - the same reader,
two different sources for the sentence.

**"Up to one target creature gets `<P>`/`<T>` until your next turn."**
(CR 611.2a) - `machines/layers/parse.py`'s `_PUMP_RE` now reads `until end of
turn`/`until your next turn` as alternatives (was a fixed literal), and its
`_SUBJECT` fragment now admits an optional "up to one " prefix (CR 115.6a -
was `_PLURAL_TARGET_SUBJECT`'s own "up to N target creature**s**" shape
only, never the singular). `_pump_and_keyword_builder` takes `until_next_
turn: bool`, setting `Duration.UNTIL_YOUR_NEXT_TURN`/`until_next_turn_of`
in place of the ordinary end-of-turn duration. Proven on Garruk, Veiled
Butcher's own `+2` and, off-set, Liliana, the Last Hope's `+1` (identical
sentence shape, different numbers).

**"Until your next turn, whenever a creature attacks you or a planeswalker
you control, it gets `<P>`/`<T>` until end of turn."** - a delayed
triggered ability (CR 603.7) with two independent durations at once: the
watch itself lasts until the creating ability's controller's own next turn
(`DelayedTrigger.expires_end_of_next_turn`, CR 603.7b's stated-duration
twin of `Duration.UNTIL_YOUR_NEXT_TURN` (CR 611.2a), dropped by the new `DelayedTriggers.
expire_end_of_next_turn_for`, called from `Game.begin_turn_for` alongside
the continuous-effect and play-permission stores that already end there),
firing on every matching attack until then (`remaining=None`); each pump it
grants, once fired, lasts only until that turn's own ordinary cleanup
(`PumpEventSubject`, a new `DelayedEffectSpec` that reads which creature the
firing `ATTACKS` event was actually about off `AbilityOnStack.event`, since
this trigger names no object at creation time the way `TapSubject`'s own
fixed `subject_id` does). The compound defender ("you" the player, or a
planeswalker you control) is `DelayedTrigger.defending_controller_only`,
checked against the new `GameEvent.defender_controller` field - resolved
once, at attack declaration (`Game._emit_attacks`), because `DelayedTrigger.
matches` has no `Game` to ask "who controls this id" of. Parser: `_parse_
until_your_next_turn_attack_pump_clause`, tried ahead of the ordinary
per-clause dispatcher in `_ability_effect_or_notice` (the identical "read
the compound sentence whole" treatment `parse_casting_rule_clause`'s own
call already gets there). Proven on Jace, Reality Sculptor's own `-3` and,
off-set, Tamiyo Meets the Story Circle's chapter I (the identical sentence
on a Saga chapter trigger rather than a loyalty ability - proof this is
CR 603.7's general delayed-trigger mechanism, not something tied to a
planeswalker's own cost).

**A real target-legality bug this stream's own -X reanimation exposed**:
`Game.legal_target`'s own CR 608.2b re-check substituted a loyalty
ability's announced X back into its printed text only when the printed
*cost* literally contained the mana symbol `{X}` - never true of a loyalty
cost, whose own X is spelled `"−X"`/`"+X"` with no braces at all. So
`resolve_targets` re-checked every variable-loyalty-cost ability's own
target against the *literal, unsubstituted* "X" ("target creature card
with mana value X"), which - as the surrounding comment already said, for
the wrong reason - matches nothing, and silently dropped every legal
target. Sorin, Vengeful Bloodlord's own "−X: Return target creature
card with mana value X from your graveyard to the battlefield." was the
symptom: the ability resolved, paid its loyalty, and reanimated nothing.
Fixed by reading the identical `cost_announces_x(ability.cost)` helper
`Game._effect_of`'s own resolution-side dispatch already uses for the same
reason, rather than the narrower literal check. Sorin's own second sentence,
"That creature is a Vampire in addition to its other types.", is a plain
anaphoric rider (`_RIDER_BECOMES_TYPE_IN_ADDITION_RE`, in `_parse_referent_
object_clause`) - CR 205.1b's "in addition to its other types" as a one-shot
layer-4 `add_subtype` grant on whatever the antecedent's own reanimation
actually returned, the identical shape `_amass`'s own name-becomes-subtype
line already reads.

**"Twenty-five or more loyalty counters among `<name>`s you control"** -
Jace, Reality Sculptor's own `0` activation restriction. `_CONDITION_
LOYALTY_AMONG_NAMED` (`models/game/`), summing `CardState.loyalty`
(CR 306.5c) across every battlefield permanent sharing the named printed
name, read by the existing `Game.condition_holds`/`_activation_condition_
holds` CR 602.5b machinery with no new call site. Needed a real numbers.py
gap fixed first: no compound number word above the tens existed at all
("twenty-five" parsed to `None`), so `count_pattern`/`parse_count` gained
`_parse_compound_tens` (tens-plus-ones, hyphen or bare space) - a general
fix, not scoped to loyalty counts, since every parser in the codebase reads
counts through this one module.

**"Exile all but the bottom card of `<each opponent's|target player's>`
library."** - the other half of Jace's own `0`. `_parse_exile_all_but_
bottom_of_library_clause` (`_EXILE_ALL_BUT_BOTTOM_OF_LIBRARY_RE`), reading
both the unscoped group subject ("each opponent's") and CR 115.1's ordinary
player target ("target player's") as one shape, moved through `Game.
exile_cards` as a single CR 603.2c batch. Proven on Jace's own group form
and, off-set, on Nicol Bolas, the Arisen's identically-worded but *targeted*
`-12` - the same effect clause, a different subject shape entirely.

**"Each opponent discards `<n>` cards. For each opponent who didn't discard
`<n>` nonland cards this way, `<consequence>`."** - Garruk, Veiled Butcher's
own `-3` ("... you draw a card.") and, sharing the identical antecedent
(`_each_opponent_discards_and_count_shortfalls`, the new shared helper both
read), Kroxa, Titan of Death's Hunger's own enters-or-attacks trigger
("... loses 3 life.", off-set, joined with "then" rather than a new
sentence, and landing its consequence on each shortfall *opponent*
themselves rather than the controller) - two wrappers
(`_parse_each_opponent_discards_then_draw_per_shortfall_whole_text`,
`_parse_each_opponent_discards_then_shortfall_loses_life_whole_text`) over
one antecedent, since only the consequence and its subject differ between
real printings, never the discard-and-count half.

**"Each `<player|opponent>` sacrifices `<n>` `<description>` of their
choice. If you sacrificed `<description>` this way, `<consequence>`."** -
Garruk, Veiled Butcher's own `-2` ("... create a 4/4 green Beast creature
token with trample.") and, off-set, Rise of the Witch-king's identical
antecedent with a different consequence ("... you may return another
permanent card from your graveyard to the battlefield."). `_parse_each_
sacrifices_then_conditional_whole_text` (`_EACH_SACRIFICES_THEN_
CONDITIONAL_RE`) reuses `_EACH_SACRIFICES_OF_THEIR_CHOICE_RE`'s own
sacrifice machinery for the antecedent and tracks only whether the
resolving ability's own controller personally sacrificed a matching
permanent - CR 608.2c's "this way" ties the rider to the antecedent's own
outcome, and with several players sacrificing, only the controller's own
share of it is what "you" ever means here. Rise of the Witch-king's own
consequence needed one more small, general fix: `_RETURN_CARDS_FROM_YOUR_
GRAVEYARD_RE` (the no-target, choose-based reanimation shape) now reads an
optional leading "you may" as a real CR 608.2d choice and "another" as
`{COUNT}`'s own missing synonym for one (CR 400.7's "an other" object, not
a `numbers.parse_count` quantity word).

**"[Until end of turn, ]you may activate loyalty abilities of `<subject>`
on any player's turn any time you could cast an instant."** (CR 606.3's own
timing, loosened) - a new `LoyaltyInstantSpeedPermission` record
(`models/game/_activation.py`), checked first in `Game.why_cannot_activate`'s CR 606.3
branch (`Game._loyalty_instant_speed_permitted`) ahead of the ordinary
`can_cast_sorcery` refusal - never touching CR 606.3's *other* half, the
once-per-turn-per-permanent rule, which stays enforced regardless. Three
real subject shapes share one reader (`_parse_loyalty_instant_speed_
clause`, `_LOYALTY_INSTANT_SPEED_RE`): a bare "planeswalkers you control"
(unscoped), a "`<Subtype>` planeswalkers you control" (subtype-filtered -
Jace's Machinations' own "... loyalty abilities of Jace planeswalkers you
control ... Until end of turn ...", a temporary, resolved grant), and a
proper name (self-referential to the granting source's own short name -
Teferi, Master of Time's off-set "... loyalty abilities of Teferi ...",
which is not a resolving grant at all but a *permanent static ability*, so
`_loyalty_instant_speed_permitted` also reads a source's own printed text
directly for the identical sentence, the same "static ability, no
resolution record" posture `attacker_cap_restriction` and the 0-loyalty
exemption above both already take, and `Game.emblems_of` alongside
`permanents_controlled_by` for the source list - CR 114.2's emblem
"applies as though it were printed on a permanent", so the identical
sentence read off a command-zone emblem is the same read, not a separate
mechanism). Proven off-set on Teferi's Talent's/Teferi, Temporal Archmage's
own emblem text ("You get an emblem with '... loyalty abilities of
planeswalkers you control ...'"), minted directly through `Game.
create_emblem` and checked the same way.

**"Whenever you activate a loyalty ability, you gain 1 life. You may play
an additional land this turn."** - Way of the Paradox's own granted
trigger. The life-gain half needed nothing new (a plain "you gain N life"
player clause, and CR 606's own "activate a loyalty ability" trigger event
S5 already built); the land half is new: `Game.extra_land_plays`/`Game.
grant_extra_land_play`, a resolving-instruction twin of `machines.layers.
additional_land_plays`'s existing *static*-ability reader, summed together
in `Game.land_allowance`, reset with `lands_played` at the start of each
turn. `_ADDITIONAL_LAND_PLAY_RE` reads with or without a leading "you may"
and is checked ahead of `_parse_optional_player_clause`'s own generic
"you may" strip, since the grant itself is unconditional CR 305.2 - the
printed "may" belongs to the ordinary land play it makes legal, never to a
CR 608.2d choice about accepting the grant.

**Proliferate (CR 701.34a)**, entirely new - the keyword action did not
exist anywhere in the engine before this stream, and both of its halves
are modelled. `Game.proliferate(chosen, chosen_players)` adds one more
counter of each kind a chosen permanent or player already has;
`_parse_proliferate_clause` (`_PROLIFERATE_RE`) reads the bare keyword and
CR 107.3f's own "`<n>` times[, where X is `<expr>`]" repeat count through
the same `_fixed_or_where_x_amount` reader Empower Jace's own "N, where X
is ..." shape already uses, asking a fresh `CHOOSE_CARDS` question over
every countered permanent and a fresh `CHOOSE_PLAYERS` question over every
countered player before each repetition (`exact=False`, "any number", CR
608.2d, each skipped outright when its own candidate list is empty) - a
counter a repetition just added can make a permanent or player newly
eligible for the next one. The player half needed a new `DecisionKind.
CHOOSE_PLAYERS` (`Decision.players`, a tuple of usernames - `Decision.
cards`' own twin, since a player has no `UUID`) and a matching `Answer.
usernames` field for the pause/replay tape, both wired into `Game.ask`'s
validation and `decisions.default_answer` the same way `CHOOSE_CARDS`
already is. Proliferate reads as one CR 608.2c instruction even though it
is now two separate `Game.ask` questions: nothing about the *result* - who
ends up with what extra counters - depends on which order the two
questions were asked in. Proven off-set on Fuel for the Cause's own bare
"Counter target spell, then proliferate.", staging a real poisoned and
experienced opponent directly (`Game.add_player_counters`) the same way
the permanent half stages a real countered permanent.

Tam, the Possibility's own "Proliferate X times, where X is the number of
planeswalker types among planeswalkers you control." needed two more
fixes, both found writing this stream's own scenario tests. First,
`count_expression` had no reader for "the number of planeswalker types
among planeswalkers you control" at all - `_COUNT_PLANESWALKER_TYPES_RE`
counts distinct subtypes among the controller's own `Type.PLANESWALKER`
permanents, needing no closed word list the way `BASIC_LAND_TYPES` does:
CR 205.3j's own planeswalker types (verified whole this session,
`mise run rules:find 205.3j`) are exactly whatever subtypes a planeswalker
permanent carries, nothing narrower. Second, `_parse_proliferate_clause`'s
own `effect()` silently fell back to `times = 1` whenever the "N times"
tail printed an X this wave could not read, rather than failing the whole
clause closed at parse time the way every sibling CR 701 keyword-action
reader in this file already does (`_parse_damage_each_group_clause` among
them) - so an unreadable X would have quietly proliferated once instead of
recording that it went unread. Fixed by moving the `_fixed_or_where_x_
amount` check to parse time and returning `None` for the whole clause on a
miss.

**Sweep, this stream:** `scripts/sweep_pool.py --effects` - 134 of 1250
silent (up from the 129-of-1039 baseline the FRA S1 section above already
reports; the growth is this stream's own proof cards, none of them left
silent, against a larger card count from every merged stream's own
`scripts/add_card.py` fixtures). Registry rows unchanged (`EFFECTS` 1,
`TRIGGER_EFFECTS` 6, `ACTIVATED_EFFECTS` 0) - every fix above is a parser,
a selector, or a general condition/duration/count reader, never a
card-name-keyed row.

**FRA S4 merged into `int-engine-dsl` (this note).** Merging fra-s4's own
proof-card fixtures (`scripts/add_card.py`) into a pool `fra-s10b` had
already grown raised silent from 130-of-1233 to 133-of-1255 - six real
clauses across six cards nothing in either branch had closed yet, found by
diffing the sweep's own card list across the merge rather than assumed
harmless. Four were closed test-first as part of landing this merge:

- **"Each opponent discards N cards." with no shortfall consequence**
  (Nicol Bolas, the Ravager's own enters trigger) - the existing shortfall
  antecedent (`_EACH_OPPONENT_DISCARDS_THEN_DRAW_PER_SHORTFALL_RE` and its
  "loses life" twin) only ever matched a *two*-sentence instruction naming
  a shortfall; a bare instruction with nothing after the period fell
  through both. `_parse_each_opponent_discards_clause` reads the bare
  shape directly (`tests/scenarios/test_each_opponent_discards_plain.py`).
- **A compound "nonland permanent card" quality** (Solve for
  Disappointment's own "you choose a nonland permanent card from it") -
  `_nonland_or_typed_card_matcher` only ever read a bare type or that
  type's negation, never CR 110.4a's "permanent" noun grouping six types
  at once with an optional negated type in front of it. Fixed generally: a
  quality ending in " permanent" now composes CR 110.4a's own permanent-
  card-type set with whatever negation (if any) precedes it, so any future
  "non`<type>` permanent card" phrasing reads for free
  (`tests/scenarios/test_reveal_hand_and_choose.py`).
- **"The owner of `<target>` puts it on their choice of the top or bottom
  of their library"** as one sentence over a targeted *permanent* (Plan for
  All Outcomes' own enters trigger) - `_OWNER_PUTS_ON_TOP_OR_BOTTOM_RE`
  only ever matched Subtlety's own two-clause shape ("choose ...spell." /
  "Its owner puts it..." naming a spell on the stack).
  `_parse_owner_of_target_puts_on_top_or_bottom_clause` is the single-
  sentence, permanent-targeting sibling, same CR 108.3 owner/controller
  split (`tests/scenarios/test_owner_puts_permanent_on_top_or_bottom.py`).
- **"For each player, choose a creature that player controls. Each player
  sacrifices all creatures they control not chosen this way."** (The
  Eternal Wanderer's own `-4`) - a wholly new shape, every player's own
  CR 608.2d protective choice made in CR 101.4 APNAP order before either
  player's own sacrifice sweep runs
  (`tests/scenarios/test_each_player_chooses_creature_then_sacrifices_rest.py`).

**Two clauses from that same six-card list were left open here, documented
rather than hardcoded around:**

- **Teferi, Master of Time's own `-3`, "Target creature you don't control
  phases out."** and `-10`, "Take two extra turns after this one." - both
  closed by S31 (see its own section below): phasing is a subsystem now,
  and the extra-turn clause reads any count.
- **Tamiyo Meets the Story Circle's own chapter II, "Discard any number of
  cards, then investigate twice for each card discarded this way."** and
  **chapter III, "Shuffle up to three target cards from your graveyard
  into your library."** Neither a "discard any number, then investigate a
  count scaled by how many were discarded" reader nor a "shuffle a chosen
  subset of target graveyard cards into a library" reader exists yet.

Sweep after the four closed clauses: 128 of 1255 silent (comfortably under
the 130 ceiling the reviewing coordinator set), 0 unmatchable trigger
conditions, registry rows unchanged (`EFFECTS` 1, `TRIGGER_EFFECTS` 6,
`ACTIVATED_EFFECTS` 0).

## Ability-word clauses: block cap, -N/-M pump, quoted-grant-to-targets

Flow 2's own ability-word task (T15): every reported gap under Descend,
Inspired, and Strive, plus off-pool proofs for Enrage, Morbid, Repartee, and
Survival that the clause *under* each ability word actually runs, not only
that the trigger fires.

**CR 509.1b's "can't be blocked by more than one creature"** - the mirror of
menace (CR 702.111b), and just as much a whole-declaration fact as menace
is, not a per-(blocker, attacker) one: `machines/combat.py`'s
`blocked_by_at_most_one_refusal`, called from `declaration_refusal` beside
the existing menace check. Two shapes are read: the printed, unconditional
sentence (Charging Rhino, `_blocked_by_at_most_one_sentences`, the same
self-referential-subject reading `_evasion_restriction_sentences` already
does for plain "can't be blocked") and `BLOCKED_BY_AT_MOST_ONE_GRANT_TEXT`,
a fixed literal checked directly with `has_ability` the way `ATTACK_
WITHOUT_DEFENDER_TEXT` already is - a bare granted fragment with no subject
and no trailing full stop is not a `layer_readable_sentences` sentence at
all, so the sentence-search path would never see it. Akawalli, the Seething
Tower's own Descend 8 ("... gets an additional +2/+2 and can't be blocked
by more than one creature.") is the conditional case: `machines/layers/`'s
`_DESCEND_GATED_SELF_STATIC_LEADING_RE`/`_TRAILING_RE` now accept an
optional "an additional" ahead of the pump delta, and the trailing
non-keyword clause is granted verbatim by the existing `_split_gated_grants`
"not `has ...`" branch - no new machinery there, only the regex widening.
Tested in `scenarios/test_blocked_by_at_most_one.py` and (the pump/gating
half) `scenarios/test_descend_ability_word.py`.

**A general "`<target>` gets -N/-M" reader** - `machines/layers/`'s
`_SUBJECT` (and therefore `_PUMP_RE`) only ever read a "you control"
controller clause after a target's noun; Deepwater Hypnotist's own Inspired
clause, "target creature an opponent controls gets -3/-0 until end of
turn.", needed the second possessive too. `_CONTROLLER_CLAUSE` now covers
both. The negative delta itself needed no new code - `COUNT` already
includes zero and every digit, so "-3/-0" was always inside `_PUMP_RE`'s
own grammar once the controller clause matched. Burrog Befuddler's ETB
("target creature an opponent controls gets -1/-0 until end of turn.") is
the off-pool, non-Inspired proof that the reader is general across any
trigger; Pain Seer's own Inspired clause is a *third*, unrelated effect
("reveal the top card of your library and put that card into your hand.
You lose life equal to that card's mana value.") - the Dark Confidant
template, previously entirely unbuilt (no reader anywhere read "reveal the
top card ... put that card into your hand" as its own clause) - closed with
a three-clause merge, `_merge_reveal_top_hand_lose_life_equal_to_mana_value_
clauses`, the "that card" (CR 608.2c) anaphora resolved off the live
`CardState` the reveal touched rather than a second lookup. Tested in
`scenarios/test_inspired.py`.

**"`<any number of|up to N|N>` target creatures [you control] each gain
"`<quoted ability>`"" until end of turn"** (CR 611.2a's duration on CR
113.10a's ability-adding grant, aimed at resolved *targets* rather than a
board-wide `Selector`) - genuinely new: `machines/layers/model.py`'s existing
group-quoted-ability-grant builders (`_GROUP_QUOTED_ABILITY_GRANT_RE`,
`_GRANT_QUOTED_ABILITY_THEN_RETURN_FRONT_FACE_RE`) are all sourced off a
*permanent's own printed static text*, reconciled onto `CardState.granted_
ability_texts` every board sweep by `sync_granted_ability_texts` reading
`quoted_ability_grants`'s "what could this **source** grant" vocabulary - a
one-shot spell resolution that grants to whatever it targeted has no
permanent on the battlefield whose printed text that reconciliation could
ever re-derive the grant from (`sync_granted_ability_texts`'s own docstring
already excludes exactly this shape, citing Urza's Saga's one-shot chapter
II grant as the precedent). `machines/effects/`'s new
`_parse_plural_target_gain_quoted_ability_whole_text` instead appends the
quoted text directly to each resolved target's `granted_ability_texts` (the
same primitive `_parse_target_gains_ability_until_cast_from_exile_clause`
already uses for its own differently-durationed grant) and schedules a
`DelayedTrigger` per target - `RevokeGrantedAbility`, reused unchanged -
watching `TriggerEvent.BEGINNING_OF_STEP`/`Step.CLEANUP` rather than a
named game event, since CR 514.2's cleanup-step turn-based action is where
every "until end of turn" effect ends and CR 514.3a keeps that step open
for priority when something genuinely triggers there. Read whole, ahead of
`split_effect_clauses`, the same way every other quoted-whole-paragraph
shape in this module already is: the granted ability text itself commonly
carries its own internal comma (Launch the Fleet's own "Whenever this
creature attacks, create a..."), which the naive top-level comma cut would
slice mid-sentence. The *target* phrase ("any number of target creatures",
"up to two target creatures you control") is handed to `_targets_
understood(..., count_agnostic=True)` rather than re-derived, since
`machines/targeting.py`'s `profile_for_text` already reads every one of
those count shapes for the casting side.

Proven the granted trigger actually fires, not merely that the text lands:
Launch the Fleet's own attack trigger creates a Soldier token when the
granted creature attacks (which needed its own fix - `machines/effects/`'s
"create N tokens ... tapped and attacking" shape only ever existed paired
with a forced sacrifice, `_ATTACK_TAPPED_ATTACKING_TOKENS_THEN_SACRIFICE_RE`
et al.; the **permanent**, unconditional form
`_parse_tapped_attacking_tokens_whole_text`/`_TAPPED_ATTACKING_TOKENS_RE`
did not exist, so a granted "tapped and attacking" token with no sacrifice
sentence after it silently created nothing). Warriors' Lesson (off-pool,
"up to two target creatures you control", a differently-worded granted
ability) proves both the grant and its combat-damage-draw trigger firing,
and that the grant is actually gone by the next cleanup step. Tested in
`scenarios/test_strive.py`.

**Two multi-symbol mana-cost regressions the strive proof cards exposed**,
unrelated to strive's own rules but blocking the proof cards' own sweep
verdict: `machines/effects/_common.py`'s `_COST_INCREASE_PER_TARGET_LINE_RE` and
`machines/targeting.py`'s twin `_COST_INCREASE_PER_TARGET_LINE` both matched
only a single mana symbol (`\{[^}]+\}`) in "This spell costs `<N>` more to
cast for each target beyond the first." - every pool printing of the shape
happened to cost one generic symbol (Fireball's/Launch the Fleet's own
`{1}`), so Aerial Formation's off-pool `{2}{U}` exposed the gap. Both now
read one-or-more symbols, matching `machines/casting/`'s own `_COST_INCREASE_PER_
TARGET_RE`, which already did. `machines/effects/`'s own `_BARE_
CONTINUOUS_PUMP_RE`/`_CONTINUOUS_PUMP_OR_KEYWORD_RE` and `machines/layers.
py`'s `_PLURAL_TARGET_SUBJECT` were also widened to accept "any number of"
alongside "up to N"/"N", the same shape Aerial Formation's own "Any number
of target creatures each get +1/+1 and gain flying until end of turn."
needed on the plain-pump side.

**Descend's intervening-*if* shape** (CR 603.4/608.2a) - distinct from the
gated-*static* shape above and from CR 700.11's own per-turn "descended
this turn" event count: "When/Whenever ..., if there are N or more
permanent cards in your graveyard, `<effect>`." `machines/triggers/`'s
`intervening_if_holds` had no branch for it at all - `_descend_permanent_
card_count_holds`/`_DESCEND_PERMANENT_CARD_COUNT_CLAUSE` is the new one,
reading `machines/layers/model.py`'s own `count_permanent_cards` (imported
locally to avoid a real circular import: `machines/layers/` imports `combat.py`,
which imports this module). **What actually blocked both proof cards from
ever reaching that branch**: `machines/abilities.py`'s `_ABILITY_WORD`
regex, used to strip a CR 207.2c label before `_parse_triggered` ever sees
the line, capped its second word at letters only - "Descend 4"/"Descend 8"
never stripped, so the whole line never started with "When"/"Whenever" and
silently became a `StaticAbility` instead of a `TriggeredAbility` for
*every* triggered descend clause in the pool (harmless for the static/pump
shape, which `machines/layers/` reads straight off raw oracle text and
never consults this classification - fatal for a triggered one, which
`abilities_triggered_by` only ever finds as a real `TriggeredAbility`). Now
accepts a bare number as the second word, matching `machines/layers/`'s
own `_ABILITY_WORD_RE` that already did. Coati Scavenger (ETB, "if there
are four or more permanent cards in your graveyard") and Starving Revenant
(a non-self-referential "whenever you draw a card" trigger, "if there are
eight or more") are the off-pool proofs, both ways - triggers and does not
trigger below the threshold (CR 603.4: the ability never becomes pending at
all, not one that fires and does nothing). Starving Revenant's own ETB
("surveil 2. Then for each card you put on top of your library, you draw a
card and you lose 3 life.") needed a third new merge, `_merge_surveil_then_
for_each_on_top_draw_and_lose_life_clauses`: `_merge_surveil_then_if_
quality_to_hand_clauses`'s existing sibling only ever read the surveil's
*graveyard*-bound half (`CardSplit.moved`); this reads the *kept* half
(`CardSplit.top_order`, which `Game.surveil` always fills), drawing and
losing life once per card kept so a sibling "whenever you draw a card"
trigger - this same card's own Descend 8 - fires once per card, not once
for the batch. Tested in `scenarios/test_descend_ability_word.py`.

**Morbid's "enters with N counters if a creature died this turn"** - a CR
614.1c replacement effect, not a triggered ability at all, so it shares
none of the machinery above. `machines/replacement/enters.py`'s `_ENTERS_WITH`
already had a *leading* `(?:If (?P<condition>...),\s*)?` group (evaluated
generically at gathering time for any `ENTERS_WITH`/`ENTERS_TAPPED` effect
whose `condition` is set, via `_enters_tapped_condition`/`_read_enters_
condition`), but no trailing one, and Festerhide Boar's own printing puts
the condition after the counters ("... enters with two +1/+1 counters on
it if a creature died this turn."). Added a trailing `(?:\s+if
(?P<trailing_condition>.+?))?` group, folded into the same `condition`
field either way, plus `_read_enters_condition`'s own new "a creature died
this turn" case (`Game.creatures_died_this_turn > 0`, the same running
count `machines/triggers/conditions.py`'s `_creatures_died_this_turn_holds` already
reads for the *triggered*-ability shape of the identical fact, Darklight
Phoenix's threshold form - the two readers do not share code because the
reading sites are different, not because the fact is). `--card` still
reports Charging Rhino's and Festerhide Boar's own clauses as
`static_unaudited`, the same as Mindskinner's identical CR 509.1b shape and
every other combat-restriction/replacement-effect line this sweep does not
have visibility into (`scripts/sweep_pool.py`'s own severity ordering:
`static_unaudited` is "an unknown, never a claim of coverage", not a bug -
`silent` is the only bucket that is) - both are proven correct by scenario
instead. Tested in `scenarios/test_morbid.py`.

Enrage (Needletooth Raptor: combat and noncombat damage both fire it, zero
and prevented damage do not - `test_enrage.py`), Repartee (Rehearsed
Debater: an instant/sorcery targeting a creature pumps it, one targeting a
player does not - `test_repartee.py`), and Survival (Cautious Survivor: the
second main phase's own beginning-of-step trigger, gated on whether the
creature is tapped - `test_survival.py`) needed no engine changes at all;
each off-pool proof card is new pool coverage for an ability word whose
underlying trigger and clause were already both correctly built.

Sweep after this task: `--keywords` unchanged at this task's scope (four
keywords outside it remain - Compleated, Miracle, Monstrosity, Sneak, each
its own subsystem, tracked separately); `--effects` shows none of Charging
Rhino, Akawalli, Deepwater Hypnotist, Launch the Fleet, Gruesome Discovery,
Bellowing Aegisaur, Ranging Raptors, Stirring Hopesinger, Kona, Basking
Capybara, Didact Echo, or any printing added by this task as `silent`
(Charging Rhino and Festerhide Boar are `static_unaudited`, the documented,
non-bug category above; every other card is `handled`).

## Flow 1, T5/G2b: Veil of Summer's opponent-cast condition, per-turn

## can't-be-countered, and the "you and `<group>`" subject split

Three independent gaps Veil of Summer's three sentences exposed, each closed
generally rather than for this one card, plus the compound-subject splitter
the third sentence needs. Veil's own player-hexproof half (its fourth
sentence, in the reminder text's own words: "You and they can't be the
targets of blue or black spells or abilities your opponents control") is
**not** built here - see the row's own note at the end of this section for
why, and what still fails closed.

**"An opponent (has )?cast a `<colour>`[ (and/)?or `<colour>`]\* spell this
turn"** - a new `Game.condition_holds` branch, `_CONDITION_OPPONENT_CAST_
COLOR`, read the same way `_CONDITION_CAST_A_SPELL_THIS_TURN` already reads
a card-type/subtype quality off `Game.spells_cast_this_turn`, now reading a
colour (CR 105.1's five) instead, checked against every opponent's own list
rather than the asking player's. Reached from two different printed shapes
through the identical branch: Veil of Summer's trailing "Draw a card if an
opponent has cast a blue or black spell this turn." (`_parse_condition_
clause`'s existing trailing-if reader, built by T4, needed nothing new here
beyond `condition_holds` learning the shape) and Sandstalker Moloch's
differently-worded intervening if, "if an opponent cast a blue and/or black
spell this turn" (CR 603.4) - `machines/triggers.intervening_if_holds`
gained one new, narrowly-gated call, `_opponent_cast_color_holds`, that
recognises only this one condition's shape (by the identical regex,
imported from `models/game/_conditions.py`) and then asks `Game.condition_holds`
directly, rather than a second copy of the colour/opponent logic living in
`machines/triggers/` - the two cards can never drift apart on what
"cast" or "an opponent" means. Every other intervening-if shape in that
ladder is untouched; this does not become a general `condition_holds`
fallback for triggered abilities. Tested in
`scenarios/test_opponent_cast_colour_condition.py`.

**"[Other ]Spells you control can't be countered this turn"** - CR 611.2c's
second sentence: a continuous effect generated by a resolving spell or
ability that changes no characteristic and no controller "modifies the
rules of the game, so it can affect objects that weren't affected when that
continuous effect began" - unlike the printed, per-object "This spell can't
be countered" `test_cant_be_countered.py` already covers (CR 113.6g,
`casting_restrictions.cannot_be_countered`), this grant has to reach a spell
already on the stack *and* one the same controller casts later the same
turn. Recorded as a new `CastingRuleKind.SPELLS_CANT_BE_COUNTERED_GRANT`
row on `Game.casting_rule_effects` (`create_spells_cant_be_countered_grant`)
- the same list Ranger-Captain of Eos's noncreature restriction and
Teferi's sorcery-speed-flash grant already live on, with `Duration.
UNTIL_END_OF_TURN`, so it expires through that list's own existing
`Game.cleanup_step` filter with no change to cleanup itself. Read back in
the one place CR 113.6g's own refusal is already enforced, `Game.counter`,
alongside `cannot_be_countered` (CR 101.2: either "can't" is enough) via the
new `spell_protected_from_countering`. `CastingRuleEffect` gained one new
field, `excluded_source_id`, for Determined's own "**Other** spells you
control" (Bound // Determined's back half) - the resolving spell that
granted the protection is excluded from it by identity, never by name, so a
second copy of the same card is unaffected. The field is dump-reachable
from `Game`, added without a schema bump per this wave's own convention (the
integration task bumps once for the whole wave). An ability a player
controls is never covered, by the same "has a `.card`" convention
`cannot_be_countered` already uses for CR 405.1's "no card behind it".
Tested in `scenarios/test_cant_be_countered_this_turn.py` (Determined cast
through `Casting.cast_as_split_half`, the same CR 709.3 choice
`test_split_cards.py` already exercises).

**"You and `<group>` you control gain `<keyword(s)>` until end of turn"** -
a compound *subject*, not two CR 608.2c instructions (`split_effect_
clauses`'s own guard, `_PLAYER_GROUP_SUBJECT_AND_RE`, built by T0, already
keeps it whole as one clause). `_parse_you_and_group_gain_clause` splits it
into a player part and a group part sharing one predicate, and hands the
group part - "`<group>` you control gain `<keyword(s)>` until end of turn"
- to the ordinary mass-grant reader, `_parse_mass_pump_group_clause` /
`machines/layers/parse.py`'s `_MASS_PUMP_UNTIL_EOT_RE`. That reader needed two
small widenings to take Veil's group half at all: its subject alternation
learned "permanents you control" (CR 403.3: every object on the battlefield
is a permanent, not only creatures - `_mass_creature_group_targets` and
`_MASS_SUBJECT_RE` in `machines/effects/continuous.py` gained the identical branch,
using the existing `all_permanents_controlled_by` selector), and its
`keywords` capture widened from a bare comma/"and" list of one- or two-word
items to a bounded run of letters/commas/apostrophes/hyphens/spaces, so
"hexproof from blue and from black" (CR 702.11f) is captured whole for
`_split_and_validate_keywords` to split, rather than only ever matching a
plain keyword name. Proven off Veil's own real sentence: after the split,
"permanents you control gain hexproof from blue and from black until end of
turn" grants a real, per-target layer-6 "Hexproof from blue"/"Hexproof from
black" ability (CR 611.2c's fixed-now group), enforced the same place every
other granted hexproof already is (`Game.hexproof_abilities`) - a blue
targeted removal spell from the pool cannot target a permanent Alice
controls, a red one still can. Tested in `scenarios/test_veil_of_summer.py`
(the permanents half only - see below).

**The player half stays a recorded gap, on purpose.** `Game.grant_player_
hexproof`/`grant_player_shroud` and their own clause reader
(`_PLAYER_GAINS_HEXPROOF_RE`/`_player_gains_hexproof_clause`) already exist
and already read the narrowed sentence "You gain hexproof from blue and
from black until end of turn" correctly (a prior, unrelated wave built
CR 702.11c/702.11d's player-hexproof machinery, schema 37) - but wiring
*this* card's player half to them is a separate task's scope, kept apart on
purpose so the two halves land independently. Until that lands,
`_parse_you_and_group_gain_clause` records a `PlayerSubjectSplitNotice`
(`Game.player_subject_split_notices`) instead of granting or silently
dropping the player half - the same "unreadable is not the same as no
effect" convention every other notice list in `machines/effects/` keeps.
Veil of Summer therefore resolves fully (draws correctly, protects its
controller's spells from countering, grants the permanents half of its
hexproof), with the player half recorded as an explicit, loud gap rather
than a silent one.

Sweep after this task: `--effects` shows neither Veil of Summer nor
Sandstalker Moloch as `silent`. Sandstalker Moloch is `handled`. Veil of
Summer was `notice` at this point in the wave - its worst clause, not its
best: `parse_mixed_effect_for_spell` composes all three of its sentences
into one closure with no `__name__` of its own, so the player-half gap the
paragraph above describes had no notice stand-in name for `scripts/
sweep_pool.py`'s `_dispatch_category` to see it by. `_leaves_you_and_group_
player_half_unread` reads the card's own text the way `split_effect_
clauses` splits it for the real dispatcher and downgraded the verdict
directly, so a "you and `<group>`" compound subject could not read
`handled` anywhere in the pool until T12 (below) actually granted the
player half. Bound // Determined's back half, Determined, is `handled`,
and its front half, Bound, is unchanged (`silent` - a `_parse_shared_
subject_clauses`-shaped gap out of this task's scope, T5b's own).
`--targeting` stays at 0.

## Flow 1, T12: Veil of Summer's player hexproof (CR 702.11c/702.11d)

Closes the gap the T5/G2b row above documents: the compound-subject split's
*player* half ("You gain hexproof from blue and from black until end of
turn") is now granted for real, not merely recorded.

**What changed.** `_parse_you_and_group_gain_clause`'s player half
(`player_text`, "You `<predicate>`") is handed to `parse_clause_effect` -
the exact reader `_PLAYER_GAINS_HEXPROOF_RE`/`_player_gains_hexproof_
clause` already existed to read this sentence, proven in `test_player_
hexproof_shroud.py::test_the_clause_parser_reads_hexproof_from_two_
qualities_on_you` before this task began. When it parses (Veil's sentence
does), the resulting `ClauseEffect` is called with the spell's or ability's
controller, granting through `Game.grant_player_hexproof` - the same call
flow 2's own generic mechanism makes, so `Player.targeting_grants` gains
one `PlayerTargetingGrant` per quality (CR 702.11f's "two abilities"), each
`Duration.UNTIL_END_OF_TURN`, expired by the existing `Game.cleanup_step`
filter with **no change to cleanup itself** (flow 3 owns that code; this
task only registers through the state flow 2 already wired into it). The
quality itself is read by `hexproof_qualities_in` (`machines/casting/permissions.py`),
the same CR 702.11f "from A and from B" splitter the *permanents* half
already reuses - one reader, not two. When the player-half predicate does
not parse (a hypothetical future "You and creatures you control gain flying
until end of turn" - a keyword with no meaning for a player), the code
falls back to recording a `PlayerSubjectSplitNotice` exactly as before this
task, so the fail-open convention this file uses throughout is unchanged
for whatever this reader still cannot read.

**Enforcement needed nothing new.** `Game.hexproof_refusal` already judges
"[quality]" off the *source's* characteristics
(`_quality_characteristics_of`), not the target's, already exempts the
target's own controller ("your opponents" - CR 702.11b/CR 702.11d), and is
already asked in three places: `TargetingProfile.check` at announcement
(spells and abilities alike), the live-candidate filters, and `legal_
target`'s own CR 608.2b resolution recheck - so a Veil cast in response to
an already-targeted black spell makes that target illegal and the spell
does nothing on resolution, with no code change here. All of that is flow
2's, built and tested generically before this task started; this task only
supplies the missing *call* that actually produces the grant Veil's own
sentence describes. Tested in `tests/scenarios/test_player_hexproof_from_
quality.py`: an opponent's blue or black spell (Peek, Mind Rot) refused, a
red one (Lava Spike) allowed; the caster's own blue spell still legal; an
opponent's blue or black *ability* (Persistent Petitioners, Bile Urchin)
refused, a red one (Orcish Spy) allowed; Veil cast in response fizzles an
already-targeted Mind Rot (CR 608.2b); the grant gone after `cleanup_step`;
and the full, unmodified card text granting both qualities as two separate
`PlayerTargetingGrant`s with no `PlayerSubjectSplitNotice` left behind
(CR 702.11f).

**Proof exemption (D2), argued.** The project's own "prove generality on a
card that was not the reported one" rule is met everywhere else in this
row - `_player_gains_hexproof_clause`'s reader was proven generically
before this task on a narrowed sentence, and the enforcement path
(`hexproof_refusal`) was proven generically by flow 2 on Blossoming Calm, a
different printing entirely. What remains specific to Veil is the
*mechanism this task wires up*: routing a "You and `<group>`" compound
subject's player half into that reader. A second proof printing for that
exact wiring does not exist to reach for: CR 702.11d's "hexproof from
[quality]" granted to a *player* (as opposed to a permanent) is one of the
rarest templates MTG prints, and a search of every local fixture under
`src/magic_cards_model/data/printings/` for "hexproof from" on a "you"/"you
have hexproof" subject turns up nothing besides Veil of Summer - no other
Modern-, Pioneer- or Standard-legal printing in this repo's pool grants a
player hexproof from a quality at all, let alone through this same
compound-subject shape. Absent network access to a full Scryfall bulk-data
sweep in this session, this is a local-pool search, not an exhaustive one,
but it is consistent with the card's own design history: Veil of Summer is
the templating example most MTG rules resources cite for this exact
sentence, and no reprint or functional reprint exists in the tracked
formats. The *general* half of the mechanism (the "You and `<group>`"
split itself, and `parse_clause_effect`'s dispatch of whatever the
predicate turns out to be) stays provably general - a different predicate
still falls back to a recorded notice rather than a silent drop or a Veil-
only hardcode - so this exemption is scoped to "no second player-hexproof-
from-quality printing exists to prove it on", not to the parsing mechanism
itself.

Sweep after this task: `--effects` no longer lists Veil of Summer under
either `silent` or `notice` - it is `handled`. `--targeting` reports one
unreadable phrase, on Nahiri, the Unforgiving - unaffected by this task (my
diff touches no targeting-phrase code) and out of this task's scope; it
predates this task in the shared wave branch. The pool-wide silent count is
95, comfortably under this wave's
`<= 103` target. No schema bump: `PlayerTargetingGrant.quality` and
`PlayerSubjectSplitNotice` are both pre-existing dump-reachable fields
(flow 2's schema 37 and T5/G2b respectively); this task adds no new field.
The dispatch fingerprint (`tests/dispatch_fingerprint_baseline.json`) is
unchanged - `_parse_you_and_group_gain_clause` is still the winning parser
for this clause shape; only what it does internally changed.

## S04: characteristics that exist only off the battlefield (CR 113.6c)

"As long as `<this>` isn't on the battlefield, it's a `<P/T>` `<subtype>`
`<type>` in addition to its other types." (Grist, the Hunger Tide). CR 113.6c:
an ability that names the zones it doesn't function in "functions everywhere
except for the specified zones, even outside the game". Not a CDA (CR 604.3a's
fifth criterion: it sets values "only if certain conditions" hold), so it is
not a copiable value either (CR 707.2).

| Piece | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| Reader | `machines/layers.off_battlefield_characteristics` | Parses the template per line after self-name normalisation; every granted word must be a CR 205.2a type or CR 205.3 subtype. Memoised on text. |
| Object | `CardState.types`/`.subtypes`/`.printed_power`/`.printed_toughness` | Add the grant in every zone but the battlefield (CR 205.1b additive). `printed_types` is the grant-free type line. |
| Spell | `CardState.types_as_a_spell` | Adds the grant to a spell's cast-face types regardless of where the object is now: `why_cannot_cast_now`/`why_cannot_cast_restriction` (casting.py), the noncreature cost tax (`Game`), prowess (`keywords.py`), "N `<type>` spells cast this turn" (`machines/triggers/`). |
| Board | `layers.off_battlefield_characteristics_of`, `Game.characteristics_of` | Off the battlefield: `printed_characteristics` (copiable values, grant-free) plus the grant. |
| Entering | `CardState._entering_battlefield`, `Game.put_onto_battlefield` | CR 614.12: replacement effects see the permanent "as it would exist on the battlefield" - Containment Priest does not exile a Grist coming in from exile, and Kinjalli's Sunwing (off-pool proof) does not tap one returned by Generous Revival. |
| Opponents' permanents enter tapped | `replacement._compile_opponents_permanents_enter_tapped` | CR 614.1d: "<plural permanent types, each optionally nonbasic> your opponents control enter tapped" (Kinjalli's Sunwing; the list form covers "Artifacts, creatures, and lands" and "Creatures and nonbasic lands"). Built as the off-pool CR 614.12 proof for Grist: its type check reads `CardState.types` under `_entering_battlefield`. An unread noun or any condition fails closed (not compiled). |
| Look-back | `CardState.remember_last_known_power_toughness` | LKI types/subtypes are compared against the off-battlefield answer, so a Grist that died as a planeswalker keeps `last_known_types == (PLANESWALKER,)` (CR 603.10a). |
| Card filters | `machines/effects/` | Graveyard/library/exile creature-card readers (`_SELECT_FROM_TOP_KINDS`, Tyvar's return, mass exile/reanimate, look-at-top creature, Agatha's Soul Cauldron's reflexive check) and Boneyard Wurm's CDA (`machines/layers/`) read `CardState.types`, not `Card.types`. |

Proof: `tests/scenarios/test_off_battlefield_characteristics.py` - one
zone/filter pair per test on real printings that are not Grist and not in the
deck pool: Essence Scatter (stack, may target) and Negate (stack, may not),
Thalia, Guardian of Thraben (no tax), Soul-Scar Mage (no prowess), Duress
(hand, cannot take), Grisly Salvage (library, offered), Raise Dead (graveyard
target), Boneyard Wurm (graveyard count), The Darkness Crystal (exile target,
enters as a planeswalker only), Kinjalli's Sunwing (CR 614.12, with a
Grizzly Bears control that Sunwing does tap; Containment Priest is kept but is
in the deck pool), plus Grist's
own +1 (milled Grist is an Insect card) and -5 (graveyard Grists count,
including one that went to 0 paying for it).

**No second printing carries the template.** Scryfall, 2026-09-23:
`o:"isn't on the battlefield"` returns Grist and Falkenrath Gorger ("Each
Vampire creature card you own that isn't on the battlefield has madness" - an
ability grant to other cards, not this shape); `o:"on the battlefield, it's"`
returns Grist and Invasion of Zendikar // Awakened Skyclave (whose "As long as
Awakened Skyclave is on the battlefield, it's a land" is the opposite zone
condition). As with D1 (Bound), the reader is proven on the listed card and
the widened readers on the second printings above, each a different
zone/filter pair.

## S09: linked "exiled with this" piles (CR 607.2a)

Keen-Eyed Curator, Boiling Rock Rioter, Voltaic Visionary // Volt-Charged
Berserker and Pyxis of Pandemonium were silent. Every clause of all four now
sweeps `handled` (Volt-Charged Berserker's "This creature can't block." is
`static_unaudited` and proven by `test_play_from_linked_exile_trigger.py`).
CR numbers verified with `mise run rules:find`: 607.1, 607.1c, 607.2a, 607.3,
406.3, 406.3a, 406.3b, 400.7, 113.7a, 601.1a, 305.2a, 110.2a, 110.4a, 205.2a,
608.2d, 608.2g, 601.2f, 601.2h, 107.3a, 115.1a, 115.1b, 303.4a, 701.23b.

| Mechanic | Rules | How | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linking what an ability exiled to its source, for every exile an ability makes | CR 607.2a, CR 406.6, CR 400.7 | `machines/effects.link_cards_exiled_during`, called by `Game._resolve_ability` after the effect runs: when the source prints another ability reading "the exiled card(s)"/"exiled with [this object]" and the resolving ability's own text instructs an exile, every card newly in exile without a pile of its own gets `ExileMarker.LINKED` back to the source. `ExileAnnotation.linked_permanent_stamp` records which incarnation (the source's `zone_change_stamp`), and `ExileAnnotation.links_to`/`Game.cards_exiled_with` match on it, so a permanent that left and returned reads none of its earlier self's pile. An activated ability now carries `AbilityOnStack.source_stamp`, captured by `Game.begin_activating` before a cost could move the source | all four files below |
| "As long as there are N or more card types among cards exiled with this `<type>`, it gets +X/+Y and has `<keyword>`" | CR 607.2a, CR 205.2a, CR 613.4c, CR 613.1f | `machines/layers._GRAVEYARD_CARD_TYPES_GATED_SELF_STATIC_RE` widened from delirium's "cards in your graveyard" to the linked pile and the subject "it"; `_linked_exile_card_types_gated_self_static_builder` counts `count_card_types` over `LayerContext.cards_exiled_with` (the shared exile zone now rides on `LayerContext.exile`) | `scenarios/test_linked_exile_card_type_threshold.py` |
| "you may cast `<spell>` from among cards [you own] exiled with this `<object>`[ without paying its mana cost]" | CR 607.2a, CR 608.2d, CR 608.2g, CR 108.3, CR 406.3b, CR 601.2f-h, CR 107.3a | `machines/effects._CAST_FROM_LINKED_EXILE_RE` / `_cast_from_linked_exile_effect`: candidates are face-up, nonland cards in the source's own pile matching the subtype/type words (`_quality_matcher`), the owner when "you own" is printed, and an exact mana value (X from the activation) when printed; then `Game.cast_during_resolution`, which gained `pays_mana_cost` for the paid form (the X of a paid mana cost is chosen as for miracle). `Game._resolution_cast_option_is_legal` now reads the spell's own targets (`spell_profile_for_text`, CR 115.1a-b) rather than the whole card text, so a creature whose *activated* ability targets is castable and an Aura with nothing to enchant is not (CR 303.4a) | `scenarios/test_cast_from_linked_exile.py` (Boiling Rock Rioter; Kaho, Minamo Historian as the second printing) |
| "search your library for up to N `<quality>` cards, exile them, then shuffle" | CR 701.23a, CR 701.23b, CR 701.24a | `machines/effects._SEARCH_UP_TO_AND_EXILE_RE`; the exile is linked by `link_cards_exiled_during` (Kaho's enters trigger) | `scenarios/test_cast_from_linked_exile.py` |
| "When you play a card exiled with this `<type>`" | CR 601.1a, CR 607.2a, CR 400.7 | `machines/triggers._PLAY_A_CARD_EXILED_WITH_CONDITION` watches `TriggerEvent.CAST_SPELL` and the new `ExtraTriggerEvent.PLAYS_LAND` (emitted by `Game.play_land` and `Game._play_land_during_resolution`); both carry `GameEvent.origin_exile_annotation`, the pile the card was played out of (a cast reads `CastRecord.exile_annotation`), matched against this incarnation of the source | `scenarios/test_play_from_linked_exile_trigger.py` |
| "Each player turns face up all cards they own exiled with this `<type>`, then puts all permanent cards among them onto the battlefield" | CR 406.3, CR 406.3a, CR 607.2a, CR 110.2a, CR 110.4a, CR 113.7a | `machines/effects._TURN_LINKED_FACE_UP_THEN_PUT_PERMANENTS_RE`: the pile of the object the ability was activated from (its stamp taken before the sacrifice cost), turned face up per owner in APNAP order, then each owner puts their permanent cards onto the battlefield. A face-down card with only a bare `ExileMarker.LINKED` link still has no characteristics (`CardState.has_no_characteristics`) until then | `scenarios/test_face_down_linked_exile_return.py` |

Proof printings: a Scryfall search (2026-09-23) found no second printing of

(Modern-legal, not in the deck pool). `sweep_pool.py --effects` before/after:
