## The behavioural sweep: parsed is not played (`tests/test_behavioural_sweep.py`)

`card_support` (and `sweep_pool.py` on it) is static: "a dispatcher returned
an effect for this text". It said `handled` for Devourer of Destiny's cast
trigger on the day that trigger vanished in production (b4316b8; fixed by
838d1b0: a line merely *mentioning* hexproof made Kaito hexproof, so CR 603.3d
removed the only-target trigger). The behavioural sweep executes instead.

**What it runs.** For every card in the fixture pool that exists in Modern,
Pioneer or Standard (`support.in_target_formats`), every triggered and every
activated clause `card_support` classifies `handled`:

- a trigger's event is raised through the real engine path - chosen by the
  engine's own parsed `TriggeredAbility.event` (or `_unread_trigger_events`
  for `event=None`), never by card name: put onto the battlefield or cast
  (ETB, "when you cast this spell"), destroy/sacrifice/exile/bounce (dies,
  leaves), declare attackers/blockers and deal combat damage, play whole
  turns (every "at the beginning of", draw step, untap step, Saga chapter),
  cast a probe spell, tap a mana source, draw/gain/discard/scry/energy,
  counters, monstrosity, transform, morph face up, targeting, waterbend.
  "Other object" conditions take their probe from `support._probe_cards`
  (the engine's own reachability probe);
- an activation is announced through `Game.begin_activating`/
  `activate_ability` (or `off_zone_activation` for a hand/graveyard/exile
  ability) with the first legal targets and the cost's objects chosen by the
  cost's own `CardRequirement`;
- it passes only if the ability reaches the stack (CR 603.3) - or, a
  triggered mana ability, resolves on the spot (CR 605.4a) - and resolving
  it changes the game or asks a question (CR 608.2d), with no notice
  (`ResolutionEffect` in `tests/scenarios/harness.py`: the engine failing
  closed on a clause is a failure, not an effect).

**Boards.** One stock board: alice (the controller, active) has three of
each basic plus Wastes and only colourless non-land permanents; bob's
coloured permanents all *mention* a targeting protection they do not have
(Kaito on alice's turn, a non-monstrous Fleecemane Lion) and his artifacts
grant or remove hexproof elsewhere (Shadowspear, Dragonfire Blade). A trigger
that CR 603.3d removes for "no legal target" while the target restriction
itself (`TargetRequirement.rejects`) accepts one of those objects fails on
the spot - the Devourer defect, caught for every targeting trigger, not just
cast triggers (the old per-cast-trigger guard in
`test_hexproof_granting_lines_are_not_hexproof.py` is folded into this).
Each case tries the board four ways, stopping at the first that works:
`quiet` (stock), `busy` (an eventful turn: three instants, two creature
spells, life gained, two draws, a sacrifice, a permanent card discarded, an
opponent's blue spell; a richer board with an enchantment, a 4-power
creature, more Mountains and snow lands), `lonely` (no opposing non-land
permanents), `war` (every creature attacks, then five creatures die). A
target or cost the stock board cannot supply is added from the pool by the
engine's own `rejects`/`why_not` (`_target_material`, `_cost_material`).

**Skips.** `TRIGGER_KIND_SKIPS` is per event kind, reviewed, and empty: every
event kind in the pool is raised. `KNOWN_ENGINE_GAPS` is per clause and
`xfail(strict=True)`: real gaps the sweep found that need new cost plumbing,
left for the silent-card campaign - Illuminated Folio ("Reveal two cards from
your hand that share a color") and The Filigree Sylex ("Remove ten oil
counters from among permanents you control and sacrifice ..."), both "cannot
build a cost" (Tameshi's return-a-land cost has been built since f67d0a6).

**Drivers added 2026-09-24** (per event kind or precondition, never per
card), which took the last 13 unexecuted cases to executed: a Class level-up
is raised by activating the level ability from one level below (CR 716.2a);
"if it entered from your graveyard" puts the source, or another creature,
onto the battlefield from the graveyard (CR 603.4); an intervening "if this
[permanent] has N or more [kind] counters on it" stages the counters; "if an
opponent controls more [lands/creatures/artifacts] than you" gives the
opponent one more than the controller, counted on the stock board; disguise
and megamorph are turned face up like morph (CR 702.168a, 702.37e); "from
anywhere other than your hand" casts the Adventurer from exile; "noncreature
permanents" probes with the stock Equipment and enchantment; a "target ...
spell" requirement gets the first stock probe spell its own `rejects`
accepts; "target token" gets a predefined token (CR 111.10); and a "blocking
or blocked by [this]" activation is made with the source attacking and
blocked (CR 509.1g). One was an engine gap, fixed test-first: "you play a
land or cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand" (Shadow of the
Goblin, proof Vega, the Watcher; CR 601.1a, 116.2a) -
`tests/scenarios/test_play_from_anywhere_other_than_hand.py`.

**Numbers (2026-09-23).** 821 cases: 478 triggers executed across 31 event
kinds (215 enters, 52 beginning-of-step, 49 cast, 41 dies, 31 attacks, 20
Saga chapters, 12 damage, 11 tapped for mana, and the long tail), 340
activations executed, 3 known gaps xfailed, 0 skipped; 280s single process.
`mise run test` leaves it out; `mise run test:behaviour` runs it alone and
`mise run test:full` - the merge gate - runs everything. Every case is its
own parameter, so it also runs under pytest-xdist.

**Findings, each fixed test-first on the way** (CR numbers verified with
`mise run rules:find`): a resolved Adventure was exiled without its
adventured pile, so the creature could never be cast (CR 715.3d); Prairie
Dog's "if you haven't cast a spell from your hand this turn" (CR 603.4); The
Darkness Crystal's die-replacement exiled without the CR 607.1 link its own
activation targets; "a creature attacks you or a planeswalker you control"
read as the attacker's controller (Slumbering Dragon, proven on Isperia,
Supreme Judge; CR 506.2, 508.1b); "N or more creatures died this turn",
"you attacked with N or more creatures this turn", "it has no <kind> counters
on it" activation restrictions (Lagomos, both Ojer temples, Minas Tirith;
CR 602.5b); off_zone_activation could not pay an exile cost (Scrapheap
Scrounger); "Exile this artifact" as a cost (Relic of Progenitus, Brittle
Effigy; CR 700.7); Might Makes Right's "each creature on the battlefield with
the greatest power" (CR 208.1); "you attack with one or more creatures ...
that many" (Screaming Swarm; CR 508.3d); "[you may] put a card you own from
outside the game into your hand" (North Wind Avatar, Mastermind's
Acquisition; CR 108.3b). New pool printings: Sliver Construct (target
material for "target Sliver"), Isperia, Minas Tirith, Brittle Effigy,
Mastermind's Acquisition. Rules verified for the sweep itself: CR 603.2,
603.3, 603.3d, 603.4, 605.4a, 608.2d, 602.2, 702.11b.

## S25: mass effects with qualifiers, and damage-dealt-to-self redirection

Flame Sweep, Elspeth, Sun's Champion (-3) and Screaming Nemesis were silent;
every clause of all three now sweeps `handled`. Mass-effect qualifiers are
read off the computed board (CR 613.1, 613.5) once, as the effect is applied
(CR 608.2h), with no target (CR 115.10a). Nemesis's "that much" is the damage
the triggering event actually dealt after prevention (CR 615.6); "any other
target" excludes the source (CR 115.4); the life-gain lock is
`Player.cannot_gain_life`, set only on a player the damage actually reached,

control" reader is gone; the general "except for" grammar reads it. CR

702.26f's "for as long as" durations ending at phase-out.

## Golden behaviour snapshots: played is pinned (`tests/golden/`)

The behavioural sweep proves each handled ability *does something*; its
goldens pin *what*. Every executed case writes and then compares
`tests/golden/<card-slug>/<triggered|activated>-<n>.json`:

- `board` - the setup in the engine's own scenario DSL: each seat's
  `Scenario().player(...)` arguments, predefined tokens, tapped material, the
  start step, and whether the busy/war turn was played first;
- `recipe` - the variant and the attempt (name, index, parameters) that
  raised the event, or for an activation whether the source entered this
  turn;
- `action` - the ability on the stack: source, controller, targets, modes, X;
- `delta` - what its resolution changed: objects moved/tapped/damaged/
  countered/pumped, tokens created, life and player counters, questions asked
  (CR 608.2d), notices, changed game fields, the stack left behind.

Objects are labelled `<name>@<owner>#<k>` from a fixed walk of the game, never
by raw id; the board is built under the engine's id allocator seeded by the
case, the variant and the board's contents, and `Game.game_uid` is pinned the
same way, so shuffles and ids are identical on every run (checked across
`PYTHONHASHSEED` values). A mismatch fails the case's own test id with a
unified diff; `mise run golden:update` (`pytest ... --update-golden`)
regenerates them and the diff is reviewed in the commit, never hand-edited.
`test_every_golden_belongs_to_a_swept_case` flags a stale golden.

**Format decision.** The engine's `snapshot.py` is a board *cache*, not a
format, and the api's play-script DSL (`contract/playscript.schema.json`) is a
seat's conditional move plan - it has no board setup, and engine tests may
not depend on the api repo. The carrier is therefore engine-native: the
scenario harness's own builder arguments plus the sweep's recipe, as JSON.

**Replayable.** `tests.golden.load(path)` returns a `Golden`;
`build_board()` builds the recorded board plus the recipe's staging (source
primed: face, Class level, Aura, intervening-if counters; target spell cast)
through the harness, `replay()`
plays the recorded recipe through the real engine and returns the record
(equal to the file while behaviour is unchanged; `tests/test_golden_snapshots.py`
replays three). `mise run golden:replay <file>` prints a golden and its replay.

**Proven (2026-09-24, scratch copies).** Reverting 838d1b0's hexproof fix
fails the Devourer of Destiny case; with the sweep's own no-legal-target guard
also disabled, the golden alone still fails it - the trigger falls back to the
busy board and exiles alice's Intangible Virtue instead of Kaito. Changing the
"you gain N life" reader to N+1 fails Guide of Souls' golden with
`"life": [20, 21]` becoming `[20, 22]`.

**Numbers.** 925 goldens (3.7 MB); the sweep with comparison runs 344s single
process (926 passed, 2 xfailed), against 280s before goldens - the extra is
the two state projections around each resolution.

## C00-T2: player casting, draw and search prohibitions

High Noon, Teferi, Time Raveler and Voice of Victory's cast-count/timing
statics, and Grafdigger's Cage's and Soulless Jailer's cast-from-zone
statics, were already implemented by `machines/casting_restrictions.py`
before this task; they were `static_unaudited` (present, unproven) and are
now backed by scenario tests. Three genuinely new mechanisms were built:
the per-turn draw cap, the search prohibition, and (in `machines/
replacement.py`) a real fix to the enter-the-battlefield "can't" family -
Soulless Jailer's "Permanent cards" clause was silently inert: `_CARD_TYPE_
WORDS` had no entry for the word "permanent", so `_cant_enter_replacements`
read `wanted is None` and skipped building the replacement outright. CR
numbers verified with `mise run rules:find` (`rules:pull` first, effective
September 25, 2026): 101.2, 110.1, 121.2b, 400.4a, 601.3, 604.1, 604.2,
611.1, 611.2c, 611.3a, 613.11, 614.17, 614.17d, 701.23.

| Mechanic | Reader | Reported card(s) | Off-pool proof | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "`<Creature/Permanent>` cards in graveyards [and libraries] can't enter the battlefield" - CR 614.17d's own "can't" family (not a replacement effect), the destination reset to the object's origin zone (CR 400.4a); widened to accept a bare "permanent" filter (no type restriction) and an optional "non`<type>`" exclusion, the same convention `_copy_candidates` already used for Clever Impersonator's "any nonland permanent" | `replacement._cant_enter_replacements`, `_cant_enter_applies`, `_CANT_ENTER_RE` | Grafdigger's Cage, Soulless Jailer | Kunoros, Hound of Athreos (single zone); Weathered Runestone ("Nonland permanent", two zones) | `test_graveyard_library_cast_and_enter_bans.py` |
| "Each opponent/player can't draw more than one card each turn" - CR 121.2b's own per-individual-draw check, asked once per draw inside `Game.draw_cards`'s CR 121.2 loop rather than once per instruction, so a "draw two" against a cap of one still performs the first | `casting_restrictions.draw_cap_restriction`, `_DRAW_CAP_RE`, wired into `Game.draw_cards` | Narset, Parter of Veils | Spirit of the Labyrinth ("each player", not "each opponent") | `test_draw_limit.py` |
| "Spells and abilities your opponents control can't cause their controller to search their library" - a self-search-only gate (the causer and the searcher are the same player, so a "search target opponent's library" shape is untouched by construction); wired into the shared `Game.search_library`/`search_and_put` funnel via a new `caused_by` parameter, threaded from the dominant "search your library for..." effect family (`_search_and_place_for`/`_build_search_clause`) | `casting_restrictions.search_prohibition_source`, `_SEARCH_PROHIBITION_RE` | Ashiok, Dream Render | Diabolic Tutor (an unrelated tutor exercising the same shared funnel) | `test_search_prohibition.py` |
| "Each player can't cast more than one spell each turn" / "Each opponent can cast spells only any time they could cast a sorcery" / "Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn" - pre-existing readers, now proven | `casting_restrictions.blanket_cant_cast_restriction`, `sorcery_speed_restriction_source` | High Noon, Teferi Time Raveler, Voice of Victory | Rule of Law (identical text); Teferi, Mage of Zhalfir (identical static on an unrelated creature printing) | `test_cast_count_and_timing_prohibitions.py` |

Proof printings added: Rule of Law, Teferi, Mage of Zhalfir, Kunoros, Hound
of Athreos, Weathered Runestone, Spirit of the Labyrinth, Diabolic Tutor.

Scope boundary, documented rather than silently narrowed: `caused_by` is
wired only into the dominant "search your library for ..., put it ..., then
shuffle" clause family (fetchlands, ordinary tutors) - not into the rarer
"its controller may search ..." anaphoric shape (Ghost Quarter) or the
top-of-library "reveal it, then shuffle and put that card on top" family
(Mystical Tutor), neither of which any listed card for this task needs.
Both default `caused_by` to `None` (unchanged prior behaviour) rather than
silently guessing a controller.

CR 616.1's choice of which replacement or prevention effect applies first is
put to the affected player (or the affected object's controller) by
`replacement.choose_effect`, as a `CHOOSE_A_MODE` question whose prompt cites
CR 616.1, after CR 616.1b-c's forced tiers; asked again per CR 616.1f only
while two or more distinct effects remain. Solphim beside Artist's Talent: Bob
takes 8 (doubling first) or 10 (+2 first) as he answers
(`test_damage_increase_and_double.py`). CR 616.1a's self-replacement tier is
still a hook with nothing to hang on it.

Lance.

## C00-T5: enters tapped / enters with counters / enters untapped

Chalice of the Void, Walking Ballista, Murktide Regent, Ral, Monsoon Mage //
Ral, Leyline Prodigy, Slumbering Trudge, Darkslick Shores, Spirebluff Canal,
Hall of Storm Giants, Boggart Trawler // Boggart Bog, Disciple of Freyalise //
Garden of Freyalise, Hydroelectric Specimen // Hydroelectric Laboratory, Witch
Enchanter // Witch-Blessed Meadow and Spelunking were already `static_
unaudited` on every one of these clauses, not silent or notice - most of the
underlying replacement-effect machinery (`_self_enters_modifiers`,
`_enters_tapped_condition`/`_controls_other_lands`, `_optional_enters_payment`/
`_pay_life_or_tapped`, `_compile_lands_you_control_enter_untapped`, and
`amount_expression`'s "three minus X" arithmetic) already existed and already
worked; this wave is mostly proof-by-scenario-test of code nobody had driven
yet, plus two genuine gaps it found along the way. CR numbers verified with
`mise run rules:find`: 109.5, 119.4, 205.2a, 205.2b, 302.6, 400.7, 601.2i,
604.2, 607.2q, 613.5, 614.12, 614.12a, 614.1c, 614.1d, 616.1, 702.66a, 712.12,
712.8f.

| Mechanic | Reader | Card(s) | Off-pool proof | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "[This] enters with X `<kind>` counters on it" (CR 107.3m's own X) | `replacement._self_enters_modifiers` (pre-existing) | Walking Ballista, Chalice of the Void | Hangarback Walker (already proven) | `test_enters_with_x_counters.py` |
| "[This] enters with a `<kind>` counter on it for each `<description>`" - a genuinely new counter-count shape, singular and per-matching-thing rather than a literal count or an "equal to `<expr>`" - `replacement._COUNTER_FOR_EACH`/`_read_counters` widened to read it, carrying the "for each" tail as `amount_expression` unevaluated the same way the "equal to" shape already does | `replacement._COUNTER_FOR_EACH` (new); `effects.amount_expression`'s two new terms below | Murktide Regent, Ral, Leyline Prodigy | Diregraf Colossus (a third, unrelated "for each" category - Zombie cards already in the graveyard, read by the pre-existing `count_expression` subtype-in-graveyard term, proving the outer template generalises past the two motivating cards) | `test_enters_with_counted_counters.py` |
| "`<types>` card(s) exiled with it" - CR 607.2q's link, written as the cost is paid rather than read after the fact | `machines.objects_as_costs.delve` (new: sets `CostComponent.link_to_permanent_id` to the spell's own id on every substitution it builds), `CostComponent.pay`'s `EXILE` branch (new: writes `ExileAnnotation(marker=LINKED, ...)` onto each card once `Game.exile_cards` moves it), `effects._CARDS_EXILED_WITH_IT_RE`/`_read_type_word_list` (new `amount_expression` term) | Murktide Regent | - (delve's own "exiled with it" shape is Murktide-specific in the current pool; the outer template's generality is proven by Diregraf Colossus above instead) | `test_enters_with_counted_counters.py` |
| "`<types>` spell(s) you've cast this turn" | `effects._SPELLS_CAST_THIS_TURN_AMOUNT_RE` (new `amount_expression` term, over the pre-existing `Game.spells_cast_this_turn`) | Ral, Leyline Prodigy | - (Ral's own back-face ETB is also exercised end-to-end through the coin-flip transform in the pre-existing `test_ral_monsoon_mage.py`) | `test_enters_with_counted_counters.py` |
| "[This] enters with a number of `<kind>` counters on it equal to `<expr>`. If X is N or less, it enters tapped" - both halves already read by the pre-existing `amount_expression` "minus" arithmetic and `_X_IS_RE`/`_x_is` | `replacement._read_counters`/`amount_expression` and `_enters_tapped_condition`/`_x_is` (pre-existing, unmodified) | Slumbering Trudge | - | `test_enters_with_x_counters.py` (`test_walking_ballista_...` neighbours; Slumbering Trudge itself is proven by the parse-and-apply path shared with the X-counter tests) |
| "[This] enters tapped unless you control `<N>` or fewer other lands" / "If you control `<N>` or more other lands, this land enters tapped" - both polarities of the same count, pre-existing and unmodified | `replacement._YOU_CONTROL_OTHER_LANDS_RE`/`_controls_other_lands`/`_enters_tapped_condition` | Darkslick Shores, Spirebluff Canal, Hall of Storm Giants | - | `test_enters_tapped_land_count.py` |
| MDFC land face "As this land enters, you may pay `<N>` life. If you don't, it enters tapped" - the CR 614.12a choice, pre-existing and unmodified | `replacement._optional_enters_payment`/`_pay_life_or_tapped` | Boggart Trawler // Boggart Bog, Disciple of Freyalise // Garden of Freyalise | - (Witch Enchanter // Witch-Blessed Meadow and Hydroelectric Specimen // Hydroelectric Laboratory already proven by `test_mdfc_land_play.py`) | `test_mdfc_pay_life_or_tapped.py` |

Boggart Trawler // Boggart Bog was not yet in the pool; added with
`scripts/add_card.py`. Diregraf Colossus and Prized Amalgam (a Zombie
graveyard filler for its own test) were likewise added, both legal in Modern
and Pioneer, neither in `magic-cards-model-api/decks/*.txt`.

`Game.schema_version` 64 -> 65: `CostComponent.link_to_permanent_id` is a new
field, reachable from `Game` through a pending `AbilityOnStack.
keyword_activation`/`.unless_payment`'s own `CostPayment.components`.
`tests/test_game_schema_version.py` gained the matching refusal test.
`sweep_pool.py --effects`: 9 silent / 1 notice (Verdant Command, unrelated to
this task) before and after - none of this task's cards were ever silent or
notice to begin with, and none of the new readers touch any other card's
dispatch.

## C00-T6: Spectacle, bestow's own CR 704.5m/CR 604.6 exceptions, scenario proof of pre-existing per-count reductions and additional-cost-exile

Abhorrent Oculus, Emrakul the Promised End, Hollow One, Leyline Binding,
Scion of Draco, Obsidian Charmaw, Detective's Phoenix and Kaheera, the
Orphanguard were all already `handled`/`static_unaudited`-with-working-code
on main; this task's own new work is Spectacle (previously unimplemented -
`ignored_keywords` listed it) and two real bugs in bestow's resolution path
that surfaced while proving Detective's Phoenix's "You may cast this card
from your graveyard using its bestow ability" end to end. Light Up the Stage
and Skewer the Critics now sweep `handled`. CR numbers verified with
`mise run rules:find` this session: 106.7, 116.2g, 118.7a, 118.8a, 305.6,
601.2f, 701.59a, 701.59b, 702.5a, 702.103a, 702.103b, 702.103f, 702.137a,
702.139a, 702.139b, 704.5m.

| Mechanic | Reader | Reported card | Off-pool proof | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spectacle: "Spectacle [cost]" - an alternative cost (CR 118.9, 601.2b/f-h) available only "if an opponent lost life this turn" | `casting._option_from_keyword` (`canonical == "spectacle"`), `KeywordCastOption.spectacle`, `Game.spectacle_condition_holds` (reads `Player.life_lost_this_turn`) | Light Up the Stage, Skewer the Critics | Rix Maadi Reveler (a creature spell, a differently priced cost) | `test_spectacle.py` |
| `CardState.move_to`'s CR 702.103b carve-out only excused a STACK->BATTLEFIELD move, not a STACK->STACK re-statement (`Game._put_on_stack` restates the zone of a spell already on the stack for every ordinary cast) - so `bestowed` was cleared before CR 601.2f's cost was even paid, and no bestow spell, hardcast or from a graveyard permission, could ever resolve as the Aura CR 702.103b promises | `card_state.CardState.move_to` (`zone is not origin` guard added to the `bestowed` clear) | Detective's Phoenix | Hopeful Eidolon | `test_bestow_from_graveyard.py` |
| `keywords.why_cannot_enchant` read only a card's own printed "Enchant [x]" line, never CR 702.103b's dynamic "gains enchant creature" grant - so CR 704.5m's own state-based sweep read a freshly bestowed, legally attached Aura as having no enchant ability at all and put it in the graveyard the instant it entered | `keywords.why_cannot_enchant` (`aura.bestowed` fallback to `["creature"]`) | Detective's Phoenix | Hopeful Eidolon | `test_bestow_from_graveyard.py` |
| CR 702.103f's own exception to CR 704.5m: a bestowed Aura illegally attached (its host left the battlefield, was destroyed, etc.) becomes unattached and ceases to be bestowed instead of going to its owner's graveyard the ordinary Aura way | `keywords.aura_state_based_actions` (`permanent.bestowed` branch, both the unattached and the illegally-attached cases) | Detective's Phoenix | Hopeful Eidolon | `test_bestow_from_graveyard.py` (`test_the_enchanted_creature_dying_reverts_the_bestowed_aura_to_a_creature`) |
| CR 604.6's "You may cast this card from your `<zone>` using its `<keyword>` ability" - bestow's own graveyard permission (Detective's Phoenix) - was already generic (`casting._printed_zone_permissions`, landed with bestow's own modelling before this task); proven end to end here rather than only at the option-listing level | `casting._printed_zone_permissions` (pre-existing) | Detective's Phoenix | - (the reader is generic across any keyword/zone pair a card prints; the graveyard-specific proof is Detective's Phoenix itself, the only pool card carrying the sentence) | `test_bestow_from_graveyard.py` |
| "As an additional cost to cast this spell, exile `<N>` cards from your graveyard" - pre-existing generic reader (`cost._PHRASE_EXILE`/`cost_component_for_phrase`), proven end to end on the required card with corner cases (short graveyard, under-choosing, wrong zone) | `cost.cost_component_for_phrase` (pre-existing) | Abhorrent Oculus | - (the reader is proven generic elsewhere: Necropolis Fiend's activation-side "Exile X cards", Seasoned Pyromancer's "Exile this card", Force of Will's "Exile a blue card from your hand") | `test_additional_cost_exile_from_graveyard.py` |
| "This spell costs `<N>` less to cast for each `<card type in graveyard / cycled-or-discarded this turn / basic land type controlled (Domain) / opponent's `{C}`-producing land>`" - pre-existing generic readers (`Game.cost_reduction_for`), proven end to end on all four required cards | `game.cost_reduction_for` (pre-existing) | Emrakul, the Promised End; Hollow One; Leyline Binding; Scion of Draco; Obsidian Charmaw | - (each already has dedicated genericity proofs in `test_dynamic_cost_reduction.py`/`test_cost_reduction_shapes.py`/`test_self_reduction_reaches_the_cast.py`) | `test_cost_reduction_per_count.py` |
| Companion's type-disjunction condition ("Each creature card in your starting deck is a `<type>`, ... or `<type>` card") - pre-existing (`companion._TYPE_DISJUNCTION_RE`), a changeling creature's every-creature-type CDA (CR 702.73a) proven to satisfy it | `companion.companion_condition_satisfied` (pre-existing) | Kaheera, the Orphanguard | Fire-Belly Changeling, Changeling Outcast, Runeclaw Bear | `test_companion_type_condition.py` |

Behavioural sweep: a "cast a spell from your graveyard" trigger is driven by
casting a fitting probe out of the graveyard under an engine-granted
permission (`_casting` in `tests/test_behavioural_sweep.py`).

Proof printings added: Summon: Fat Chocobo, Summon: Primal Garuda, Clive,
Ifrit's Dominant, Joshua, Phoenix's Dominant, Flame Wave, Vohar, Vodalian
Desecrator, Liliana, Untouched by Death, Gisa and Geralf, Kess, Dissident
Mage, Secrets of the Dead.

new shapes it could not raise before: a boast activation stages the source's
attack (`attacked_this_turn`), a symbol-threshold exile cost stages the
richest black printings in the graveyard, and an "equipped creature you
control attacks" trigger attaches a real Bonesplitter to the attacker.
Connive N (CR 701.50d) is not read - no legal printing prints a count
`effects.amount_expression` can evaluate (Raffine, Scheming Seer; Spymaster's
Vault).

### C02-T7-r1: closing the round's four cross-file blockers

A scope audit found the four items above the r1 notes describe were left as
documented, matched-but-refused `notice`s or `xfail`s rather than fixed,
each because the fix needed a file nominally owned by a different C02 task
that same round (`combat.py`, `machines/triggers/`, `machines/layers/`). All four are
closed; see the rows above for each mechanic's own final shape. Two general,
non-card-specific engine fixes fell out of the work and are worth recording
here on their own:

- `Game._ask_trigger_targets` was handing `profile_for_text` a triggered
  ability's *whole* printed text - condition and effect together - to work
  out what the ability itself announces as a target when it goes on the
  stack (CR 603.3d). A condition containing the bare word "target"/"targets"
  (Speedball's own "that targets Speedball") could therefore be misread as
  an attempted, mandatory targeting requirement of the ability's own, with
  no legal candidate - silently removing the whole ability from the stack
  (CR 603.3d) before its real, targetless effect ever ran. Fixed generally:
  it now reads `TriggeredAbility.effect` (already split off the condition by
  `machines/abilities.py`'s own parser) for every ordinary triggered
  ability, not `.text`. This closed the exact gap
  `tests/scenarios/test_unparsed_trigger_targets.py`'s own docstring had
  predicted and asked to be rewritten for once fixed: Bonecrusher Giant,
  Loki, God of Mischief, and Stirring Hopesinger each had a "becomes the
  target of"/"that targets" *condition* misread the same way, and all three
  now correctly report `understood=True` with no targeting requirement and
  no `TargetingNotice` at all, instead of a false `UNPARSED`.
- `effects_for`'s static-only battlefield sweep never consulted
  `_granted_ability_effects` at all (only the resolution path did,
  deliberately, so a granted *activated* ability - Umbral Mantle's own case
  - never applied passively). Widened to try it on both paths with
  `static_only` threaded through to `parsed_layer_effects`, so
  `_effect_sentences`'s own `StaticAbility`-only gate does the actual
  filtering: a resolved trigger's own self-granted *static*/CDA line (Ms.
  Marvel's own) now reaches the sweep exactly when it is genuinely static,
  and an activated one is still refused there. `CardState.granted_ability_
  texts` needed populating before that sweep runs too, which a one-shot
  resolved self-grant had never done (unlike a static ability's own printed
  quoted grant, `quoted_ability_grants`/`sync_granted_ability_texts`) -
  `_sync_stored_grant_ability_texts` is the stored-effect twin of that sync,
  called every board computation and reconciled off the stored
  `ContinuousEffect` itself, so the grant comes off again the instant
  `end_the_turn` drops it.
| "mill N, put any number of `<quality>` cards from **those cards** into your hand" - VERIFY ONLY (C01-T8's reader): widened to accept "those cards" alongside "from among them" | `effects._MILL_THEN_MAY_TAKE_FROM_MILLED_RE` | Rick Jones, Destined Sidekick | - | `test_look_at_top_play_from_top.py` (`test_rick_jones_mills_four_and_takes_an_enchantment_from_among_them`) |

## FB3: `blocked_casts` - refused casts reported, not silently dropped

`machines/legal_actions.py`'s own `_cast_actions` computed
`_why_cannot_cast_face` (CR 117.1a's timing, `casting.why_cannot_cast_now`,
plus CR 611.1's rules-modifying prohibitions, `casting.why_cannot_cast_
restriction`) per face and `continue`d past a refusal without keeping it -
`legal_actions` never grows a row for an illegal cast (CR 601.3), correctly,
but a seat reading it alone had no way to tell "nothing to cast" apart from
"Ocelot Pride sat in hand the whole game, uncastable only because the stack
was never empty". `blocked_casts(game, player, pending=None)` is the
companion enumeration: one `BlockedCast` (`models/action.py`) per face the
per-face check refused, carrying the engine's own reason verbatim and the CR
number it leads with, read off the refusal string rather than re-derived.
Timing/prohibition only - a card with no permission to be cast from its zone
at all (`why_cannot_cast_from`) and a land (CR 305.1: never a spell) are
left out entirely, the same as `legal_actions`. `_cast_actions`/
`_permission_cast_actions` now take an optional `blocked` output list so the
one walk that decides a face is refused is the one walk that reports it;
`legal_actions` itself is unchanged, and the dispatch fingerprint and
goldens do not move - no `EFFECTS`/`TRIGGER_EFFECTS`/`ACTIVATED_EFFECTS` row
was added. The plain hand cast and `_permission_cast_actions` were not the
only per-face checks inside `_cast_actions`: the keyword/marker/granted
cast-option loop (flashback, escape, Adventure) and the CR 118.9
alternative-cost loop each ask the identical `_why_cannot_cast_face`/
`why_cannot_cast_restriction` question and used to `continue` past a
refusal there too - fixed to call the same `_record_blocked`, so a
graveyard flashback sorcery or an exiled Adventure creature refused by a
CR 611.1 prohibition is reported exactly like a hand card is.

| Mechanic | Reader | Reported card | Off-pool proof | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CR 117.1a timing and CR 611.1 prohibition refusals on a `CAST` face, enumerated with the engine's own reason instead of dropped | `machines.legal_actions.blocked_casts`, `models.action.BlockedCast` | Ocelot Pride | Act of Treason (sorcery timing), Ambush Viper (a flash creature never blocked), Repudiate // Replicate (CR 709.3a: only the sorcery half of a split card blocks), Voice of Victory (a CR 611.1 prohibition, not a timing question), Faithless Looting (a flashback sorcery blocked by a graveyard-casting prohibition, the keyword-option loop), Bonecrusher Giant (its exiled Adventure creature half blocked by a CR 611.1 prohibition, the `pays_mana_cost=True` keyword-option branch) | `scenarios/test_blocked_casts.py` |

## EC1: energy payments - "you may pay {E}. If/When you do", and no printed symbol reaches `ManaCost.parse`

Nine in-format energy cards crashed live and in `card_support` with
`ValueError: unsupported mana symbol: {E}`: `_parse_may_pay_energy_if_you_do_
clause`/`_parse_reflexive_pay_energy_clause` declined a consequence they
could not read, and the dispatcher fell through to the ordinary-mana twins,
whose `(?:\{[^}]+\})+` group accepted {E} and handed it to `ManaCost.parse`.
Three changes close it. The energy and mana twins now share one consequence
reader (`pay_consequence_effect` for CR 118.12's "If you do", on the same
ability; `reflexive_pay_consequence_effect` for CR 603.12's "When you do",
run by the reflexive ability through `ReflexivePayEnergyConsequence` or the
new `ReflexivePayManaConsequence`). The mana twins read mana symbols only
(`ManaCost.try_parse`, `None` for {E} (CR 107.14), {T} (CR 107.5), {Q} (CR
107.6) or any other non-mana symbol), so an energy text is never misrouted.
And every call site that parses printed text a regex captured asks
`ManaCost.try_parse` and reads the text or declines: the pay twins,
`_exact_mana_cost_matcher` (the search description is refused), the "may
pay ... attacking token" and "pay or lose" delayed readers, `machines/cost/`'s
waterbend, whole-phrase (`total_cost_for_phrase`: the phrase is unread) and
cumulative-upkeep hybrid readers, `combat._attack_cost_match` (the CR 508.1h
line is not claimed), `keywords._keyword_cost` (unpayable), the devotion
condition in `machines/layers/` (the symbol is not counted), and in `machines/casting/`
the CR 118.9 "pay {N}" alternative cost (falls to the phrase reader), the
splice parameter (refused) and the per-target cost increase (the cast is
refused with the engine's reason, CR 601.2f, rather than under-charged).
`ManaCost.parse` itself still raises: it is a primitive. Sites that format an
integer (`f"{{{amount}}}"`), parse a card's own `mana_cost` field, or take a
caller's argument (`Casting.increase_cost`'s `_as_mana`) are unchanged.

The consequences read, beyond `parse_mixed_effect`:

- the source anaphor "it gets +N/+N [and gains <keyword>] until end of turn"
  / "it gains <keyword> ...": "it" is the object the trigger event names (the
  attacker, the creature that died), the ability's source when it names
  none; applied as a CR 611.2 one-shot continuous effect to that object only
  while it is still on the battlefield (CR 400.7);
- a one-shot continuous effect over the ability's own announced targets,
  "another target [attacking] creature [you control] gets +N/+N and gains
  <keyword>": read off the consequence's own text, not the whole printed
  ability; the target is announced as the trigger goes on the stack (CR
  603.3d), "another" excludes the source, and an illegal target on
  resolution means the ability does not resolve and the payment is never
  asked (CR 608.2b);
- "target creature can't block this turn" (CR 509.1b), a new targeted clause
  granted as the self line "This creature can't block." until end of turn,
  the same modelling `_TARGET_CANT_BE_BLOCKED_RE` already uses for "can't be
  blocked this turn";
- a reflexive modal "choose one -": the mode is chosen as the reflexive
  ability is put on the stack (CR 603.3c, CR 700.2b) by the existing modal
  trigger path, and the clause is read only when every mode reads;
  `_create_continuous_effect_of_ability_for_mode_text` now applies an
  untargeted mode ("This creature gains vigilance and lifelink ...") to the
  source instead of to an empty target list;
- "this <noun> deals damage equal to its power|toughness to <target>", a new
  targeted clause for abilities: the power is read as the damage is dealt,
  through the layer system on the battlefield and by last known information
  off it (CR 608.2h, CR 113.7a) - a dies trigger (CR 603.10a) deals the power
  the creature died with.

With too few energy counters the payment is not offered (CR 118.3,
`Game.may_pay_energy`'s `affirmative_is_legal`) and nothing happens; a
declined payment does nothing. Every in-format {E} card in the oracle dump
now gets a `card_support` verdict without raising (75 handled, 29 silent, 2
unaudited - the silent ones are "Pay {E}: ..." activations and "you get six
{E}"-style clauses, outside this task).

## EC2: one condition reader - registry, activation instructions, timing, parse boundaries, compounds

Three paths ask "is this printed condition true?" - CR 603.4/608.2a's
intervening "if" (`triggers.intervening_if_answer`), CR 602.1b's activation
instructions (`Game.activation_instruction_refusal`, battlefield and
off-battlefield alike) and `Game.condition_holds` (modal "If ..., choose N
instead", "Activate only if"). Each now ends in one shared fallback,
`machines/conditions.read_condition`: a registered `ConditionReader` (one
module per family - `timing`, `board`, `cast_record`, `history`, `player`,
`objects`), then `Game.builtin_condition_holds`' own `_CONDITION_*` chain,
then the compound combinator. A reader that claims a clause always answers
True/False (False when its context, e.g. the event, is missing); only an
unclaimed clause is None, and None is what fails closed
(`InterveningIfNotice`, an activation refused with the engine's reason). The
classifier's probes land here too: `triggers.intervening_if_readable(printing,
ability)` and `Game.unread_activation_restrictions(ability, source)`;
`scripts/condition_inventory.py` runs both over the pool or an oracle dump.
New persisted state (schema 81, 74 on the branch): `Game.turn_counts`/`turn_counts_last_turn`
(per-turn count ledger, `note_turn_count`/`turn_count`; "combat_phases"
counted as each beginning of combat begins), `Game.damage_dealt_this_turn`
(`DamageDealt`, written by `conditions.history.record` from every
`DEALS_DAMAGE` event - `Game.emit` calls the hook for every event),
`CastRecord.cast_step`/`cast_during_turn_of`, `GameEvent.declared_attacker`.

The behavioural sweep stages what the new instructions and conditions ask
for: an activation runs at the step its "Activate only during ..." names
(`_activation_step`), and "an opponent lost life this turn" / "a card left
your graveyard this turn" are made true on the stock board before the case
(`_history_threshold`).

### EC4: turn-history conditions (clusters H1-H5)

Every turn-history clause below is read by `machines/conditions/history.py`
for both an intervening "if" (CR 603.4, rechecked by CR 608.2a) and an
"Activate only if" restriction (CR 602.5b). The facts come from
`history.record` (every `Game.emit`) into `Game.turn_history`
(`TurnHistoryEntry`: entered, to_graveyard, to_hand, sacrificed, attacked,
crewed - each with the object's characteristics at that moment),
`turn_counts`, `turn_facts` and `damage_dealt_this_turn`; a crime (CR 700.13)
is recorded where a spell or ability with its targets goes on the stack,
energy paid (CR 107.14) in `Game.may_pay_energy`/`pay_any_amount_of_energy`,
excess damage (CR 120.10) in `Game.deal_damage`, exile arrivals by
object identity (CR 400.7) on every event and before any card leaves exile.
"Last turn" reads the rolled ledgers (`history.end_turn`). Schema 83.
`scripts/condition_inventory.py --clusters H1,H2,H3,H4,H5` reports 0 unread.

The behavioural sweep drives every one of them: a combat fought before the
turn plays on (`fought`), a crewed Vehicle or subtype partner for "a <q> and a
<q> attacked", exactly N partners, a hasty creature that entered this turn, N-1
spells cast before an "it was the Nth spell" source, counters put on another
permanent, and a transformed creature face as a combatant - `SWEEP_DRIVER_GAPS`
is empty again. Luminarch Ascension's "Activate only if this enchantment has
four or more quest counters on it" is cluster O1 (EC6), not a turn-history
clause; EC6's object-state reader reads it, so the entry went at the EC
round 2 merge.

## Player-state conditions (EC5: hand, graveyard/exile, life, poison, library)

`machines/conditions/player.py` reads every S1-S3 clause as one grammar - a
subject ("you", "that player"/"they" = the trigger event's player, "defending
player" CR 506.2/508.5, "an opponent"/"a player" = any, "each opponent"/"each
player" = every), a count ("no", "a", "exactly N [or M]", "N or more/fewer/
less", "fewer/more than N", "at least/most N", via `magic_cards_model.numbers`)
or a comparison between players, and a zone. Card qualities go through
`game._card_quality`, permanents through `game._permanent_quality`. Used as an
intervening if (CR 603.4/608.2a) and as "Activate only if" (CR 602.5b) alike.
The starting life total (CR 103.4) is recorded on `Player.starting_life` as
the player is made, from the life it is made with - never assumed to be 20.

| Mechanic | Reader | Reported card | Off-pool proof | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "`<subject>` has/have `<count>` [`<quality>`] cards in `<their>` hand / library / graveyard" (CR 402.1, 401.1, 404.1) | `_player_has_cards` | Ragamuffyn, Lavaborn Muse | Keldon Megaliths, Shrieking Affliction, Hollowborn Barghest, Imaginary Pet, Reaper of Night, Magus of the Library, The Biblioplex ("exactly zero or seven"), Pit Keeper, Battle of Wits | `test_condition_hand_size.py`, `test_condition_graveyard_contents.py`, `test_condition_life_and_poison.py` |
| "`<subject>` has more/fewer `<cards in hand / life / poison counters>` than `<you / each opponent / an opponent / each other player>`" - strict, a tie is not more | `_more_than` | Kitsune Bonesetter | Robber of the Rich, Glorious Enforcer (Sokenzan Renegade's "a player has more ... than each other player" read on a bare board) | `test_condition_hand_size.py`, `test_condition_life_and_poison.py` |
| "there's/there is/are `<count>` [`<quality>`] cards in your graveyard", "`<count>` cards are in your graveyard" | `_cards_in_your_zone` | Walltop Sentries | Lys Alana Dignitary, Shadowborn Demon, Wall of Forgotten Pharaohs / Sand Strangler (the Desert half of the C1 compound) | `test_condition_graveyard_contents.py` |

| "`<this object / its name>` is in your graveyard / on the battlefield / in exile [or ...]" (CR 700.7; CR 400.7 - a recheck reads the source only while its zone-change stamp is the ability's) | `_self_in_zone` | Master of Death | Firemane Angel, Skyblade's Boon | `test_condition_graveyard_contents.py` |

| "it doesn't have the same name as another `<quality>` you control or a `<quality>` card in your graveyard" (CR 201.2a, 709.4; "it" = the event's subject, by last known information once gone) | `_same_name_as` | Guardian Project | - (only printing) | `test_condition_graveyard_contents.py` |

An intervening if that says where its own source is ("if this card is in your
graveyard", "if Firemane Angel is in your graveyard or on the battlefield", "if
this card is the only creature card in your graveyard") is the zone statement of
CR 113.6b: `triggers.zones_ability_functions_in` asks
`conditions.player.zones_the_source_names` first, so Master of Death, Nether
Spirit, Bridge from Below and Firemane Angel trigger from the graveyard, and a
clause that only counts a pile (Sanguine Spy's "among cards in your graveyard")
leaves its source on the battlefield.

## EC6: object state, event subjects and designations - saddle, suspect, renown, venture built

`machines/conditions/objects.py` reads every O1/O2/O3/S4 clause (163, `scripts/condition_inventory.py --clusters O1,O2,O3,S4`: 0 unread). One subject resolver serves every reader: "this `<type>`" and the source's own name or short name (CR 201.5, 201.5c) are the source; "it"/"he"/"they"/"that creature"/"that spell" are the trigger event's subject (the damaged object for "... is dealt damage", CR 120.3), else the source; "enchanted/equipped `<type>`" is what the source is attached to (last known once it has left). A past-tense clause, or a present-tense one about the subject of a leaves-the-battlefield event, is asked of the object as it last existed (CR 603.10a): `last_known_counters` (now snapshot only by a move off the battlefield, so a dies trigger's look-back survives the card being exiled from the graveyard), `last_known_types`/`subtypes`/`colors`, power/toughness rebuilt from the printing plus the counters it left with, and `CardState.last_known_attachments` (new: the Auras and Equipment attached as it left). Qualities are CR 205's vocabulary (colours, supertypes, card types, every subtype, historic CR 700.6), never a free word, so nothing outside those claims a clause.

Opus and Repartee are CR 207.2c ability words (no rules meaning of their
own); every card below is an ordinary CR 601.2 cast trigger. CR numbers
verified with `mise run rules:find` this session: 207.2c, 601.2h, 202.3e,
106.3, 603.7, 505.1, 300.1, 702.34a, 608.2c, 608.2b, 118.9, 611.2a.

## SoS round 2 (sos-t2): Converge in every position, X-count Fractal tokens, 2^X, cast-not-from-hand

`machines/converge.py` is the one shared "colors of mana spent" reader
(CR 207.2c's ability word; `colors_of_mana_spent(game, obj)`, distinct
non-colorless colors off `CastRecord.mana_spent`) that Prismatic Ending's own
converge clause and CR 702.44b's Sunburst already carried independently -
every other converge printing in the Secrets of Strixhaven pool now reuses
it, in three positions: an effect (read directly off the resolving spell), a
target-legality comparison (`machines/targeting.ComparisonCount.
SOURCE_COLORS_SPENT`, read off the ability's own source rather than the
target - CR 603.3d puts a triggered ability's own targets on the stack only
after its source has already finished being cast, unlike Prismatic Ending's
own spell-position converge, which CR 601.2c/601.2h's ordering keeps
unreadable as a restriction), and an enters-with-counters term
(`machines/effects._amount_term`'s new "color[s] of mana spent to cast
it/this spell/this creature" branch, read through `machines/replacement.
_self_enters_modifiers`'s existing `_COUNTER_FOR_EACH` reader).

Wildgrowth Archaic's own "Whenever you cast a creature spell, that creature
enters with X additional +1/+1 counters on it" is a new capability: an
enters-with replacement effect *created by a cast trigger* rather than
printed on the entering object itself. The trigger resolves first
(CR 603.3b: it goes on the stack above the spell that caused it) and writes
a plain "This creature enters with N `<kind>` counters on it." sentence
directly onto the still-on-stack creature spell's own
`CardState.granted_ability_texts` (CR 113.10a: functions exactly as if
printed). `_self_enters_modifiers` was extended, additively, to also read
`ENTERS_WITH`-shaped lines off `granted_ability_texts` alongside the card's
own printed text - the one zone change that keeps that field
(stack-to-battlefield, the same exemption `_carry_cast_record` already
relies on for `CastRecord`) is exactly the window this needs.

Two new `count_expression` terms: "the number of cards you've drawn this
turn" (EC4's own `Game.cards_drawn_this_turn`, already read as a boolean by
`machines/conditions/history._drew`, reused here as a count) and "the number
of differently named `<qualifier>` you control" (CR 201.4a's copiable name,
generalised over any card type or subtype, not fixed to lands). A new
`_parse_referent_object_clause` rider, `_RIDER_PUT_VARIABLE_COUNTERS_RE`
("Put X `<kind>` counters on it, where X is `<expr>`"), threads either count
through the existing `_parse_token_then_object_anaphor_clause_pair`
two-sentence "Create ... token. `<rider>`." dispatch with no further
per-card code.

`CastRecord.origin_zone` (CR 601.2a), already used the other way by Ral,
Monsoon Mage/Ojer Pakpatiq-style "cast from your hand" reads, is what
answers "if this spell was cast from anywhere other than your hand" - no new
cast-zone tracking, only a new reader of the existing field. Mathemagics'
own "draws 2ˣ cards" is CR 107.3a's ordinary announced X, exponentiated
rather than used literally.

| Mechanic | Reader | Reported card | Off-pool proof | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Converge (CR 207.2c) - the shared "colors of mana spent" reader, in an effect position: discard (Arcane Omens), damage-then-exile-excess (Archaic's Agony, CR 120.4a/120.10), token-creation-then-counters-and-life (Snarl Song), a three-actor compound draw/damage/life (Together as One), a target-less "you" clause | `converge.colors_of_mana_spent`; `effects._parse_converge_discard_by_colors_spent`, `_parse_converge_damage_then_exile_excess_clause`, `_parse_converge_fractal_tokens_and_life_clause`, `_parse_converge_draw_damage_life_clause`, `_parse_converge_draw_and_lose_life_clause` | Arcane Omens, Archaic's Agony, Snarl Song, Together as One | Painful Truths (the target-less "you draw X and lose X life" shape) | `test_converge_effect_shapes.py` |
| Converge, the enters-with-counters position: "This creature enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each color of mana spent to cast it." | `_COLORS_OF_MANA_SPENT_TO_CAST_IT_RE` in `effects._amount_term` | Magmablood Archaic, Rancorous Archaic, Wildgrowth Archaic | Skyrider Elf | `test_converge_effect_shapes.py` |
| Converge, the target-legality position: "exile target nonland permanent an opponent controls with mana value less than or equal to the number of colors of mana spent to cast this creature" | `targeting.ComparisonCount.SOURCE_COLORS_SPENT`, resolved in `TargetRequirement._counted_bound` off `source_id` | Sundering Archaic | - (reuses `exile_ability_targets`'s existing generic "exile target `<phrase>`" reader once the comparison itself is readable; no card-specific code) | `test_converge_effect_shapes.py` |

Put X `<kind>` counters on it, where X is `<expr>`." - a two-sentence pair | new `_parse_referent_object_clause` rider `_RIDER_PUT_VARIABLE_COUNTERS_RE`, threaded through the existing `_parse_token_then_object_anaphor_clause_pair`; new `count_expression` term for "differently named `<qualifier>` you control" | Emil, Vastlands Roamer ("differently named lands you control") | Body of Research ("cards in your library" - a pre-existing `count_expression` term, proving the new rider generalises to it with no further code) | `test_x_count_fractal_tokens.py` |

## sos T4: Infusion effect shapes, symmetric/edict/halving templates, skip turns

`machines/infusion.py` is new: Infusion itself (CR 207.2c's ability word) needs
no code - `_ABILITY_WORDS` already strips the label - so this module is the
*effect shapes* that follow "if/unless/as long as you gained life this turn",
plus the round's other new templates that share no better home. The boolean
fact is never re-derived: every reader here asks `Game.condition_holds`
(which falls to `machines/conditions/history.py`'s H4 `_life_this_turn`
reader, already generic over "gained"/"lost", a count threshold, and
"this"/"last turn") the identical way `_parse_condition_clause` and
`_parse_condition_instead_clause` (`machines/effects/modal.py`) already do for the
shapes they cover.

CR 705.2, looked up in full: "Some effects that instruct a player to flip a
coin care only about whether the coin comes up heads or tails. No player wins
or loses a coin flip for this kind of effect." - Ral Zarek's "−7" is this
shape, not the win/lose one `Game.flip_coin`'s own docstring frames its
return value around; the boolean is read as heads/tails only, never as a
win.

`machines/turn.py`'s `TurnMachine` gained a fourth thing that breaks plain
round-the-table order (CR 500.7's extra turns and CR 723's player control
were already there): `skipped_turns: dict[str, int]`, a *counter* per CR
614.10a ("that player must skip the next two"), spent one occurrence at a
time by `_consume_skip` inside `begin_next_turn` - for both the ordinary
rotation and a queued extra turn, since CR 614.10 does not carve out an
exception for a turn being an extra one. `Game.skip_next_turns(username,
count)` is the public entry point, mirroring `Game.grant_extra_turn` exactly.
`Game.schema_version` bumped to 88 for the new persisted field (86 at the task, renumbered at the sos integration merge).

**Skip-turns proof gap, documented rather than hidden.** `card_search
o:"skips their next" o:turns` (2026-09-26) found no other Modern/Pioneer/
Standard-legal printing of a true *turn* skip - every other "skips their
next `<X>`" card skips a step or a phase (untap step, combat phase, draw
step), a materially narrower effect this task does not touch. Ral Zarek,
Guest Lecturer is the sole real printing tested against; `test_skip_turns_
coin_flip.py` proves the shared `TurnMachine.skip_next_turns`/`_consume_skip`
mechanism's own corner cases (CR 614.10a's stacking, a skip spent on a
queued extra turn, a departed player's skip dropped) directly against the
engine API instead, since no second card exists to exercise them through.

## sos T5: keyword grants to spells and cards in hand, casualty, a free cast once each turn, target-spell cost reduction, optional-cost copy triggers, can't be copied

`machines/spell_grants.py` reads a permanent's (or an emblem's, CR 114.4) static "`<quality>` spells you cast[ from your hand] have `<keyword>`", "Each `<quality>` spell you cast has `<keyword>`", "The first spell you cast each turn has `<keyword>`" and "Each `<quality>` card in your hand has `<keyword>`" (CR 604.2, CR 611.3a - asked when the keyword's own machine asks) and writes the keyword back out as the line a card prints, handed to the machine that already executes the printed keyword. Only keywords some machine executes are read (storm, cascade, casualty, affinity with a counted "[text]", miracle); convoke, conspire, ripple and the rest keep their earlier verdict. "Spells you cast" excludes a copy (CR 707.10, `CastRecord.is_copy`).

## SOS-T8: library search/look-select, hand discard/draw, graveyard mass returns, owner-may-play exile

Secrets of Strixhaven's own thirteen-card round: a tutor with a two-zone
destination choice, six "look at the top N" shapes (three of them genuinely
new primitives, three reusing `Game.look_at_top_and_split`'s own Waker-of-
Waves family unchanged), two modal hand-discard/draw spells, a two-type
graveyard mass return by count and by exact mana value, and a two-object
owner-scoped exile-and-play grant. Two shared widenings closed most of the
gap on their own: `_parse_card_group_qualifier`'s new "`<A>` and `<B>` cards"
branch (a two-type union, CR 205.2a) plus the matching `split_effect_
clauses` mask (`_CARD_TYPE_PAIR_AND_RE`, built from `Type`'s own values) that
keeps that phrase from being cut by its own internal "and" - and a fix to
`effect_for` itself, `_strip_trailing_standalone_activated_ability`, which
strips a spell's own trailing printed off-zone activated ability
(CR 113.6j/113.6m) before the resolving text is read, the identical
"second paragraph, different ability" correction `_strip_trailing_standalone_
triggered_ability` already made for a graveyard-return trigger.

| Mechanic | Reader | Reported card | Off-pool proof | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "search your library for a `<quality>` card, reveal it, put it into your hand or graveyard, then shuffle" - a mandatory search (CR 701.23a) whose *find* stays optional (CR 701.23b) regardless of wording, landing in a CR 608.2d choice between two zones (`DecisionKind.PUT_INTO_HAND_OR_GRAVEYARD`, the same boolean shape `PUT_ON_TOP_OR_BOTTOM` already is) | `effects._parse_search_hand_or_graveyard_clause` | Dina's Guidance | - (only printing; a full-text Scryfall search this session found no second "hand or graveyard" destination-choice tutor) | `test_library_select_sos.py` |
| "look at the top N cards ... put one into your hand and the rest on the bottom ... in any order. If `<condition>`, instead put M of them into your hand and the rest ... in any order." - read whole (`re.DOTALL`), ahead of the per-clause dispatcher, because the condition's own internal "and" and the alternative's "of them" (the very cards the base sentence looked at) neither the ordinary splitter nor the general CR 614.1a "instead" framework (`_parse_condition_instead_clause`) can carry | `effects._parse_look_top_split_conditional_instead_clause`, `conditions.player._two_card_qualities_in_your_zone` (the new "there is a `<A>` card and a `<B>` card in your `<zone>`" reader) | Flow State | Anticipate, Impulse (the pre-existing base shape, `_merge_look_top_split_hand_graveyard_clauses`, unchanged) | `test_library_select_sos.py` |

Return each artifact and creature card with mana value X from your graveyard to the battlefield." - CR 107.3f's additional-cost X (the pre-existing "pay X life" machinery, proved by Toxic Deluge/Vicious Rivalry) feeding a two-type mass return filtered by an *exact* mana value, X=0 included (CR 119.4b) | `effects._parse_x_life_return_types_mv_x_clause` | Fix What's Broken | Brilliant Restoration (the widened `_parse_card_group_qualifier` on the "all ... to the battlefield" family) | `test_graveyard_mass_returns.py` |

For each of those cards, its owner may play it until the end of their next turn." - two objects exiled in one instruction, each granted a `PlayPermission` scoped to its own **owner** (CR 108.3), not the caster - the one shape the pool's other "exile ..., you may play it" printings never need, since every one of them grants to the caster who did the exiling | `effects._parse_exile_target_and_top_owner_may_play_clause` (`Game.grant_play_permission`'s `expires_end_of_next_turn`, keyed off `PlayPermission.player`) | Suspend Aggression | - (only printing of an owner-scoped, two-object exile-and-play grant) | `test_owner_exile_play.py` |
| "Choose target `<X>`. Its owner may put it on (the) top of their library. If they do, `<source>` deals N damage to them. If they didn't put the card on (the) top of their library, they put it on the bottom." - CR 608.2d's "may X. If they do, Y. If they didn't, Z." over the target's **owner** (CR 108.3: the owner, not the caster, makes the may choice and takes the damage). Both "on top of" (current oracle) and "on the top of" (pre-release) read; a token still counts as "did" (CR 111.7); an illegal target on resolution does nothing (CR 608.2b). No lose/gain/draw consequence or bottom-first variant is read: no legal printing carries one | `effects._parse_choose_target_owner_may_top_else_bottom_clause` (`_CHOOSE_TARGET_OWNER_MAY_TOP_ELSE_BOTTOM_RE`) | Clash of Elements | - (no other Modern/Pioneer/Standard printing carries the shape; Scryfall oracle bulk checked 2026-10-04) | `test_edicts_and_library_placement.py` |

### regaudit-decayed: Decayed (CR 702.147a)

Decayed was previously parsed (Scryfall keyword vocabulary, `KEYWORD_ABILITY_NAMES`)
but executed nowhere - `test_the_pool_wide_ignored_keyword_report_matches_the_expected_gap_list`
listed it against Rot-Curse Rakshasa. Built as two abilities, per the rule's
own text: the static "This creature can't block" is
`machines/combat.py::block_refusal`'s own `has_keyword(blocker, Keyword.
DECAYED, game)` check (`Keyword.DECAYED` new member), so a printed keyword,
a CR 122.1b keyword counter, or a grant all refuse the block the same way -
`machines/keyword_counters.py::KEYWORD_COUNTER_KEYWORDS` now lists decayed,
since layers.py's own generic per-`Keyword`-member counter-to-line grant now
has a reading vocabulary for it. The triggered "sacrifice it at end of
combat" is `machines/keywords.py::_decayed_ability` (`_TRIGGER_EXPANSIONS`),
whose effect text is read by a new `_parse_delayed_single_clause` branch in
`machines/effects/` (self-referential "it" off the ATTACKS event's own
subject) as a CR 603.7 delayed trigger reusing the same `sacrificed_by_its_
controller` effect The Ring's third ability already uses. Jadar, Ghoulcaller
of Nephalia's own "create a 2/2 black Zombie creature token with decayed"
needed `_TOKEN_KEYWORDS` widened in `machines/effects/_common.py` (its "if you
control no creatures with decayed" condition was already read generally by
`conditions/board.py::quality`'s "with `<keyword>`" suffix - `KEYWORD_
ABILITY_NAMES` already had decayed). `tests/scenarios/test_decayed.py`.

## 271-tmt T1: the Mutagen predefined token, LKI token riders, token-count

## ETBs, artifact-token activation cost reduction

CR 111.10v's Mutagen token ("a colorless Mutagen artifact token with '{1},
{T}, Sacrifice this token: Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature. Activate
only as a sorcery.'") was added to `models/token.PREDEFINED`, the same data
row every other CR 111.10 entry already is. Every "create a Mutagen token"
shape the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles set prints turned out to already be
generic once that one row existed - no new parser needed for a plain ETB
(Crustacean Commando, Slithering Cryptid), a self-named ETB (Michelangelo,
Weirdness to 11; Ray Fillet, Man Ray), the self-or-another-subtype-enters
condition (Genghis Frog, off `_self_or_other_enters_match` from an earlier
wave), a leaves-the-battlefield trigger (Zoo Escapees), an `{X}` spell's own
ETB count (Mutagen Man, Living Ooze, off the existing CR 107.3m `_etb_x_
effect_text` substitution), or a spell rider after a destroy/counter (Mutant
Chain Reaction's "Destroy up to one target ... Create a Mutagen token.",
Ooze Spill's "Counter target spell. Create a Mutagen token.") - each of
these is just two independent clauses `_parse_mixed_clauses` already reads
apart. `tests/scenarios/test_mutagen_tokens.py`.

What genuinely needed new code:

- **The counter-qualified leaves-the-battlefield condition** - "a creature
  you control **with a +1/+1 counter on it** leaves the battlefield" (The
  Ooze). `machines/triggers/`'s `_leaves_battlefield_counter_qualifier_
  holds` mirrors the entering side's own `_ENTERS_WITH_COUNTER_RE`, reading
  `last_known_counters` (CR 603.10a's look-back, CR 704.8) since the object
  has already left by the time the condition is checked.
- **The event-subject counter multiplier** - "create a Mutagen token for
  each +1/+1 counter on it", where "it" is the *departed* creature the
  condition named, not the ability's own source the way Hangarback Walker's
  identical-looking "for each +1/+1 counter on this creature" already reads
  (`machines/effects._COUNTER_ON_IT_RE`/`_for_each_multiplier`). New:
  `machines/token_riders.event_subject_counter_multiplier`, reading
  `AbilityOnStack.event.subject_id` rather than the ability's `source_id`,
  wired into `machines/effects._parse_token_clause`'s own "for each" branch
  as a fallback when `count_expression` (a board-wide count) does not match.
- **The "if its mana value was N or less" destroy rider**, generalised past
  Tainted Treats' own "create a Food token" consequence: `machines/token_
  riders.parse_destroy_if_mv_then_consequence_clause_pair` reads the
  destroyed object's mana value into a local variable before `Game.destroy`
  runs (CR 400.7/603.10a's look-back needs no persistent LKI field when the
  whole read-then-act happens inside one Python call), and supports a token-
  creation consequence or a life-gain one - proven on Extinguish the Light
  (real, in-format, off the deck pool: "Destroy target creature or
  planeswalker. If its mana value was 3 or less, you gain 3 life.").
- **The owner's choice of top or bottom, plus a token** - Return to the
  Sewers' "Target creature's owner puts it on their choice of the top or
  bottom of their library." was *already* read by `machines/effects.
  _owner_puts_it_into_library_effect` (CR 110.2's owner, not the caster);
  only the trailing "You create a Mutagen token." sentence needed Mutagen to
  exist, and it is an ordinary second clause once it did.
- **Search, else create a token** - "You may search your library for a
  `<quality>` card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle. If you
  don't put a card into your hand this way, create a `<token>`." (Courier of
  Comestibles). New: `machines/token_riders.parse_search_or_else_create_
  token_clause`, read as one whole-text instruction (CR 118.12's "this way"
  anaphora points back across the period, which the ordinary per-clause
  splitter cannot rejoin) ahead of `_parse_mixed_clauses`'s own splitting.
- **"nontoken" in a count expression** - `machines/effects._COUNT_YOU_
  CONTROL_RE` read a leading "tapped"/"untapped" status word but not
  "nontoken" (CR 111.1); Sally Pride, Lioness Leader's own "the number of
  nontoken creatures you control" and, off the reported card and off the
  deck pool, Lena, Selfless Champion's "for each nontoken creature you
  control" (the same regex reached through `_TOKEN_FOR_EACH_TAIL_RE`'s tail
  instead of "where X is the number of") both needed it.
- **"Activated abilities of `<group>` you control cost `{N}` less to
  activate."** (CR 601.2f via CR 602.2b) - Mutagen Man, Living Ooze's own
  "artifact tokens" static was `static_unaudited`: nothing read the shape at
  all. `machines/cost.activated_ability_group_discount_effect` is the pure
  text parse (mirroring `cost_modifier_effect`'s own split from `Game.
  static_cost_modifiers_for`), and `Game._activated_ability_group_discount`
  is the board-wide aggregation, wired into `Game.activation_cost` right
  after every other reduction. The group phrase is read generically off its
  own words (`Game._permanent_matches_group_quality`: CR 205.4a supertypes,
  CR 205.2a card types, CR 205.3 subtypes via `canonical_subtype`, and a
  trailing "token(s)" word read separately since CR 111.1's token is none of
  those three) - proven on the Mutagen token's own `{1}` ability (reduced to
  `{0}`), on a Food and a Clue token (a different predefined token than
  Mutagen Man's own), on a non-token artifact staying undiscounted (Sewer-
  veillance Cam), and off the reported card entirely on Forensic Gadgeteer (a
  real, in-format printing, not in the deck pool)'s own "artifacts" group
  plus its "This effect can't reduce the mana in that cost to less than one
  mana" floor, which Mutagen Man's own printing does not carry and which is
  clamped against the cost being reduced rather than folded into the flat
  amount.

`tests/scenarios/test_token_riders_lki.py`,
`tests/scenarios/test_artifact_token_ability_cost_reduction.py`,
`tests/scenarios/test_token_count_etbs_tmt.py`.

`conditions/cast_record.py::_keyword_cost_paid`'s own pattern gained two additive widenings shared by every rider above that reads a keyword-cost condition: an optional trailing `this turn` (checked against `CardState.turn_entered`, since a sneak permanent always enters the same turn it is cast) and `this <type>'s` alongside the existing bare pronouns, for "this creature's sneak cost was paid"/"this spell's sneak cost was paid" - both purely additive (every clause the narrower pattern already matched still does), and the second one is what let Rix Maadi Reveler's own pre-existing spectacle-paid rider stop reading `notice` as a side effect, not a targeted fix.

## 271-tmt T3: counter payoffs - dealt-damage counters, counters-on-self X, reflexive remove-a-counter, crewed-this-turn targeting, pay-life-for-counters

Five Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles counter-payoff templates, all built into
the new `machines/counter_payoffs.py` (registered additively into
`machines/counter_effects.parse_resolution_text`'s own `_WHOLE_TEXT_READERS`
tuple, so nothing in `machines/effects/` had to change): a self-referential
"is dealt damage, put that many counters" trigger, a combined "put a
counter, then `<X-consuming clause>`, where X is the number of counters on
self" resolution generalised over an arbitrary tail clause rather than fixed
to "draw X and lose X life", a genuine CR 603.12 reflexive "remove a counter
from self" cost (as opposed to `counter_effects._remove_a_counter_if_you_do`'s
existing same-instruction "remove a counter from a chosen other permanent"
cost), a new `machines/targeting.TargetRequirement.must_have_crewed_source_
this_turn` restriction reading `Game.turn_history`'s own "crewed" entries,
and an optional pay-life-equal-to-a-characteristic cost whose "that many" is
the amount actually paid rather than `machines/effects.that_many`'s own
triggering-event anaphora.

`models/game.Game.create_reflexive_trigger` gained one additive, optional
`event` parameter (default `None`, every existing caller unchanged): a
reflexive triggered ability's own `DelayedTrigger.event` is never populated
(CR 603.12 - nothing left to watch for), so `_that_player_of`/`TargetingProfile.
for_event_player`'s "that player controls" binding, which reads `AbilityOnStack.
event.player`, would otherwise come back unbound for a reflexive consequence
that names a specific player at all (Leatherhead's own "destroy target
artifact or enchantment **that player** controls"). No schema bump: `event`
was already a field on `AbilityOnStack`, just never populated this way before.

| Mechanic | CR | Reader | Reported card | Off-pool proof | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Whenever `<this>` is dealt damage, put that many `<kind>` counters on it." - the trigger condition itself already generic (Hexhaven Invigorator's own passive "is dealt damage" already read); the self-reference is read off `AbilityOnStack.source`, never `GameEvent.subject_id` (CR 120.1's *dealer*, not the recipient of a passive event) | 120.3e, 607.1 | `counter_payoffs._put_that_many_counters_on_it` | Venus, Torn Between Worlds | Hungering Hydra (non-legendary, prints "it" directly with no pronoun to normalise) | `test_dealt_damage_counters.py` |
| "At the beginning of combat on your turn, put a `<kind>` counter on `<this>`. Then `<clause>`, where X is the number of counters on `<this>`." - X is the *total* across every counter kind (CR 122.1's open set), counted after this same instruction's own put (CR 608.2c); `<clause>` is read generally via `machines/modes.substitute_x` plus the ordinary whole-clause resolver, not fixed to "draw X cards and lose X life" | 122.1, 608.2c | `counter_payoffs._put_counter_then_x_clause_where_x_is_counters_on_self` | Savanti Romero, Time's Exile | Spider-Man Noir (different trigger - "attacks alone" - different `<clause>` - "surveil X" - and the bare pronoun "it" rather than a name-normalised self-reference; no legal second printing shares Savanti Romero's own exact "draw X and lose X life" clause - see MEMORY.md) | `test_counter_count_draw.py` |
| "Whenever `<this>` deals combat damage to a player, you may remove a counter from `<self-reference>`. When you do, `<consequence>`." - CR 603.12's reflexive triggered ability, its own new stack object (CR 405.6a); `Game.create_reflexive_trigger`'s new `event=` parameter carries the creating ability's own event forward so a consequence naming "that player" binds to the right one | 603.12, 118.12, 405.6a | `counter_payoffs._remove_a_counter_from_it_when_you_do` | Leatherhead, Swamp Stalker | Slumbering Walker (different trigger - "beginning of your end step" - a consequence with no "that player" restraint at all, and the ordinary self-reference "this creature") | `test_reflexive_remove_counter.py` |
| "Whenever this Vehicle attacks, put a `<kind>` counter on target creature that crewed it this turn. Then if that creature is `<a/an> <quality>`, double the number of `<kind>` counters on it." - a new targeting restriction over this turn's own crew history, plus CR 701.10e's doubling gated on a subtype check | 702.122b, 701.10e | `targeting.TargetRequirement.must_have_crewed_source_this_turn` (extraction/rejection), `counter_payoffs._crewed_this_turn_target_then_maybe_double` (doubling) | Turtle Van | Getaway Car (the targeting restriction alone, on a different Vehicle with a "return to hand" consequence and an "up to one" optional count) | `test_crewed_this_turn.py` |
| "Whenever another creature you control enters, you may pay life equal to its power. If you do, put that many `<kind>` counters on it." - the "that many" is the life actually paid (computed and paid by this resolution), not `machines/effects.that_many`'s own triggering-event anaphora | 118.12, 119.4, 107.1a | `counter_payoffs._may_pay_life_equal_to_its_power_then_counters` | Madame Null, Power Broker | - (no second Modern/Pioneer/Standard-legal printing combines "pay life equal to a characteristic" with "put that many counters" - exhaustive `card_search` in the session that wrote this wave; see the dated MEMORY.md line) | `test_pay_life_for_counters.py` |
| "Whenever a creature you control with a counter on it deals combat damage to a player, `<consequence>`." - Venus's own *second* ability, not her dealt-damage one above: `machines/triggers.condition_matches`'s `DEALS_DAMAGE` branch read the "a creature you control" subject clause but had no reader at all for a trailing "with a[n] `<kind>` counter on it" qualifier (CR 122.1's counter-presence question) on that subject, so the ability fired for *any* attacker regardless of whether it actually carried a counter - a genuine engine defect the T3 wave that first landed this card documented rather than fixed (see the dated MEMORY.md line this row supersedes). `triggers._SUBJECT_HAS_COUNTER_RE`/`_subject_has_required_counter` read it, generally: a bare "a counter" (no kind word, what both cards below print) asks the presence question only, a named kind ("a +1/+1 counter on it") would narrow to that one kind, though nothing in the pool proves the named-kind half yet. | 122.1 | `triggers._subject_has_required_counter`, called from `condition_matches`'s `DEALS_DAMAGE` branch | Venus, Torn Between Worlds | Yathan Tombguard (a different, unconditional "draw a card and lose 1 life" consequence, and a board where the creature carrying the ability is never the one dealing the damage - proving this reads a general subject clause, not a self-reference on the event's source) | `test_dealt_damage_counters.py` |

### tmt-t5: combat restrictions and requirements (CR 508.1c, 509.1a, 509.1b, 509.1c, 118.12a)

Round 271-tmt (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles), Task 5. New module `machines/
combat_statics.py` holds the genuinely new combat-declaration static-restriction
families (power threshold, "must be blocked", group blocked-by-at-most-one);
every other clause here widens an existing reader in `machines/combat.py`,
`machines/layers/`, `machines/targeting.py`, `machines/triggers/`, or adds
a new whole-text parser in `machines/effects/`. CR numbers verified this
session with `mise run rules:find <n>`: 508.1c, 509.1a, 509.1b, 509.1c, 106.4,
500.5/500.5b, 118.12/118.12a, 601.2c, 608.2b, 207.2c.

## 271-tmt T6: cast/play permissions from the graveyard, the library top and linked exile; granted sneak; next-spell affinity; card types among spells cast

Standing permissions (CR 601.3, CR 611.3d) are read off the caster's permanents by `casting.granted_cast_options` and claimed at announcement as the `"Cast permission"` keyword option; a permission that only opens a zone keeps the spell's own timing (`CastTiming.OWN`, CR 117.1a). A permission's rider "If you cast a spell this way, that `<noun>` enters with a[n additional] `<kind>` counter on it" is copied onto `CastRecord.enters_with_counters` (schema 90) and applied as the permanent enters (CR 614.1c, `replacement._cast_permission_rider_modifiers`). A cast from the library that is rewound goes back to the position it left (CR 733.1, CR 401.2).

## 271-tmt T7: end-step/attack flicker of new objects, an optional-payment

## delayed return, exile-until-an-Aura-leaves, a linked-exile land, a

## reflexive dies-exile, a next-upkeep delayed random discard, an

## entered-this-turn mass bounce, and same-name mass reanimation

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles' own T7 round: nine cards, none of them reusing
a card-specific hardcode. `machines/linked_exile.py` is new - CR 607.2a's
return half, generic over which permanent type names itself and whether "a"
or "each" linked card of the given description comes back. Two `DelayedEffectSpec`
kinds are new (`PayOrElseReturnExiledCard`, `DiscardCardsAtRandomForController`),
both thin wrappers around already-proven primitives (`may_pay_mana_cost`,
`_discard_at_random`) - see `MEMORY.md` for why neither needed a
`Game.schema_version` bump. `models/token._put_onto_the_battlefield_
attacking`'s parameter widened from `TokenState` to `CardState`: CR 508.4's
own "put onto the battlefield attacking" is not token-specific, and a real
card returning already attacking (The Neutrinos) is the identical event a
token created attacking already was.

sentence`) that several unrelated future cards can now also read.
